title_zh: “值得吗？”
abstract_zh: 柯达公司于1880年在纽约罗彻斯特成立，后来成为美国第二大化学公司，据说生产了世界上80%的电影胶片。一个多世纪以来，柯达渗透到美国视觉文化的方方面面——从家庭相册到广告、好莱坞电影以及战争和国家监控技术。用柯达胶片拍摄的大众传播图像，以其原型主题和风景，赋予了国家幻想以视觉形式，而消费品则邀请普通人在这些集体幻想中为自己成像。柯达胶片被视为一种化学过程、企业基础设施和想象媒介，它强化了一种特定的美国“美好生活”愿景，在20世纪实现了全球垄断，并在幻想、图像和分子层面上重塑了世界。柯达在当地作为一个“总体机构”运作，是福利国家的前身和代理。它通过工人家庭分配福利和资源，在此过程中使核心家庭在罗彻斯特成为社会学现实。工人被承诺30年的工资和之后的养老金，他们的孩子也假定能在“柯达”找到工作。柯达曾在罗彻斯特雇佣超过62,000名工人，全球另有60,000人。但在1983年，它开始了一系列裁员，最终导致2012年破产。一年后，它作为Kodak Alaris重新出现。新柯达只雇佣约一千名工人，人数还在不断减少。新柯达仍占据柯达公园的一角，这是公司最古老和最大的化工厂，他们仍生产胶片，但数量很少，面向小众电影市场。许多前柯达员工在公司重组计划中失去了福利和养老金，他们将公司的衰退描述为对其关爱工人及家庭承诺的背叛。许多员工承认柯达不可逆转地污染了环境，使工人和工厂邻居暴露于有毒物质中。在玩笑和窃窃私语中，他们将癌症和流产归咎于工业污染。柯达是美国二恶英的最大排放源，二恶英是“人类已知最危险的物质”，多年来，其工厂旁的河流是纽约州污染最严重的。城市居民知道这一点。他们能在空气中闻到：一股燃烧塑料的气味，在夜晚和周末最为严重。然而，许多前员工继续庆祝公司支持了他们的家庭，并制造了构成美国帝国的材料。他们知道柯达的美国梦愿景是有毒的，但他们仍然依恋于大规模工业生产能带来大规模繁荣的愿望。这是一个最普通的矛盾，通常就是爱的方式。2015年8月，我和Ted在South Wedge的一家酒吧里。一位同事介绍我们认识。他也是处女座，有西北大学的博士学位。他的妻子是历史学家，儿子甚至是诗人。我喜欢他，而且，我猜，他知道我在罗彻斯特做什么。“今天又有人问我是否值得，”我告诉他。“那人说，‘考虑到家庭遭受了多少痛苦’——他指的是裁员——‘我和我的朋友互相问，这值得吗？’然后他问我，我认为柯达值得吗？这到底是什么意思，‘值得’？我带着引号说。‘我不知道该怎么回答！这根本不是我的问题！我问的是柯达如何改变了世界，而不是它是否“值得”。’”“嗯，”Ted问，“那值得吗？”“什么值得？”我问。“值得吗？你怎么回答他的？”“哦！嗯，好吧，你的意思是如果把裁员和污染算进去？”从银矿提取银的成本，从煤矿提取煤的成本，用于制造胶片，癌症的成本，修复的成本，不修复的成本，所有流入杰纳西河的废水的成本（杰纳西在塞内卡语中是“美丽山谷”的意思；这是豪德诺索尼人的土地），以及河岸中残留的废物。一位科学家告诉我，那里的银比世界上任何地方都多。“那些东西是附带损失，”我告诉Ted。“它们没有被计入资本主义的成本。也许柯达既值得又不值得。”我举起手掌模仿正义的天平，但如何将永远的河流与家庭照片相权衡呢？“也许两者都是。也许两者可以同时为真。”离别人的良心这么近感觉不礼貌。我合上面前的笔记本，盖上笔帽。“我想那不是我在这里试图做的重点。我更感兴——”“嗯，也许这不是重点，但你认为呢？”Ted追问。“你知道吗，我不知道。我不知道这样的计算是否可能——判断柯达在世界上做的善事是否多于恶事或相反。老实说，当人们问时，我想我说这个问题无法回答。因为柯达塑造了世界。它重塑了我们的眼睛和我们看世界的方式。我们不知道没有柯达的世界。”我垂下目光，看着面前的啤酒，在八月的潮湿中，把酒标完整地撕下来。但Ted保持沉默，所以我继续说。“有一个我喜欢的法国哲学家，菲利克斯·加塔利？他有一本很酷的书叫《三种生态》，在书中，他谈到他在法国电视上看到的一位科学家。这位科学家面前有两箱水。一箱是来自马赛港的脏水、污染水，另一箱是‘纯净、未污染’的‘正常’水，加塔利说。在脏水中，有一只刚出海的章鱼。它‘健康，茁壮，几乎在跳舞’，加塔利说，但当科学家把章鱼从脏海水中取出，倒入干净水中时，几乎立即，章鱼‘蜷缩起来，沉到底部，死了’[加塔利1989, 43]。它如此习惯于生活在有毒的世界中，以至于没有毒它就活不下去。它无法回头。那就是我们。我们是那只章鱼。没有回头路。我们生活在这个世界，”我说。这就是作为图片的世界，柯达描绘的世界。“我们只能通过，嗯，柯达彩色棱镜来评判它，你知道吗？”“实际上，Ted，我有时候会这么说。我引用卢梭的一些话，关于文明是一切的堕落，没有回头路，同时，我们身处的混乱中也有好的东西。只有在这里，在这些限制中，我们才知道生活中甜蜜的部分：家庭、爱。这种堕落给了我们爱的能力，‘人类已知的最甜蜜的感觉’。这部分是引用的，”我对Ted说。“友谊、家庭和浪漫的爱，这些我想以某种形式保留的东西。”它们可能加起来不是“美好生活”，但甜蜜的部分仍然存在。“而且无论如何，没有回头路，”我说。“我们是摄影的存在。我们无法取消世界的双重性，也无法撤销摄影改变世界的方式。”“确实如此，”Ted说。谢天谢地，我想。“家庭，”Ted说。“我们做了有意义的事情。我们给了人们记住他们生活的东西和材料。当房子着火时，你拿什么？你拿照片。”他翻动着一个想象中的鞋盒。“那是关于帮助人们。我们通过照片了解自己。生日、假期——我只想到我们给孩子们拍的照片，看着他们长大。我记得，有一次在我姐姐家，她有一个整个碗——一个真正的鱼缸放在厨房柜台上，里面装满了她还没冲洗的胶卷。如果你记得，冲洗胶卷并不便宜。我说，‘噗，给我吧。我拿到研究实验室给我的朋友。’他们不应该这样做，但他们愿意。为了奥运会，我们会有员工加班双班制作胶卷。”柯达胶卷被用于每一个宣传图片，每场比赛的照片终点。“那是一种服务，”Ted说。他们会举行仪式。男人们带着妻子，经理给每个加班的人发别针。”2“我知道听起来很俗气，但我们认为我们是在为美国做这些。现在呢？”他通过圈起的嘴唇大声呼气。“我不太确定。还有人想要这个吗？我们还知道人们想要什么吗？我们以为是图像质量，但我们错了。”曾几何时，柯达决定了欲望；现在他们甚至找不到它。“人们对多年来低分辨率的数字图像很满意。数字是不同的！它是关于分享图像、移动图像。现在，就像是，想出一个可能让我们维持生计的应用。他们还在想办法让柯达数字化。”柯达保障了一个幻想近一个世纪。现在什么幻想能保障我们呢？Ted，他在几乎30年的裁员中幸存下来，在我俩在啤酒花园的那个夜晚几个月后被解雇了。获得如此之多却失去一切，值得吗？这是一个在事情结束时提出的问题，一个心碎时提出的问题，无法回答。提问的“我”不是坠入爱河的“我”。“值得吗”让我想要把世界维系在一起，即使这个世界已经破碎。我没有回答，而是试图探讨并解释为什么它无法维系。按照它的条件回答就是允许经济理性决定伦理。生命的劳动价值如何与流产和癌症集群的遗产相权衡？养老金值得健康风险、对他人的风险吗？永远的河流是几代廉价富足的合理代价吗？值得吗？与其说“是”或“否”，这个问题要求考虑情感和依恋模式，它们在现在与过去之间调解。这个问题希望从这种紧张中解脱，从询问者正在经历的焦虑矛盾中解脱：在世界尽头的生命尽头，是否有可能自豪地回顾？有没有办法转移这个问题，承认这些类别无法通约？如果我们能够容忍矛盾，同时持有两者——“巨大的经济利润和巨大的文化与个人损失”（Jain, 2013, 223）；甜蜜的部分和“美好生活”需要毒害世界的事实——那么这些“矛盾”，S. Lochlann Jain写道，可以变得“不仅可读，而且可活和可死”（223）。矛盾为Jain所称的哀悼政治开辟了可能性：“一个空间，其中痛苦和死亡的物质人性为沟通和集体行动提供信息”（24）。然而，正如所表达的，这个问题似乎要求确定性，并悬置在遗憾的情绪中。像怀旧一样，这种遗憾模式是“与自己幻想的浪漫”（Boym, 2007, 7）。它的向后凝视分散了主体对依恋复杂性和当下生活条件的认识。但是，怀旧可能寻求回到过去以便重新来过，而遗憾则是反思以便做得不同。但如果遗憾能回去，它能做出不同的选择吗？“值得吗”希望答案是“是”。它将个体从历史中分离出来，要求主体承担结构的分量，而不是承认能动性可能在结构中不均匀分布。这个问题希望意志能拯救我们，我们是主权、自我创造的主体，不渗透且自足。它假设有可能以其他方式渴望，从时刻和环境中抽身并做出其他选择。在这个命题下，“值得吗”低估了我们的欲望在多大程度上被招募和征召我们的感觉结构所塑造。如果我们不能以不同的方式做，至少不彻底放弃这个世界，那会怎样？如果我们把柯达的故事解读为不是英雄意志的故事，而是意志与必要性纠结成无法解开的结的悲剧，那会怎样？毕竟，我们是章鱼，我们的感官由环境塑造。“值得吗”请求允许仍然依恋于幻想：主权主体的幻想，关心公司的幻想，以及将分子操纵成物质丰裕、无尽且无害的幻想。柯达本应是更道德的选择。他们制造照片。那不像在洛克希德·马丁、波音或埃克森工作，这些都是柯达化学家的选择。他们制造照片。3同时——尤其是Ted问的方式：急促、低语、急切——“值得吗”暗示了幻想中的一道裂缝，一丝怀疑。这使得问题变得脆弱。询问者知道代价。如果答案是“不”，他们似乎认为，他们要部分为维持机器运转负责，或者他们被欺骗了。如果是后者，那意味着这根本不是爱。那是烟雾和镜子。工人只是工人，不是亲属。如果是后者，那意味着曾经串联起生活并提供道德框架的幻想终结了（Gornick, 2020 xv）。化学制造危害的正当性也会蒸发，就像胶片基在巨大的钢铸轮上干燥时飘出的溶剂（主要是二氯甲烷）。不清楚每个询问者是否能承受“不”。衡量柯达是否值得是假设损失可以计算，并且戏剧本身已经结束。这个问题希望相信，我们将达到一个时刻，可以结清账单，答案可知。柯达创造的世界可能已经结束，但我们还没有到达它的审判日。化学时间在继续。正如照片随时间变化——分子对环境的反应改变图像的外观；染料褪色，纸张变黄，边缘失去清晰度——工业碎片将塑造几代人的生活条件。溶剂、氰化物、镉、钡、多氯联苯、呋喃、照相染料、二恶英、汞、镍、无名的物质、柯达之外从未有人见过的物质、与其他物质结合成为全新事物的物质，以及如此多的银。柯达倒入河流、空气和土壤的化学物质仍然存在，存在于景观和工人、工厂邻居及其子女的身体中。因果关系几乎不可分解，并且仍在继续。如果戏剧仍在展开，结局不整洁，如果永远无法到达终点，成本与收益无法最终确定地计算，我们如何应对“值得吗”这个问题——更不用说责任问题了？我们如何从悲剧内部行动？悲剧认识到我们受制于力量——命运、结构、我们未发起的欲望——在我们进入舞台之前启动，而我们自己是其结果。但推动悲剧走向命运结局的是，角色们“继续做那些最初产生这些后果的事情”，斯坦利·卡维尔（1976）写道。悲剧之所以是悲剧，他认为，不是因为结果不可避免，而是因为角色假设命运的必然性。他们拒绝承认自己行动的重要性以及自己和他人痛苦的深度（318）。悲剧的补救措施不是遗憾的后顾，“不是重生或救赎，而是勇气，或简单的谨慎，去看并停止”（309）。它需要将目光转向当下，打断我们用银锭衡量河流价值的伦理结构。但这里有风险。提出一种替代的价值衡量标准将意味着放弃资本主义积累固有的核算模式。放弃其逻辑将意味着第二次结束世界。如果从过去及其“值得吗”中，可以成为处理和克服这些问题的切入点。来自的问题认为世界已经结束，没有它，它认识到工业“美好生活”对几代人的和规模，并可能从作为的转向。它要求一种几乎是当下如何与过去相关的方式，因为它涉及因果关系以及一个人在失去和剩余甜蜜中的位置，是移动的一种方式，使在遗憾中纠缠时，可以成为的邀请，并在曾经串联生活和的意义上进行。它打开询问者对情感的开放性，并使他人能够在一个与资本主义不同、并指向这个世界终结的伦理中参与。值得吗？也许答案不是“是”或“否”，而是对的重量的承认。柯达是工业秩序的一部分，它塑造了我们的世界和我们的身体和，同时它使这个世界更加值得。如果它不是这样，而希望这个世界是。那意味着。而且其中有很多我想抓住的东西。

title: A fablab at the periphery: Decentering innovation from São Paulo
abstract: Abstract In recent decades, many tech spaces have emerged worldwide to promote innovation. Based on ethnographic research, this article examines one of such initiatives in Brazil—a public laboratory of digital fabrication located in a low‐income neighborhood in the periphery of São Paulo. While scholars have exposed the neoliberal aspects of fablabs, this article aims to de‐center hegemonic understandings of innovation by attending to its situated practices. Analyzing the techno‐optimist aspirations and institutional legacies behind this laboratory, I explain how the US‐based fablab model was reconfigured in light of community concerns and previous Latin American experiments of digital inclusion. Against a monolithic image of tech collectives, I show how lab workers cultivated a diverse range of audiences and creative practices, specifically those of working‐class women. The article concludes with a call for more anthropological attention to overlooked tech practices as a means to imagine fairer and more solidary forms of innovation.
title_zh: 边缘的法布拉实验室：从圣保罗去中心化创新
abstract_zh: 近年来，世界范围内涌现出许多旨在促进创新的科技空间。基于民族志研究，本文考察了巴西的这样一项举措——一个位于圣保罗周边低收入社区的数字制造公共实验室。虽然学者们已经揭示了法布拉实验室的新自由主义方面，但本文旨在通过关注其实践情境，去中心化对创新的霸权理解。通过分析该实验室背后的技术乐观主义抱负和制度遗产，我解释了源自美国的法布拉实验室模式如何根据社区关切和先前拉丁美洲的数字包容实验进行重新配置。针对科技集体的单一形象，我展示了实验室工作人员如何培养多样化的受众和创造性实践，尤其是工人阶级女性的实践。文章最后呼吁人类学更多关注被忽视的科技实践，以此作为想象更公平、更团结的创新形式的一种手段。

title: Lithium’s buzz: extractivism between booms in Bolivia, Argentina, and Chile
abstract: Plans for decarbonizing energy transitions – attempts to mitigate the climate crisis through electrifying the global economy – will require minerals like lithium for the electric vehicles and batteries of the near future. As a result, a ‘buzz’ of economic speculation, governmental policy making, and grassroots opposition is intensifying in the so-called ‘lithium triangle’ in Southern Bolivia, north western Argentina, and Northern Chile. Using archival investigation and stakeholder interviews this article examines the temporal and spatial effects of the extractivist buzz as it operates through complex ecological and social dynamics complicated further still by energy transitions. As decarbonization and the climate crisis inform and inflect extractivism, they also offer new vantages from which to understand established global, regional, and local power relations. Extractivism produces and shapes landscapes and timescapes through anticipation, frontiers, and sacrifice: buzz, boom, and bust cycles that have shaped livelihoods and landscapes in these three countries since colonization.
title_zh: 锂的嗡嗡声：玻利维亚、阿根廷和智利之间繁荣浪潮中的采掘主义
abstract_zh: 脱碳能源转型的计划——通过电气化全球经济来缓解气候危机的尝试——将需要锂等矿物用于不久的将来的电动汽车和电池。因此，在所谓的“锂三角”地区（玻利维亚南部、阿根廷西北部和智利北部），经济投机、政府政策制定和草根反对的“嗡嗡声”正在加剧。通过档案调查和利益相关者访谈，本文考察了采掘主义嗡嗡声的时间和空间效应，它通过复杂的生态和社会动态运作，而能源转型又使这些动态进一步复杂化。随着脱碳和气候危机影响并改变采掘主义，它们也提供了新的视角来理解既有的全球、地区和地方权力关系。采掘主义通过预期、前沿和牺牲产生并塑造了景观和时间景观：自殖民化以来，在三个国家中，嗡嗡声、繁荣和萧条的周期塑造了生计和景观。

title: Modelling emotion, perfecting heart: disassembling technologies of affect with an android bodhisattva in Japan
journal_name: JOURNAL OF THE ROYAL ANTHROPOLOGICAL INSTITUTE
abstract: Abstract As part of a surge in technologies with so‐called ‘artificial emotional intelligence’, robotics engineers and Buddhist monks in Japan have developed an android bodhisattva to deliver teachings at a popular Zen temple. Like many recent robots in Japan, the android is designed to impact visitors’ feelings. For this reason, it can be called a ‘technology of affect’. In order to communicate how new affective technologies are facilitating intimacy in human‐machine relations in Japan, we employ the concept of ‘disassembling’. By conceptually disassembling technologies of affect and placing them in performative contexts, we show how technologies of affect also disassemble established associations between artificial agents and the feelings they evoke in popular imaginaries. We argue that identifying these disassembling processes helps demonstrate how emerging AI technologies can engender social change at the level of affect through evocative depictions of machine emotion.
title_zh: 情感建模，完美之心：拆解日本一个安卓菩萨的情感技术
abstract_zh: 作为所谓的“人工情感智能”技术激增的一部分，日本的机器人工程师和佛教僧侣开发了一个安卓菩萨，在一个受欢迎的禅宗寺庙中传授教义。像日本最近的许多机器人一样，这个安卓机器人旨在影响访客的感受。因此，它可以被称为“情感技术”。为了传达新的情感技术如何促进日本人机关系中的亲密感，我们采用了“拆解”的概念。通过概念性地拆解情感技术并将其置于述行语境中，我们展示了情感技术如何也拆解了流行想象中人工智能体与它们所唤起的情感之间的既定关联。我们认为，识别这些拆解过程有助于说明新兴AI技术如何通过机器情感的唤起性描绘在情感层面引发社会变革。

title: Rubbers Benjamin (ed.). — Inside Mining Capitalism. The Micropolitics of Work on the Congolese and Zambian Copperbelts

authors.name: Hélène Blaszkiewicz
institutions: Ministère de l’Environnement et du Développement Durable

abstract: Depuis le milieu des années 2010, la popularité des véhicules électriques et autres appareils électroniques fonctionnant sur batterie a entraîné une importante spéculation sur les métaux stratégiques. Cuivre et cobalt, dont les plus importants gisements se trouvent dans les Copperbelts d’Afrique centrale (Zambie et République démocratique du Congo), en font partie. Le boom minier ayant accompagné cette spéculation a ravivé l’intérêt scientifique pour l’extraction en Afrique. Cependant, au con...
title_zh: 鲁伯斯·本杰明编：《走进采矿资本主义：刚果和赞比亚铜带省工作的微观政治》
abstract_zh: 自21世纪10年代中期以来，电动汽车和其他电池供电的电子设备的普及引发了对战略金属的大量投机。铜和钴，其最重要的矿床位于中非的铜带省（赞比亚和刚果民主共和国），是其中的一部分。伴随这一投机的采矿热潮重新激发了科学界对非洲采矿业的兴趣。然而，关于...

title: Shacktopia
abstract: English Abstract: How modest can a utopia be? I approach this question with reference to the iShack, a solar electrification project in South Africa designed as an incremental upgrade for shack dwellers in informal settlements. Designed to provide basic energy for lighting and charging, the system also promises health and safety benefits by reducing the use of kerosene. Its promoters envision it as a bridge solution while people wait for better housing or municipal services. By offering an imperfect, stopgap form of enhancement, the venture exposes utopian expectations about progress, provoking critical anxieties about attenuated and unequal futures. At the same time, it bares the ecological limits of conventional infrastructure, the continuing inadequacies of state provision and the complex techno-politics of hope. French Abstract: Jusqu’à quel point une utopie peut-elle être modeste? J’aborde cette question en me référant à l’iShack, un projet d’électrifi cation solaire en Afrique du Sud conçu comme une mise à niveau progressive pour les habitants des cabanes dans les quartiers informels. Conçu pour fournir une énergie de base pour l’éclairage et la recharge, le système promet également des avantages en matière de santé et de sécurité en réduisant l’utilisation du kérosène. Ses promoteurs l’envisagent comme une solution de transition en attendant que les personnes concernées obtiennent un meilleur logement ou l’accès à des services municipaux. En offrant une forme imparfaite et provisoire d’amélioration, l’entreprise met à nu les attentes utopiques en matière de progrès, provoquant des angoisses critiques quant à des avenirs atténués et inégaux. En même temps, elle révèle les limites écologiques des infrastructures conventionnelles, les insuffi sances persistantes des services publics et la technopolitique complexe de l’espoir.
title_zh: 棚户乌托邦
abstract_zh: 一个乌托邦能有多谦卑？我通过iShack项目来探讨这一问题。iShack是南非的一个太阳能电气化项目，旨在为非正规住区的棚户居民提供渐进式升级。该系统设计用于提供照明和充电的基本能源，同时通过减少煤油的使用，还能带来健康和安全方面的益处。其推广者将其视为人们在等待更好的住房或市政服务期间的一种过渡解决方案。通过提供一种不完美、临时性的改善形式，该项目揭示了关于进步的乌托邦式期望，引发了人们对衰减和不平等未来的批判性焦虑。同时，它也暴露了传统基础设施的生态极限、国家供应的持续不足以及希望的复杂技术政治。

title: Longola Marche Arrière! Chinese diesel engines on Congo’s inland waterways
abstract: The comparatively cheap and mechanically accessible Chinese dakadaka diesel engines and their shotteur Z-drives have enabled wooden baleinières to significantly impact waterborne mobility, trade and transportation on the Congo River and its tributaries. While baleinières are artisanal watercraft made of local building materials, their engines are globally circulating technologies, which are able to unfold their economic, hydrodynamic and socio-technical affordances thanks to a number of local technical adaptations. On the basis of ethnographic fieldwork in Tshopo province (DR Congo) foregrounding the engines’ use, the article discusses the adaptations the Chinese engines and their propulsion system undergo to enable a felicitous engagement of their intrinsic engineered forces with the muscular, natural, and social forces present in their local riverine habitat. While this entanglement of forces depends on the distributed character of collective onboard engine care, it also encourages the emergence of baleinière owners (armateurs) as a new group of local entrepreneurs. These insights help us understand why, despite frequent breakdowns, the engines and the boats they propel enable and democratize the access to new forms of connectivity and mobility for large parts of Congo’s riverine and travelling urban populations. In a context of enduring economic precarity, the technical intervention of ‘removing (the engine’s) backward gear’ (Li. kolongola marche arrière) is therefore also of metaphoric significance.
title_zh: 《朗戈拉倒车档！》：中国柴油发动机在刚果内河航道上的应用
abstract_zh: 相对廉价且机械上易于操作的中国dakadaka柴油发动机及其shotteur Z型驱动装置，使木质baleinière船能够显著影响刚果河及其支流上的水上交通、贸易和运输。尽管baleinière是由当地建筑材料制成的工艺船舶，但其发动机是全球流通的技术，通过一系列当地技术适应，能够发挥其经济、流体动力学和社会技术特性。基于在刚果民主共和国乔波省进行的民族志田野调查，重点关注发动机的使用，文章讨论了中国的发动机及其推进系统所经历的改造，以使其内在的工程力与当地河流环境中的肌肉、自然和社会力量成功结合。虽然这种力的交织依赖于船上集体发动机维护的分布式特性，但也促进了baleinière船主作为当地企业家新群体的出现。这些见解有助于我们理解，尽管频繁发生故障，但这些发动机及其驱动的船舶为何能够使刚果河流域及流动城市人口中的大部分人获得并民主化新型连接和移动性。在持续的经济不稳定背景下，“拆除（发动机的）倒车档”这一技术干预也因此具有隐喻意义。

title: Beyond Confinement: Cape Gangsters and the Sub-Saharan Trade of Stolen Electronics
abstract: Instead of being perceived as confined to oppressive spaces in South Africa, detached from mainstream society, in this article I show that gangsters in Cape Town have harnessed liberalisation since the 1990s to become players in the market economy. This is illustrated by means of two criminal practices that support the illicit trade in electronics: residential burgling and transnational smuggling. By tracing the circulation of stolen electronics, gangsters and their migrant collaborators are shown to use flexible procedures to prevent detection and custody. These procedures capitalise on the changes brought by liberalisation, allowing for the efficient flow of electronics consignments to distant African cities and villages. It is argued that thinking through these procedures allows for a nuanced understanding of contemporary gang dynamics beyond confinement.
title_zh: 超越禁锢：开普敦帮派与撒哈拉以南地区的被盗电子产品贸易
abstract_zh: 本文认为，开普敦的帮派并没有如通常认为的那样被局限在南非压迫性的空间中、与主流社会脱节，而是自1990年代以来利用自由化成为了市场经济的参与者。这一点通过支撑电子产品非法贸易的两种犯罪实践——入室盗窃和跨国走私——得以说明。通过追踪被盗电子产品的流通，文章展示了帮派成员及其移民合作者如何运用灵活的程序来避免被发现和拘留。这些程序利用了自由化带来的变化，使得电子产品货物能够高效地流向遥远的非洲城市和村庄。文章认为，思考这些程序有助于在理解当代帮派动态时超越禁锢的视角。

title: Chinese-manufactured commodities and African agency in the democratization of consumption: the example of electronic devices in Cameroon
abstract: Liberalizing the economy brought both social and economic complications to the lives of many Cameroonians and growing numbers of affordable commodities manufactured in China. Focusing on electronic devices (primarily mobile phones, computers, recording gadgets and solar kits), this article considers how these new private possessions have become integrated into existing practices of social representation and to what extent they have transformed the lives of Cameroonians. The article examines through whose agency these commodities arrived, the findings being based on interviews with travelling traders and consumers and upon observations on Cameroonian and Chinese markets in the 2010s. It highlights that African importers of Chinese-manufactured products carefully select and order supplies in China that are affordable and meet the tastes of local consumers. The availability of these goods enables Cameroonians to engage in the consumption of global commodities, heightening their sense of global connection, whilst also concurrently complicating the display of social hierarchies. The importation of these commodities also created business opportunities for numerous traders and service providers.
title_zh: 中国制造商品与非洲消费者民主化进程中的能动性：以喀麦隆的电子设备为例
abstract_zh: 经济自由化给许多喀麦隆人的生活带来了社会和经济上的复杂性，同时越来越多来自中国的廉价商品涌入。本文聚焦于电子设备（主要是手机、电脑、录音设备和太阳能套件），探讨这些新的私人财产如何融入现有的社会表征实践，以及它们在多大程度上改变了喀麦隆人的生活。文章考察了这些商品通过谁的中介而来，研究基于2010年代对行商和消费者的访谈以及对喀麦隆和中国市场的观察。研究强调，中国产品的非洲进口商会精心挑选和订购中国供应中价格实惠且符合当地消费者口味的商品。这些商品的可得性使喀麦隆人能够参与全球商品的消费，增强了他们的全球联系感，同时也使社会等级的展示变得复杂。这些商品的进口也为众多贸易商和服务提供商创造了商业机会。

title: Cutting without Cutting Connection: The Semiotics of Power Patrols in Urban Tanzania
abstract: Abstract Before the total cutoff of a household for unpaid electrical bills, and in anticipation of the violence it might precipitate, national power utility inspectors in Dar es Salaam have recourse to a gradient of ‘soft’ disconnections designed to signal good faith and encourage repayment. Drawing on a mixture of semiotics and exchange theory, this article argues that such soft disconnections may be understood as moments when the shared grounds of the household-utility relation—both the physical power network and social commitments it embodies—become figured, modified, and ultimately preserved in the face of urban postcolonial strain. Whereas semiosis is often thought of as a kind of infrastructural bridge that links sign to interpretant (or object to sign), the inspectors’ reflexively phatic signaling of common grounds highlights the thoroughly semiotic nature of infrastructure itself. More generally, the very presumption and preservation of shared grounds is a salutary alternative to the anti-relational violence and extinction that characterizes much of the contemporary world.
title_zh: 不切断连接的切断：坦桑尼亚城市电力巡查的符号学
abstract_zh: 摘要 在因未缴电费而完全切断家庭用电之前，达累斯萨拉姆的国家电力公司巡查员会采用一种称为“软切断”的渐进式方法，旨在表明善意并鼓励还款。本文结合符号学和交换理论，认为这种软切断可以被理解为家庭与电力公司关系的共同基础——包括物理电力网络及其所承载的社会承诺——在面对后殖民城市压力时被塑造、修改并最终得以保存的时刻。尽管符号过程通常被视为一种连接符号与解释项（或对象与符号）的基础设施桥梁，但巡查员对共同基础的反思性接触行为揭示了基础设施本身的彻底符号性。更广泛地说，对共同基础的推定和保存是对当代世界许多特征——即反关系的暴力与灭绝——的一种有益替代。

title: Front and Back Covers, Volume 37, Number 4. August 2021
abstract: Front and back cover caption, volume 37 issue 4 Front cover TOXIC FLOWS: E‐WASTE RECYCLING A worker starts a fire to burn off the insulation from electrical cables to extract copper at an informal e‐waste recycling site in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Open fire is one of the methods used here to mine metals from defunct electronics devices and their components. Electronic waste is one of the fastest‐growing types of waste worldwide. However, many countries lack the formalized infrastructures necessary to collect and handle e‐waste safely. The informal sector has stepped up to fill the gap. E‐waste attracts urban dwellers seeking to extract value from these discarded materials while releasing toxic compounds detrimental to health and the environment. In this special issue on toxic flows, Samwel Moses Ntapanta follows Dar es Salaam's informal e‐waste recyclers to find out how they understand the toxic nature of their work and what measures they take to minimize exposure. The number of informal e‐waste recycling workshops in Dar es Salaam has skyrocketed in recent years. High demand for metals, like copper, offers a stable livelihood for e‐waste recycling workers. Scavenging spare parts from the electronic afterlives is primarily driven by a vibrant Tanzanian local market, giving an impetus to repurpose certain materials. During these activities (mining, repurposing, restoring and reusing), workers are exposed to many toxic chemical compounds. With little or no knowledge about these, workers in informal e‐waste recycling face unknown risks of exposure as they make a dangerous living in urban environments. Back cover TOXIC FLOWS: GLYPHOSATE Launch of the #StopGlyphosate campaign supported by the European Citizens' Initiative (ECI) and 37 European organizations in front of the European Parliament, 8 February 2017. Across the globe, grass‐roots movements against glyphosate, the world's most used herbicide, have encouraged regulators to re‐examine its safety assessments. In Europe, a drawn‐out process is widely expected to conclude that glyphosate is harmful to health and should be banned across all 28 member states. If so, this would likely lead to similar decisions in other markets, representing a blow to the agrochemical industry. More than any other pesticide, efforts to ban glyphosate have become tied up with questions of national sovereignty. From Vietnam and Thailand to Colombia and Mexico, the US government has threatened ‘trade disruption’ should a ban go ahead. The message is clear: chemical regulation is an international, not a domestic, matter. Nevertheless, glyphosate has become a standard for emerging populism. In post‐war Sri Lanka, banning glyphosate became a mission of Buddhist nationalist movements seeking to purify the national body. In the UK, Brexit supporters argued an independent UK would have the freedom to stop glyphosate (another ‘Vote Leave’ promise quickly broken). As politics the world over has re‐engaged with questions of national identity and autonomy, halting the free flow of glyphosate has become a goal for those on the left and right of the political spectrum.
title_zh: 第37卷第4期封面与封底，2021年8月
abstract_zh: 封面和封底说明，第37卷第4期 封面 毒性流：电子废物回收 工人在坦桑尼亚达累斯萨拉姆的一个非正规电子废物回收站点点火烧掉电缆绝缘层以提取铜。明火是这里用来从废弃电子设备及其组件中提取金属的方法之一。电子废物是全球增长最快的废物类型之一。然而，许多国家缺乏安全收集和处理电子废物所需的正式基础设施。非正规部门已介入填补这一空白。电子废物吸引着城市居民，他们试图从这些废弃材料中提取价值，同时释放有害健康和环境的毒性化合物。在本期关于毒性流的专题中，Samwel Moses Ntapanta 跟随达累斯萨拉姆的非正规电子废物回收者，了解他们如何理解自己工作的毒性，以及他们采取哪些措施来减少暴露。近年来，达累斯萨拉姆的非正规电子废物回收作坊数量激增。对铜等金属的高需求为电子废物回收工人提供了稳定的生计。从电子遗体中拾取备用零件主要是受到活跃的坦桑尼亚本地市场的驱动，这推动了某些材料的再利用。在这些活动（采矿、再利用、修复和重用）中，工人暴露于许多毒性化合物。由于对这些知之甚少，非正规电子废物回收工人面临着未知的暴露风险，他们在城市环境中过着危险的生活。封底 毒性流：草甘膦 2017年2月8日，在欧洲议会前，由欧洲公民倡议（ECI）和37个欧洲组织支持的#StopGlyphosate运动启动。全球范围内，反对草甘膦（世界上使用最广泛的除草剂）的草根运动已促使监管机构重新审查其安全性评估。在欧洲，一个漫长的过程被普遍认为将得出结论，即草甘膦对健康有害，并应在所有28个成员国中禁止。如果是这样，这可能会导致其他市场做出类似决定，对农化行业造成打击。超过任何其他农药，禁止草甘膦的努力已与国家主权问题紧密相连。从越南和泰国到哥伦比亚和墨西哥，美国政府威胁如果禁令实施，将造成“贸易中断”。信息很明确：化学品监管是国际事务，而非国内事务。尽管如此，草甘膦已成为新兴民粹主义的标准。在战后的斯里兰卡，禁止草甘膦成为佛教民族主义运动净化民族身体的任务。在英国，脱欧支持者认为独立的英国将有自由停止使用草甘膦（又一个迅速打破的“离开”承诺）。随着世界各地的政治重新参与国家认同和自治问题，阻止草甘膦的自由流动已成为政治光谱左右两派的目标。

title: Future‐proof: bunkered data centres and the selling of ultra‐secure cloud storage
journal_name: JOURNAL OF THE ROYAL ANTHROPOLOGICAL INSTITUTE
abstract: Abstract Abandoned after the Cold War, nuclear bunkers around the world have found afterlives as ultra‐secure data storage sites for cloud computing providers. The operators of these bunkered data centres capitalize on the spatial, temporal, and material security affordances of their subterranean fortresses, promoting them as ‘future‐proof’ cloud storage solutions. Taking the concept of ‘future‐proofing’ as its entry‐point, this essay explores how data centre professionals work with the imaginative properties of the bunker to configure data as an object to be securitized. The essay takes the form of an ethnographic tour through a UK‐based data bunker. During this tour, threatening data futures and fragile data materialities are conjured in order to secure the conditions of possibility for the bunkered data centre's commercial continuity. Future‐proofing, it is argued, provides a conceptual opening onto the entangled imperatives of security and marketing that drive the commercial data storage industry.
title_zh: 未来防护：掩体数据中心与超安全云存储的销售
abstract_zh: 摘要在冷战结束后，世界各地的核掩体被重新用作云服务提供商的超安全数据存储站点。这些掩体数据中心的操盘手利用其地下堡垒的空间、时间和物质安全可供性，将其推广为“未来防护”的云存储解决方案。本文以“未来防护”概念为切入点，探讨数据中心专业人员如何利用掩体的想象特性将数据配置为需要证券化的对象。文章以一场位于英国的数据掩体民族志考察形式展开。在这次考察中，威胁性的数据未来和脆弱的数据物质性被召唤出来，以确保掩体数据中心商业持续的可能性条件。本文认为，未来防护为理解推动商业数据存储行业的安全与营销交织的命令提供了一个概念性入口。

title: Road warriors to digital nomads: portable computers, habitats, and remote work
abstract: This article focuses on two users of early portable computers – the ‘road warrior’ and ‘digital nomad’ of the 1980s and 90s – to illustrate how portability has served an imperialist function in engineering a world fit for buffering privileged subjects against conditions of existential precariousness. The label ‘road warriors’ emerged in the early history of portable computers as a reaction against the hostile environs of airports and aeroplanes, spaces that were deemed unaccommodating to the use of laptops. These complaints made clear the importance of portable milieus, spaces that had to come into existence to accommodate the transversal of portable computers. The article examines how these emergent portable milieus functioned also as pedagogical habitats, worldly enclosures that guided white, middle/upper-classed, male executives on the means to adapt to a precarious economic existence. Drawing from computer magazines, news articles, and the manifesto Digital Nomad, the article illustrates how these habitats romanticized the value of remote workers, legitimated their transformation of environments, and laid a foundation for the world to be engineered as a buffer for privileged populations. The trend of digital nomadism today which seeks to create opportunities for the austere good life amidst endemic economic problems in the West, speaks to the currency of this imaginary and the longstanding politics of remote work, ushered in by portable computers.
title_zh: 从公路战士到数字游牧者：便携式计算机、栖息地与远程工作
abstract_zh: 本文聚焦于早期便携式计算机的两类用户——20世纪80年代和90年代的“公路战士”与“数字游牧者”——以说明便携性在打造一个适合缓冲特权主体对抗存在性不稳定条件的世界中所发挥的帝国主义功能。“公路战士”这一标签在便携式计算机的早期历史中出现，是对机场和飞机等被认为不适合使用笔记本电脑的敌对环境的一种反应。这些抱怨揭示了便携环境的重要性，即必须存在一些空间来适应便携式计算机的横向移动。文章考察了这些新兴的便携环境如何同时扮演着教学栖息地的角色，即引导白人、中上层阶级男性高管适应不稳定的经济存在的世俗围场。通过引用计算机杂志、新闻文章和宣言《数字游牧者》，文章阐释了这些栖息地如何浪漫化远程工作者的价值，合法化他们对环境的改造，并为世界被改造成特权人群的缓冲带奠定了基础。今天，数字游牧主义趋势试图在西方普遍经济问题中为严酷的美好生活创造机会，这体现了这一想象的现时性与便携式计算机所引发的远程工作的长期政治。

title: Smart homes: domestic futurity as Infrastructure
abstract: This essay analyzes the way that the Brookfield Residential (BR) Smart Home constructs domestic futurity, or a set of cultural practices and meanings pertaining to a mediated, technologically-advanced home and homelife. The BR Smart Home is a new mass-market smart domestic product produced in partnership with retail and logistics hegemon, Amazon. The Smart Home offers customizable, luxury smart living, to include the traditional (stainless steel appliances, a butler’s pantry) and the transitional (a drone heliopad, a new ‘Drop Zone’ room for Amazon and other deliveries). As an exemplar of mass-market smart home technology, the Smart Home communicates the durability of traditional conceptions of domesticity in the smart home age. At the same time, the BR Smart Home reveals the material shifts in domestic spaces goaded by new technological and economic developments. The Smart Homes’ changing spatial configurations reflect upon and intensify infrastructures that fortify divisions between the Smart Homeowners and marginalized others. Drawing on fieldwork completed at several BR Smart Homes, I argue that domestic futurity is a form of infrastructure that is (1) so well distributed as to be frequently hidden, (2) agential and transitional, and (3) subject to cultural transformation while simultaneously upholding residues of traditional domesticity.
title_zh: 智能家居：作为基础设施的家庭未来性
abstract_zh: 本文分析了布鲁克菲尔德住宅（BR）智能家居如何构建家庭未来性，即一套关于中介化、技术先进的家庭和家庭生活的文化实践和意义。BR智能家居是与零售和物流霸主亚马逊合作生产的新型大众市场智能家居产品。该智能家居提供可定制的豪华智能生活，包括传统设施（不锈钢家电、管家储藏室）和过渡性设施（无人机停机坪、用于亚马逊及其他快递的新“投递区”房间）。作为大众市场智能家居技术的典范，智能家居传达了在智能家居时代传统家庭观念的持久性。同时，BR智能家居揭示了新技术和经济发展所引发的家庭空间的物质变化。智能家居不断变化的空间配置反映并强化了基础设施，这些基础设施加深了智能房主与边缘化他人之间的鸿沟。基于在多个BR智能家居进行的田野工作，我认为家庭未来性是一种基础设施，其特点是（1）分布广泛以至于通常隐藏，（2）具有能动性和过渡性，以及（3）在经历文化转型的同时维持着传统家庭观念的残余。

title: The Data Multiple: Seeing Double in Digital Entrepreneurialism
abstract: Media and critical data scholars often critique digital entrepreneurs for endorsing narrow and positivist models of data and corporeality. But what happens when device makers plan for digital uncertainty and are invested in fostering interpretive fluidity of both data and bodies? Drawing on two years of ethnographic fieldwork with makers of wearable computing in New York City's Silicon Alley, this article argues that creators of wearable technology work with more pluralized concepts of data than digital scholars often recognize. In marketing materials and public-facing documents, devices makers often do promote the idea that wearable technology can help people to patiently synchronize their digital records so as to compile Borgesian archives of their experiences. In practice, commercial imperatives effectively require that product makers also cultivate a multifaceted regard of personal data and somatic experience. In examining how device makers capitalize on the ambiguities inherent to digital knowing and thus enact a digital economy shaped by pliable rather than atomized notions of corporeality and data, this article opens onto wider debates about the politics of digital representation.
title_zh: 数据多重性：数字创业中的双重审视
abstract_zh: 媒体和批判数据学者经常批评数字创业者支持狭隘的实证主义数据和具身性模型。但当设备制造商计划应对数字不确定性，并致力于培养数据和身体的双重阐释流动性时，会发生什么？基于在纽约硅巷对可穿戴计算设备制造商的两年民族志田野调查，本文认为可穿戴技术的创造者使用的数据概念比数字学者通常认识到的更加多元化。在营销材料和公开文件中，设备制造商确实经常推广这样的观念：可穿戴技术可以帮助人们耐心地同步他们的数字记录，从而汇编出博尔赫斯式的个人经历档案。在实践中，商业要求实际上迫使产品制造商也培养对个人数据和身体体验的多方面关注。通过考察设备制造商如何利用数字认知固有的模糊性，从而塑造一个由可塑性而非原子化的身体和数据概念所塑造的数字经济，本文开启了对数字表征政治的更广泛讨论。

title: The Shenzhen Experiment: The Story of China's Instant City. JuanDu, Cambridge: Harvard University Press, 2020, 384 pp.
title_zh: 深圳实验：中国速成城市的故事

title: Thermopolitics of data: cloud infrastructures and energy futures
abstract: This article develops the notion of a thermopolitics of data to describe an ongoing infrastructural integration of the platform economy with energy politics through the mediation of heat. Building on fieldwork conducted at a data centre owned by a major Russian digital platform that, since 2016, has been the main source of heating for the Finnish town of Mantsala, the article analyzes the ways in which the materialities of heat and data get mobilized by different actors to produce a new object-the data centre as a thermal urban infrastructure. Situating these processes in a history of shifting scientific and popular understandings of future fuels, and of the relation between information and energy, the article extends emergent scholarly literature on the cultures of thermal manipulation that underpin digital media. An enquiry into the thermopolitics of data illuminates the ways in which bodies and spaces are silently integrated and infrastructurally organized to simultaneously function as objects of quantification, commodification and differentiation, and the provisioning of thermal regulation and human care for these practices. In the formation of these relations, new regulatory, ethical and epistemological questions about the relationship between data, agency and energy arise.
title_zh: 数据的热政治：云基础设施与能源未来
abstract_zh: 本文提出了“数据的热政治”这一概念，用以描述平台经济与能源政治之间通过热的中介进行的持续基础设施整合。基于对一家俄罗斯主要数字平台拥有的数据中心的田野调查，该数据中心自2016年以来一直是芬兰曼塔拉镇的主要热源，文章分析了热和数据的物质性如何被不同行动者调动，以产生一个新的对象——作为热城市基础设施的数据中心。将这些过程置于对未来燃料以及信息与能源之间关系的科学与大众理解变迁的历史中，文章扩展了关于支撑数字媒体的热操控文化的现有学术文献。对数据热政治的探究揭示了身体和空间如何被静默地整合和基础设施地组织，以同时充当量化、商品化和差异化的对象，以及为这些实践提供热调节和人类关怀。在这些关系的形成中，关于数据、能动性和能源之间关系的新的监管、伦理和认识论问题随之产生。

title: Tracking selves or tracking relationships? Means of measuring time amongst Ethiopian runners
journal_name: JOURNAL OF THE ROYAL ANTHROPOLOGICAL INSTITUTE
abstract: Abstract GPS watches and digital self‐tracking devices (DSTDs) have been characterized as ‘self‐tracking’ devices, assuming a dyadic relationship between individuals and technologies. Amongst Ethiopian professional runners, such devices have become increasingly sought after, and yet they are embedded in deeper relationships of collaborative work, submission, and authority. They circulate between people, tracking relationships as much as they track selves. I place their use in the context of the discourses and practices of two of the main corporations working with runners in Ethiopia to suggest that the logic of exponential acceleration upon which these corporations rely is contested by Ethiopian runners, who attempt to achieve a synthesis between external scientific knowledge and pre‐existing ideas about energy, risk, and collective work. Whilst DSTDs may offer a tantalizing opportunity to give in to individualistic urges, in fact they crystallize existing tensions in Amhara society between centrifugal desire and duties of care and reciprocity.
title_zh: 追踪自我还是追踪关系？埃塞俄比亚跑者测量时间的方式
abstract_zh: GPS手表和数字自我追踪设备（DSTD）被描述为‘自我追踪’设备，假设个人与技术之间存在二元关系。在埃塞俄比亚职业跑者中，这类设备越来越受欢迎，但它们被嵌入在协作工作、服从和权威的更深层次关系中。它们在人与人之间流通，追踪关系如同追踪自我。我将它们的使用置于埃塞俄比亚两家与跑者合作的主要公司的话语和实践背景下，提出这些公司依赖的指数加速逻辑受到埃塞俄比亚跑者的质疑，他们试图在外部科学知识与关于能量、风险和集体工作的既有观念之间实现综合。虽然DSTD可能提供屈服于个人主义冲动的诱人机会，但实际上它们固化了阿姆哈拉社会中离心欲望与关怀和互惠责任之间的现有张力。

title: Unearthing conscious intent in women’s everyday resistance to mining in Indonesia
abstract: Resistance to nickel mining in Sorowako, Indonesia has existed since the operation started taking land from farmers in the 1970s. However, in Sorowako and beyond, little is known about the gendered nature of everyday resistance to mining. We conducted a photovoice study with women from two Indigenous communities affected by the same mine to uncover conscious intent in everyday resistance. Some scholars call for abandoning intent and consciousness in analytical frameworks for everyday resistance, but by pairing photovoice with a conjunctural exercise, we found women’s awareness of how dispossession and exploitation for mining affects them and their responses to mining as rural Indigenous women. The participants used photovoice to show that their everyday acts, such as accessing forbidden land, intend to lessen their domination and better their conditions, a kind of quiet encroachment of the ordinary theorized by Bayat.
title_zh: 揭示印度尼西亚女性对采矿日常抵抗中的意识意图
abstract_zh: 自20世纪70年代采矿活动开始从农民手中夺取土地以来，印度尼西亚索罗瓦科的镍矿开采抵抗就已存在。然而，在索罗瓦科及其他地区，关于采矿日常抵抗的性别化特征知之甚少。我们与受同一矿场影响的两个原住民社区的妇女进行了一项影像发声研究，以揭示日常抵抗中的意识意图。一些学者主张在日常抵抗的分析框架中放弃意图和意识，但通过将影像发声与联结性练习相结合，我们发现女性意识到剥夺和采矿剥削对她们的影响，以及她们作为农村原住民女性的回应。参与者使用影像发声展示了她们的日常行为，例如进入禁地，意在减轻支配并改善自身处境，这是一种由巴亚特理论化的“日常的悄然侵占”。

title: ‘Lifescaping’ toxicants: Locating and living with e‐waste in Tanzania
abstract: Based on fieldwork in an informal scrap recycling workshop, this article explores how unregulated electronic waste (e‐waste) handling activities in Dar es Salaam expose workers to toxic substances as part of their livelihoods. These informal economic activities are situated in the urban landscape within the surrounding global flows of e‐waste and recycling and demonstrate how workers reflect on and seek to mitigate the toxic exposures they encounter as part of daily life. The concept ‘lifescaping’ is used to show how, while informal workers may be aware of toxic exposures and make the best of tricky situations in various ways, they have limited access to information about the dangers and must develop their own strategies by performing various micro‐actions through which they hope to protect themselves.
title_zh: “生活化”有毒物质：在坦桑尼亚定位和应对电子废弃物
abstract_zh: 基于在一个非正式废品回收作坊的田野调查，本文探讨了坦桑尼亚达累斯萨拉姆不受监管的电子废弃物处理活动如何使工人接触有毒物质，并以此作为其生计的一部分。这些非正规经济活动位于城市景观中，处于全球电子废弃物和回收流动的背景下，并展示了工人们如何反思并试图减轻他们在日常生活中遇到的有毒暴露。文中使用“生活化”这一概念来说明，尽管非正规工人可能意识到有毒暴露，并以各种方式尽力应对棘手情况，但他们接触危险信息的途径有限，必须通过采取各种微小行动来制定自己的策略，以期保护自己。

title: ‘The world is sinking:’ sand, urban infrastructure, and world-cities
abstract: From the construction of ports to the dredging of access corridors for ships and the production of asphalt and concrete, sand is an inextricable part of urban environments. Focusing on the molecular transformations of sand–from silt to concrete to rubble–the first half of this paper studies the geosocial history of Dubai over the course of the twentieth century, including the dredging of Dubai Creek, the making of Jebel Ali Port, and the construction of the World Islands. I draw on reports, archival records, and newspapers, as well as existing scholarship, to demonstrate the infrastructural exuberance of Dubai, its tendency to marshal vast amounts of sand in the construction of increasingly outrageous infrastructures. In the second half of the paper, I follow some of the threads that emerge from this site in a more theoretical and comparative register. I draw comparisons between Dubai and similar world–cities in the global South, to understand and critique how this infrastructural exuberance exists alongside increasing concerns over ‘sand scarcity'. Drawing on the work of Georges Bataille (1991. The accursed share: volume 1: consumption, tr. by Hurley, R. New York: Zone Books), Gilles Deleuze and Felix Guattari (1983. Anti–oedipus: capitalism and schizophrenia, tr. by Hurley, R. New York, NY: Penguin Classics; 1987. A thousand plateaus: capitalism and schizophrenia, tr. by Massumi, B. Minneapolis: University of Minnesota Press), and McKenzie Wark (2015. Molecular red: theory for the anthropocene. New York: Verso), I develop a framework of antiproductive ecologies that treats incommensurable forms of surplus and waste (such as sand and rubble) as constitutive of world–cities. Developing Deleuze and Guattari's concept of ‘antiproduction’ from an environmental perspective, I argue that in their exuberance and thirst for construction, world–cities like Dubai attempt to organize and render productive the very planetary distribution of sand and silt.
title_zh: “世界正在下沉”：沙子、城市基础设施与世界城市
abstract_zh: 从港口建设到船舶通航通道的疏浚，再到沥青和混凝土的生产，沙子是城市环境不可或缺的一部分。本文前半部分聚焦于沙子的分子转变——从淤泥到混凝土再到碎石，研究了20世纪迪拜的地球社会历史，包括迪拜河的疏浚、杰贝阿里港的建设以及世界群岛的建造。我利用报告、档案记录和报纸以及现有学术研究，展示了迪拜基础设施的铺张，以及它在建造越来越离谱的基础设施时调动大量沙子的倾向。在论文的后半部分，我以更理论和比较的方式，追踪了从这个地点浮现的一些线索。我将迪拜与全球南方的类似世界城市进行比较，以理解并批判这种基础设施铺张如何与日益严重的“沙子稀缺”担忧并存。借鉴乔治·巴塔耶（1991，《被诅咒的部分：第一卷：消费》）、吉尔·德勒兹和菲利克斯·加塔利（1983，《反俄狄浦斯：资本主义与精神分裂症》；1987，《千高原：资本主义与精神分裂症》）以及麦肯齐·沃克（2015，《分子红色：人类世理论》）的著作，我发展了一个反生产生态学的框架，将不可通约的剩余和废物形式（如沙子和碎石）视为世界城市的构成要素。从环境角度发展德勒兹和加塔利的“反生产”概念，我认为像迪拜这样的世界城市在其铺张和对建设的渴望中，试图组织并使沙子和淤泥的全球分布变得富有成效。

title: ‘We don't even know who owns it’: the infrastructural imaginary of Spruce Pine, NC
abstract: This project explores in/visibility, publicity, and politics in the infrastructural imaginary of Spruce Pine, a mining town in the US state of North Carolina. Through participant observation and other direct experiences, and as an interdisciplinary exercise in studying from below, I examine how the town's supplying of high-quality quartz (HQQ) to high-tech industries is entangled with their promoted identity as a gem-mining location. From the perspective of ideological- and material-discursive practices, I examine processes of open secreting, disarticulation from a ‘high tech’ identity and its connotations, and a nostalgic emphasis on the town's gem-mining identity. The political ramifications of these entanglements are presented in the example of the town's pro-Trump Fourth of July parade. I conclude by reflecting on how the complex entanglements of seemingly contradictory ideological practices work in part due to their alignment with regional culture and history.
title_zh: “我们甚至不知道谁拥有它”：北卡罗来纳州斯普鲁斯派恩的基础设施想象
abstract_zh: 该项目探讨了美国北卡罗来纳州的一个矿业小镇斯普鲁斯派恩的基础设施想象中的可见性、宣传和政治。通过参与观察和其他直接体验，并作为一项从下往上的跨学科研究，我考察了该镇向高科技产业供应高纯度石英（HQQ）如何与其作为宝石矿产地点的推广身份纠缠在一起。从意识形态和物质-话语实践的角度，我研究了公开保密、与“高科技”身份及其含义的脱节，以及对小镇宝石矿业身份的怀旧强调的过程。这些纠缠的政治后果以该镇支持特朗普的七月四日游行为例呈现。我最后反思了看似矛盾的意识形态实践的复杂纠缠如何部分由于其与区域文化和历史的一致性而发挥作用。

title: British sofas and global toxic flows
abstract: Invisible and volatile, persistent and accumulating in the environment, toxic organic substances like Polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs) are used in furniture and electrical appliances. They spread around the world through commodity production and consumption, second‐hand and waste trade, and air and sea currents, as well as in the bodies of migratory animals. Absorbed by and accumulated in living beings, they may interfere with metabolism and behaviour, and damage genetic material. Their flows connect British sofas to African recycling workshops to Chinese metal traders, and tropical waste dumps to arctic seabirds. They are the kind of material that the anthropology of the Anthropocene may attach itself to in seeking critical engagement with scientists, activists, regulators, and producers and consumers.
title_zh: 英国沙发与全球有毒物质流动
abstract_zh: 多溴联苯醚（PBDEs）等有毒有机物质，具有隐形、易挥发、持久且在环境中积累的特性，被用于家具和电器中。它们通过商品生产和消费、二手及废物贸易、空气和海流，以及迁徙动物的身体传播到全球。被生物吸收并积累后，它们可能干扰新陈代谢和行为，并损害遗传物质。这些流动将英国沙发与非洲的回收车间、中国的金属贸易商，以及热带垃圾场与北极海鸟联系在一起。这类物质是人类世人类学可能依附的材料，以寻求与科学家、活动家、监管者、生产者和消费者的批判性互动。

title: Follow the computers: Entangled mobilities of people and things in transnational recycling
abstract: This paper contributes to our understanding of the social life of used computers in West Africa through analysis of the sending, distribution, recognition, and reception of recycled equipment. Based on multi-sited and longitudinal fieldwork in Denmark and Ghana, it employs George Marcus’ suggestion of following things as a methodological selection device for ethnography. Theoretically, it engages the concept of affective circuits to address how transnational recycling, belonging, hometown development, and family relations are interlinked. I present a three-fold argument: first, that the actions of sending, distributing, recognizing, and receiving used equipment enable different actors to demonstrate and perform hometown belonging, development, and leadership; second, that these capacities reflect differentiated mobilities and connectivity of the people involved; and third, that the recycled furniture and information technology (IT) gear become upcycled to objects of value, being mobilized and transformed through long-term processes and negotiations of reciprocity.
title_zh: 追踪计算机：跨国回收中人与物的纠缠流动
abstract_zh: 本文通过分析二手电脑的发送、分配、识别和接收过程，加深了我们对西非地区二手电脑社会生活的理解。基于在丹麦和加纳的多地点和纵向田野调查，它采用乔治·马库斯提出的“追踪物品”作为民族志的方法论选择工具。在理论上，它运用情感回路的概念来探讨跨国回收、归属感、家乡发展和家庭关系之间的相互关联。我提出了三重论证：第一，发送、分配、识别和接收二手设备的行动使不同的行动者能够展示和践行家乡归属感、发展和领导力；第二，这些能力反映了相关人员的差异化流动性和连通性；第三，回收的家具和信息科技设备被升级为有价值的物品，通过长期的过程和互惠协商被动员和转化。

title: Ghosts and Miracles: The Volkswagen as Imperial Debris in Postwar West Germany
journal_name: COMPARATIVE STUDIES IN SOCIETY AND HISTORY
abstract: Abstract Starting with the author's own experience of ghostliness in the archive, the article explores the political meaning of the postwar Volkswagen in West Germany as embodiment of the country's “economic miracle.” The investigation follows the uncanny in texts and images about the Volkswagen between 1945 and 1960 and argues that the car carried with it a “public secret” as a “debris” from the Nazi empire that silently transcended the 1945 divide. This reading of the Volkswagen as well as the methodological path toward it highlight a phenomenon that postcolonial scholars have described as “haunting”: a confusion about the relationship between past and present that also bears on those who study the past. Taking this analysis as an encouragement to revisit the powerful myths and “miracles” of postwar consumer cultures in the West from a new angle, the article calls for historical genealogies of these myths that conceive of the postwar West as a—not yet—postcolonial space and that cross the 1945 threshold.
title_zh: 鬼魂与奇迹：作为帝国残骸的大众汽车在战后西德
abstract_zh: 摘要从作者自己在档案中的鬼魂体验出发，探讨了战后西德大众汽车作为该国“经济奇迹”体现的政治意义。研究追踪了1945年至1960年间关于大众汽车的文本与图像中的神秘性，认为该汽车携带着一个“公开的秘密”，作为纳粹帝国的“残骸”默默跨越了1945年的分界线。这种对大众汽车的解读以及通向它的方法论路径，突显了后殖民学者所描述的“萦绕”现象：一种关于过去与现在关系的困惑，这种困惑也影响到研究过去的人。本文将此分析作为鼓励，从新的角度重新审视战后西方消费文化中的强大神话与“奇迹”，呼吁对这些神话进行历史谱系学考察，将战后西方视为一个尚未成为后殖民的空间，并跨越1945年的门槛。

title: Introduction
abstract: The introduction to this special issue begins by surveying the significance of what we call Africa’s internal energy frontiers for understanding a global energy realignment marked by experiments in renewable technologies as well as revanchist investments in fossil fuels. It then discusses capture as a concept rooted in both Marxist informed accounts of global energy regimes as well as the political histories and practices of African populations. Finally, it discusses the articles as spanning three economies of capture along Africa’s energy frontier: resurgent extractivism, post-carbon development and consumer renewables.
title_zh: 引言
abstract_zh: 本期特刊的引言首先审视了我们所谓的非洲内部能源前沿对于理解全球能源重新调整的重要性，这种调整的特点是可再生能源技术的实验以及对化石燃料的倒退投资。然后讨论了“捕获”这一概念，它根植于马克思主义对全球能源体制的解释以及非洲人口的政治历史和实践。最后，讨论了涉及非洲能源前沿三个捕获经济体的文章：复兴的榨取主义、后碳发展和消费者可再生能源。

title: The Politics of Media Infrastructure: Mobile Phones and Emergent Forms of Public Communication in Papua New Guinea
abstract: ABSTRACT Recent work in anthropology proposes that the ethnographic study of infrastructure offers a productive way to think about how states and corporations, citizens and consumers, all define their relations and obligations to each other. This article considers the politics of media infrastructure in Papua New Guinea (PNG) by tracing the moral economy of mobile phones. It focuses on (1) how mobile phone users have taken to social media to express dissatisfaction with the dominant mobile network operator, Digicel, a privately owned foreign company; and (2) how the PNG state has attempted to regulate the use of mobile phones and social media through cybercrime legislation and registration of Subscriber Identity Modules (SIM cards). Consideration of these two issues – matters of concern that gather publics around them – enables an assessment of the promise of improved telecommunications and social media, in particular, to make government in PNG more accountable and transparent.
title_zh: 媒体基础设施的政治：巴布亚新几内亚的手机与新兴公共传播形式
abstract_zh: 近期人类学的研究提出，对基础设施的民族志研究为思考国家与公司、公民与消费者如何定义彼此之间的关系和义务提供了一种富有成效的方式。本文通过追溯手机的道德经济，考虑了巴布亚新几内亚（PNG）媒体基础设施的政治。它聚焦于：（1）手机用户如何利用社交媒体表达对主导移动网络运营商Digicel（一家私营外国公司）的不满；（2）巴布亚新几内亚国家如何通过网络犯罪立法和SIM卡注册来尝试监管手机和社交媒体的使用。对这两个问题（围绕它们聚集公众的关切事项）的考察，使得评估改善电信和社交媒体（特别是使巴布亚新几内亚政府更加负责任和透明）的承诺成为可能。

title: Transgressing the Right to the City: Urban Mining and Ecotourism in Post-Industrial Romania
abstract: This article describes emerging structures of power and informal workers' everyday resistance in the context of a European Union ecotourism project in the post-industrial Romanian mining town of Bălan. In 2011 and 2012, a public-private partnership began demolishing Bălan's mine buildings, a project that exemplifies neoliberal capitalist urban renewal. The project also featured a new hybrid of urban reconstruction and urban mining: the extraction and resale of metal from anthropogenic supplies in wasted post-industrial buildings. Unemployed industrial workers, whom I call "informal urban miners," collected and sold metal alongside formal workers. Of primary importance to informal urban miners was attuning their skill and mode of communication to the demolition company's workers and heavy machinery. Although at first glance it looked like informal urban mining facilitated their integration into Bălan's neoliberal economy, I argue that this work offered unexpected opportunities for transgressing project organizers' authority. Urban anthropologists often overlook such practices when, as in the case of informal urban mining, the differences between resistance and market activity are subtle and contingently negotiated. Informal urban miners' skill and communicative practices were complexly embedded in emerging structures of power in the post-industrial city: simultaneously a necessity of the working environment, a way of sustaining a livelihood, and a way to transgress the very order that produces and reproduces such wasted urban environments.
title_zh: 超越城市权：后工业罗马尼亚的城市采矿与生态旅游
abstract_zh: 本文描述了在欧盟后工业罗马尼亚采矿小镇Bălan的生态旅游项目中，权力结构与非正规工人的日常抵抗。2011年至2012年，一家公私合营企业开始拆除Bălan的矿山建筑，该项目体现了新自由主义资本主义的城市更新。该项目还引入了城市重建与城市采矿的新混合模式：从废弃的后工业建筑中的人造物资中提取和转售金属。我称之为“非正规城市矿工”的失业产业工人与正式工人一起收集和销售金属。对非正规城市矿工而言，最重要的是调整他们的技能和沟通方式以适应拆除公司的工人和重型机械。尽管初看之下，非正规城市采矿似乎促进了他们融入Bălan的新自由主义经济，但我认为这项工作为超越项目组织者的权威提供了意想不到的机会。城市人类学家常常忽视此类实践，例如在非正规城市采矿中，抵抗与市场活动之间的差异微妙且不断协商。非正规城市矿工的技能和沟通实践复杂地嵌入在后工业城市新兴的权力结构中：既是工作环境的必需品，又是维持生计的方式，同时也是超越产生并再生产此类废弃城市环境的秩序的方式。

title: Wind extraction? Gifts, reciprocity, and renewability in Colombia's energy frontier
abstract: This article examines the circulation of gifts that binds dozens of indigenous Wayúu communities and Jemeiwaa Kai, a wind energy corporation that intends to build five wind farms in Colombia's coastal region of La Guajira. Drawing on long‐term fieldwork, I analyze how the intimate, reciprocal, and meaningful social exchanges that take place as part of the gift‐giving practices between Jemeiwaa Kai and Wayúu residents are critical for the renewability of wind energy itself, as they create and maintain the conditions for harnessing this resource without interruption. Since these exchanges acknowledge the power of Wayúu communities hosting future wind farms to disrupt their operations and infrastructures, they enable recipients to carve out a space of accountability by entangling the corporation in long‐term relationships of obligation and negotiating the ethical ways of harnessing wind in Wayúu land. The centrality of gift giving highlights that extraction, as a concept for theorizing wind energy in La Guajira, falls short of fully making sense of the variegated interactions, ethical predicaments, and forms of value production that take place on the ground, between those who have lived alongside the wind for centuries and the outsiders who now aspire to harness its force.
title_zh: 风能开采？哥伦比亚能源前沿的礼物、互惠与可再生性
abstract_zh: 本文探讨了将数十个土著Wayúu社区与Jemeiwaa Kai（一家计划在哥伦比亚拉瓜希拉沿海地区建设五个风电场的风能公司）联系在一起的礼物流通。基于长期的田野调查，我分析了Jemeiwaa Kai与Wayúu居民之间作为礼物馈赠实践一部分的亲密、互惠且有意义的社会交流如何对风能本身的可再生性至关重要，因为它们创造并维持了不间断利用这一资源的条件。由于这些交流承认了未来风电场所在地Wayúu社区有破坏其运营和基础设施的能力，它们使接受者能够通过将公司卷入长期的义务关系并谈判在Wayúu土地上利用风能的道德方式来开辟问责空间。礼物馈赠的中心性突显了“开采”作为理论化拉瓜希拉风能的概念，不足以完全理解当地发生的多样化互动、伦理困境和价值生产形式——那些与风共存了几个世纪的人与现在渴望利用其力量的外来者之间的互动。

title: “We Too Have Blackened Our Hands”: Work, Harm, and Legitimacy in a Delhi Scrap Market
abstract: Abstract The phrase “we too have blackened our hands” was often repeated to me in conversations with shop owners in what I call “Leela Market,” one of India’s largest metal scrap and parts markets, located in Delhi. I consider the refrain of “having blackened one’s hands” in order to highlight the place‐making power of repeated embodied practice and expressive forms and to explore how those who pursue their livelihood in the market invoked a particular quality and world of work to claim rightful presence and legitimacy in the city. This essay ethnographically renders two activities—“breaking a car” and “cleaning gently”—as forms of work that compose the refrain and resound through the landscape of Leela Market. These forms of work hold together various material practices and transactions, heterogeneous communities and experiences, and contested events and histories that are entangled with the transformation of metal discards into scrap and parts. As regulatory interventions challenge the relevance of the market and threaten its place in the city, these forms of work also constitute a basis for engagements with various forms and discourses of harm, pollution, and toxicity.
title_zh: “我们也染黑了手”：德里废品市场中的工作、伤害与合法性
abstract_zh: 摘要“我们也染黑了手”这句话是德里最大的金属废品和零件市场之一的“Leela市场”中，店主们经常对我重复的话。我思考“染黑了手”这一惯用语，以强调重复的具身实践和表达形式在营造地方上的力量，并探讨那些在市场谋生的人如何援引特定的工作性质和工作世界，来主张他们在城市中的正当存在和合法性。本文人种志地呈现了两种活动——“拆解汽车”和“轻柔清洁”——作为构成这一惯用语并在Leela市场景观中回响的工作形式。这些工作形式将各种物质实践与交易、异质社区与经验、以及有争议的事件与历史凝聚在一起，它们都与金属废料转化为废品和零件的过程纠缠在一起。随着监管干预挑战市场的相关性并威胁其在城市中的地位，这些工作形式也成为与各种形式的伤害、污染和毒性进行接触的基础。

title: Bodies, Toxins, and E-Waste Labour Interventions in Ghana: Toward a Toxic Postcolonial Corporality?
abstract: This article explores the lived experience of electronic waste (e-waste) workers in Agbogbloshie, a primary e-waste recycling center and scrap metal market in Accra, Ghana, that has been described by international environmental organizations as one of the most polluted places on Earth. To formulate a more critical and contextual understanding of the lives of these e-waste workers and their embodied toxic experience, the article introduces the concept of "toxic postcolonial corporality", a term deployed to navigate and confront the contentious intersection of bodies, toxins, and "green" recycling interventions in a postcolonial urban scrapyard. After introducing the social, economic, and toxic dimensions of Agbogbloshie, I discuss the problems and politics of permeability in general and the precarious boundaries of bodies, environments, and risk mitigation practices in a postcolonial context in particular. It will be argued that the notion of toxic postcolonial corporality offers a possible critical environmental health perspective that can inform anthropological engagements with the embedded lives navigating the permeable and intersecting worlds of pollution, postcolonization, and decontamination.
title_zh: 身体、毒素与加纳电子垃圾劳动干预：迈向有毒的后殖民身体性？
abstract_zh: 本文探讨了加纳阿克拉Agbogbloshie电子废物（e-waste）工人的生活经验，该地是主要的电子废物回收中心和废金属市场，被国际环境组织描述为地球上污染最严重的地方之一。为了对这些电子废物工人的生活及其具身化的有毒经验形成更批判性和情境化的理解，本文引入了“有毒的后殖民身体性”这一概念，用于导航和面对后殖民城市废品场中身体、毒素与“绿色”回收干预之间的争议性交叉点。在介绍了Agbogbloshie的社会、经济和有毒维度之后，我讨论了渗透性的一般问题与政治，特别是后殖民背景下身体、环境和风险缓解实践的脆弱边界。本文认为，有毒的后殖民身体性概念提供了一种可能的批判性环境健康视角，可以为人类学参与那些在污染、后殖民化和去污的渗透性和交叉世界中航行的嵌入式生活提供信息。
