title: Message in a Bottleneck: Supply Chain Disruptions and Manufacturing Output in the United States
journal_name: GLOBAL NETWORKS-A JOURNAL OF TRANSNATIONAL AFFAIRS
abstract: ABSTRACT We examine the effect of container shipping disruptions on US manufacturing output before and during the Covid‐19 pandemic. We augment maritime trade with a global production network model, where the reliability of container logistics is critical for the on‐time and full availability of inputs and the delivery of output to foreign markets. We combine a US container shipping reliability dataset with input–output and trade data to construct a novel supply chain disruption index that captures the integration of upstream and downstream linkages of the US manufacturing sector into the global supply chain. Our findings suggest that a one‐unit shock leads to a very similar response on output through the upstream (import) and downstream (export) channels. Industries adjust their inventory strategy to cope with supply chain disruptions. Container disruptions affect non‐durable industries through the downstream and durable industries through the upstream linkages. Our study highlights the importance of understanding the drivers of a resilient global supply chain.
title_zh: 瓶颈中的信息：美国供应链中断与制造业产出
abstract_zh: 摘要：我们考察了新冠疫情前后集装箱运输中断对美国制造业产出的影响。我们将海洋贸易与全球生产网络模型相结合，其中集装箱物流的可靠性对于投入的及时和完整可用性以及向国外市场交付产出至关重要。我们将美国集装箱运输可靠性数据集与投入产出和贸易数据相结合，构建了一个新颖的供应链中断指数，该指数捕捉了美国制造业部门上下游联系融入全球供应链的程度。我们的研究结果表明，一个单位的冲击通过上游（进口）和下游（出口）渠道对产出产生非常相似的响应。行业调整其库存策略以应对供应链中断。集装箱中断通过下游渠道影响非耐用品行业，通过上游渠道影响耐用品行业。我们的研究强调了理解全球供应链韧性驱动因素的重要性。

title: Prospecting a Socialist Oil Field
abstract: Abstract Located in China's northeastern frontier, the Daqing Oil Field was built at the height of socialist revolutionary fervor. This article approaches Daqing's extractive zone as a mediated space that hosts geotechnical encounters between humans, geomatter, and machine. To understand oil drilling as eventful mediation, a few anecdotes are first recounted to reenact Maoist contradiction as geotechnical contradiction — that is, conduct celebrated as embodying the Maoist spirit is revealed to be a result of first-order geotechnical mediation. The article then examines prospecting as a question of visuality, whereby oil workers’ skyward vision in propaganda posters is reoriented to become earthbound gazes whose fixation on data collection and whose receptiveness to energy flows suggest an alternative model of subject formation. The conclusion draws attention to underground fissures — the micro-openings in rock layers in which oil is stored — and considers them a site of non-knowledge from which the possibility of earthbound thinking emerges.
title_zh: 勘探社会主义油田
abstract_zh: 位于中国东北边境的大庆油田是在社会主义革命热情高涨时期建成的。本文将大庆的采矿区视为一个中介空间，承载着人类、地质物质和机器之间的岩土技术遭遇。为了将石油钻探理解为事件性中介，首先讲述一些轶事，重新演绎毛泽东式矛盾作为岩土技术矛盾——即作为体现毛泽东精神的行为被揭示为第一性岩土技术中介的结果。然后，文章考察勘探作为视觉性问题，其中宣传画中石油工人仰望天空的视线被重新定向为向下的凝视，这种凝视专注于数据收集并对能量流动保持开放，暗示了一种主体形成的替代模式。结论部分关注地下裂缝——储油岩层中的微小开口——并将其视为非知识的场所，从中产生了地球思维的可能性。

title: Redivisions of Work: Manufacturing Labor and Training in Switzerland's Knowledge Economy
abstract: ABSTRACT The promise of knowledge society is clean, creative, and expressive work. Technological advancements would relieve humans from the tedium and hardship of labor, and access to knowledge and expansion of higher education would diminish the existing social inequalities of industrial society. Based on ethnographic fieldwork in Switzerland's mechanical and electrical engineering industry, this article illustrates how the work experiences of apprentices challenge the image of labor in a knowledge society ostensibly freed from all forms of material, technological, and social constraint. I demonstrate that the persistence of the tedium and potential danger of industrial work, of organizational hierarchies, the decreasing social validation of mechanical and manual labor, and expectations and aspirations to singularity make youth increasingly interested in other kinds of employment and training. The article takes the work and learning relations in the Swiss mechanical and electrical engineering sector as a symptom of emerging tensions around the division of labor and valorization of different forms of skills, and the meaning and motivations of work in late capitalism. I argue that future anthropological studies of work and education in de‐industrialized settings might do well to examine the social critique of industrial work in concert with its aesthetic critique.
title_zh: 工作的再分工：瑞士知识经济中的制造业劳动与培训
abstract_zh: 摘要 知识社会的承诺是清洁、创造性和表达性的工作。技术进步将使人类摆脱劳动的乏味和艰辛，知识的普及和高等教育的扩展将减少工业社会现有的社会不平等。基于在瑞士机械和电气工程行业的民族志田野调查，本文展示了学徒的工作经历如何挑战了知识社会中看似摆脱了所有物质、技术和社会约束的劳动形象。我论证了工业工作中乏味和潜在危险的持续存在、组织等级制度、机械和手工劳动社会认可度的降低，以及对独特性的期望和抱负，使得年轻人对其他类型的就业和培训越来越感兴趣。本文以瑞士机械和电气工程部门的工作和学习关系作为新兴紧张关系的征兆，这些紧张围绕劳动分工、不同技能形式的估价，以及晚期资本主义中工作的意义和动机。我认为，未来在去工业化环境中的工作和教育的人类学研究，或许最好将工业劳动的社会批判与其审美批判结合起来考察。

title: Renovating the Cosmos and Overturning the Upside-Down: The Ontological Stakes of Bolivia’s Lithium Economy
abstract: With reference to Bolivia’s lithium economy, this article addresses a peculiar paradox: How can so many individuals within the industry persist to pledge loyalty to industrializing lithium while at the same time expressing deep frustration with the Morales-Linera regime’s industrialization project? I claim that this contradiction is the result of the complex way lithium development has interacted with the country’ s so-called democratic and cultural revolution. I reveal that the regime has utilized the lithium project as an insurgent tool to consolidate state power in a context where socialist transformation has been conceptualized as a struggle for hegemony. In this setting, the regime validated lithium development by advancing a secular version of the vivir bien paradigm. This provoked ambivalent sentiments among the workers within the lithium industry. Since local actors are able to penetrate hegemonic state discourse with their own ontological stakes, socialist hegemony is not entirely secured in Bolivia.
title_zh: 革新宇宙与颠覆颠倒：玻利维亚锂经济的存在论赌注
abstract_zh: 本文以玻利维亚的锂经济为背景，探讨了一个特殊的悖论：为什么行业内如此多的个人坚持效忠于锂的工业化，同时却对莫拉莱斯-利内拉政权的工业化项目表达深切沮丧？我认为，这种矛盾是锂发展与该国所谓的民主和文化革命复杂互动的结果。我揭示了该政权利用锂项目作为造反工具来巩固国家权力，在社会主义转型被概念化为霸权斗争的背景下。在此情境中，政权通过推进世俗版的“美好生活”范式来验证锂发展，这引发了锂行业内工人的矛盾情绪。由于地方行为者能够通过自己的存在论赌注渗透霸权国家话语，玻利维亚的社会主义霸权并未完全确立。

title: Riesgo, autoatención y autocuidado en la economía de plataforma
abstract: This article analyzes the knowledge and practices of self-care and self-care embodied by Latin American immigrants in the context of their experiences as home-deliverers of food for digital platforms in the context of Catalonia (Spain). For this purpose, a multisite ethnography is carried out in which various data collection techniques are used in the course of the fieldwork: in-depth interviews, participant observation and non-participant observation. The ethnographic work shows that the implementation of knowledge and self-care practices centered on the use of protective instruments (helmet, gloves and others) is fundamentally related to two factors: the type of vehicle that the delivery drivers use when making the deliveries and the climatic conditions in which they must work. The latter conditions, when extreme (as in the case of high temperatures) become another factor that drives riders to mobilize other knowledge and self-care practices. Finally, it should be noted that when, as a result of their work activity, delivery drivers suffered from discomfort, afflictions, illnesses and/or accidents, they resorted to self-care knowledge and practices to alleviate, control and/or overcome the health problem that afflicted them. In this sense, it is in solitude and/or in the family context (local or transnational) of the riders where they most frequently make diagnoses and carry out practices of self-care and healing of their ailments.
title_zh: 平台经济中的风险、自我关注与自我照护
abstract_zh: 本文分析了在加泰罗尼亚（西班牙）背景下，拉丁美洲移民作为数字平台送餐员的经历中所体现的自我关注和自我照护的知识与实践。为此，我们进行了一项多地点民族志研究，在实地工作中采用了多种数据收集技术：深度访谈、参与式观察和非参与式观察。民族志工作表明，以使用防护用具（头盔、手套等）为中心的自我关注和照护知识与实践的实施，主要与两个因素有关：配送员送货时使用的交通工具类型以及他们必须工作的气候条件。当气候条件极端（如高温）时，会成为促使骑手调动其他自我关注和照护知识与实践的又一因素。最后，值得注意的是，当配送员因工作活动而遭受不适、病痛、疾病和/或事故时，他们会求助于自我关注和照护的知识与实践来缓解、控制和/或克服困扰他们的健康问题。从这个意义上说，骑手们最常在孤独和/或家庭背景（本地或跨国）下进行诊断并实施自我照护和疗愈实践。

title: The Energy Equicrat: Neoliberal Subjectivity “After” Neoliberalism
abstract: ABSTRACT: Many theorists and pundits contend that neoliberalism is on the “decline,” citing shifts in political opinions and policies. I argue that these analyses overstate this decline by rendering neoliberalism as a circumscribed ideology that subjects knowingly embrace or repudiate. As a corrective, this article argues that we must apprehend neoliberalism not simply in terms of “political will” or the “war of ideas,” but also as a spatialized, habituated, and affective phenomenon that exceeds any conscious ideological agenda. Toward this end, I explore neoliberal efforts to equitably decarbonize energy infrastructure. Drawing from two years of ethnographic research on sustainable energy development in New York City, I contend that subjects who consciously repudiate neoliberal governance often unwittingly reproduce it through their day-to-day practices—even when they posit those practices in opposition to neoliberal governance. I attribute this unwitting work to the spatiality and materiality of solar infrastructure and energy efficiency upgrades. Specifically, I suggest that the decentralized landscape of sustainable energy enfolds both grassroots activists and leftist technocrats into the workings of neoliberal markets in spite of their conscious opposition to market logics. This distributed spatiality also broadens the range of subjects who participate in electricity governance, diluting the normative ideological poles that have traditionally divided these subjects, as the technocrat and the activist, the corporate worker and the anti-capitalist, coalesce through infrastructural transformation. I conceptualize this boundary-blurring subjectivity as the equicrat, short for the equity-minded technocrat, to call attention to the counterintuitive compatibility of equitable, grassroots governance and rule by experts in the neoliberal landscape. In theorizing this compatibility, the equicrat heuristic illuminates the performative terrain through which subjects at once reject and reproduce neoliberalism.
title_zh: 能源平等主义技术官僚：新自由主义主体性在“新自由主义之后”
abstract_zh: 摘要：许多理论家和评论家认为新自由主义正在“衰落”，引用政治观点和政策的变化。我认为这些分析夸大了这种衰落，将新自由主义视为一种被限制的意识形态，主体有意识地接受或拒绝它。作为修正，本文认为我们必须理解新自由主义，不仅仅是“政治意愿”或“思想之战”，而且是一种空间化、习惯化和情感化的现象，超越了任何有意识的意识形态议程。为此，我探讨了新自由主义努力公平地脱碳能源基础设施。借鉴在纽约市可持续能源发展方面两年的民族志研究，我认为那些有意识地拒绝新自由主义治理的主体往往通过他们的日常实践无意中复制了它——即使他们将那些实践置于新自由主义治理的对立面。我将这种无意识的工作归因于太阳能基础设施和能效升级的空间性和物质性。具体来说，我认为可持续能源的分散景观将草根活动家和左翼技术官僚都纳入新自由主义市场的运作中，尽管他们有意识地反对市场逻辑。这种分布式空间性也扩展了参与电力治理的主体范围，淡化了传统上分裂这些主体的规范性意识形态两极，因为技术官僚和活动家、企业工作者和反资本主义者通过基础设施转型而融合。我将这种模糊边界的主题概念化为“平等主义技术官僚”，简称公平-minded技术官僚，以引起对公平、草根治理与专家统治在新自由主义景观中反直觉的兼容性的关注。通过理论化这种兼容性，平等主义技术官僚启发式阐明了主体同时拒绝和复制新自由主义的表演性领域。

title: The Invisible Risks of Extractive Infrastructure Networks and Mining
abstract: Abstract This article uses Actor‐Network Theory to analyze mining infrastructures in Chile and develop a concept of “extractive infrastructure networks.” Focusing on the port of Punta Chungo and its connection to the Los Pelambres mine, we explore how these infrastructures, along with human and non‐human actors, create networks that sustain the extractivist economy while hiding environmental and social risks. Through a photographic essay, we show how these infrastructures are both visible and forgotten in everyday life, and how they often hide the long‐term dangers they pose to nearby communities. This paper introduces a new way to understand the complex relationships between infrastructure, environment, and society in Chile's mining industry.
title_zh: 采掘基础设施网络与采矿的隐性风险
abstract_zh: 本文运用行动者网络理论分析智利的采矿基础设施，并提出了“采掘基础设施网络”的概念。通过聚焦蓬塔琼戈港及其与洛斯佩兰布雷斯矿的连接，我们探讨了这些基础设施如何与人类及非人类行动者共同构建网络，在维持采掘主义经济的同时隐藏环境与社会风险。通过摄影散文的方式，我们展示了这些基础设施如何在日常生活中既可见又被遗忘，以及它们如何常常掩盖对附近社区构成的长期危险。本文提出了一种理解智利矿业中基础设施、环境与社会之间复杂关系的新方式。

title: Toxic Waste, Worried Communities: Building an Archaeology of Concern
abstract: Every year, the devastating effects of anthropogenic climate change become clearer, and every year, humanity's socioeconomic practices produce more devastation. What is the role of archaeology in the face of this environmental transformation? As a discipline that specializes in teasing out the contours of human-environment relations across different tempos, archaeology is indispensable for putting our current crises in long-term context. In this short piece, I would like to make a different argument. The role of archaeology is not simply to provide deep context for human-environment interaction but rather to serve as a method for investigating the hidden histories of anthropogenic sediments in the present. Beyond revealing the historical trajectories of persistent and latent waste, this approach suggests archaeology as a collaborative practice that articulates everyday community concerns with broader social logics for the purpose of building broader coalitions. We are living through what Gabriel Hecht (2018) calls “the apotheosis of waste.” Globally distributed projects like industrial capitalism, imperialism, and settler colonialism touch down in particular places to remake them for their own purposes. As these projects terraform landscapes and leave behind piles of decaying waste, they transform how environments and the societies that rely upon them reproduce themselves. These transformations have different effects and legibilities (Murphy 2013). Certain ecologies are at greater risk, and certain communities are more vulnerable to the transformation they produce. Some forms of anthropogenic persistence are ostentatiously devastating. There is no mistaking the long-term threat of a clear-cut forest for a community that relies on forests for hunting. For the most part, the effects of these transformations are latent and creeping. Heavy metals leach out of tailings (the waste material left behind from mining operations) into drinking water. Pesticides bioaccumulate across food chains. Radiating out from the ignored side of these global projects, the toxic effects of these transformations are often slow, hidden, and hard to comprehend (Nixon 2011). What does this have to do with archaeology? Our contemporary crisis is a problem of hidden pasts and their resonating effects. Archaeology is the study of latent anthropogenic objects, their histories, and their persistent effects. It would be a mistake to locate this crisis simply in the materialist realm of ecology and economics. It would also be a mistake to undo all the work that archaeology has done to become more collaborative with communities on the ground (Atalay 2006; McAnany and Rowe 2015) in the name of a global environmental crisis. That would be precisely the kind of reactionary response to “crisis” that Joe Masco (2017) and Sandy Hunter (this forum) warn about. Instead of a singular shared crisis, there are myriad communities whose existence is entangled with local environments that are negotiating destabilizing and hidden forces. This is not to deny that there are global logics which organize these forces, but the environmental transformations that are taking place across the globe must first be understood in the context of the communities who live among them, the myriad sedimented histories that these transformations emerge out of, and the forms of situated knowing and unknowing by which these transformations are made meaningful. Knowledge and meaning are interwoven into place (Basso 1996; Casey 2013). If environments are integral to the way a community remembers its history, organizes its present, and prepares for its future, then shifting environments and latent harms represent an existential challenge to the way a community reproduces, navigates, and knows its world. Local ways of knowing are not simply a source of vulnerability; they are also at the core of the communal capacity to understand and navigate these transformations. Place-based knowledge, developed over generations/millennia, is an essential medium for noticing the often-subtle transformations that define anthropogenic climate change. As environments shift, as locales of food and knowledge are disrupted, communities become concerned. By concern, I mean the affective response of a community to the subtle phenomena of a changing environment (Puig de la Bellacassa 2010; Latour 2008). Concerns are the unsettling feeling that emerges alongside destabilized riverbanks, denuded forests, and unexplainable health problems among the caribou herd that a community uses to feed itself. Concerns are less coherent than interests, the phenomena they emerge out of are “troubled and unsettled” and not clearly legible in a way that might clearly reveal harms and benefits (Puig de la Bellacassa 2010). Concerns do not represent a pure and immediate form of knowledge that locals have and scientists lack. Indeed, the ambiguity and uncanny nature of these phenomena make them prone to inaccurate interpretations or even conspiracy theories. At the same time, concerns develop around emergent phenomena whose effects are diffuse and whose histories are globally entangled. A declining caribou herd has the capacity to mobilize concerns across different communities and ways of knowing (state environmentalists and Indigenous hunters), even while producing very different concerns with very different stakes. Maria Puig de la Bellacassa (2010) argues that while interests are often zero-sum and lead to conflictual relationships, concerns are more open-ended and better at articulating care across difference. One community's concern does not just circulate internally but is oriented toward a possible future where these concerns can be alleviated, and toward a coalition of other parties that can collaborate on alleviating it. Community concerns about changing environments serve as collaborative openings for archaeologists to mobilize their methods in a way that is useful to the community but also extends beyond local interest. In the face of community concerns, archaeology can both translate and unearth. In some cases, archaeological research can make legible things that are already known by the community, yet in a way that can bring other groups to action (Liboiron 2021). This is best represented by Emma Gilheany's (this forum) work with the Inuit in Labrador. In this case, the Inuit knew there was persistent waste left behind by a military installation that was leaching harmful toxins into the soil and making people sick, but the government claimed the site had already been remediated. Using an archaeological survey to prove that this remediation was a lie, Emma's work translated the Inuit community's concerns into a register that was legible to the government. In other cases, locals have little understanding of the causes of the unsettling environmental phenomena they encounter. Here, the archaeologist can use their methods of historical reconstruction to investigate the anthropogenic residues that led to these environmental transformations and the historical causes that led to these sedimented residues. In my own research on Mill Creek Ravine Park in Edmonton, Alberta, local community members, mostly residents of a middle-class neighborhood, became concerned about the water quality of the creek in a beloved city park. These concerns emerged as much around a citizen science water monitoring project that identified the creek as having the most polluted water of any urban creek in the province of Alberta as they did around informal encounters locals had with disturbing phenomena in the creek: frothy water, river weeds turned pink, and sick pets. While water testing revealed what pollutants were present, I turned to archaeology to uncover the history behind the pollution. In performing an archaeological survey and excavation of Mill Creek Ravine, I uncovered piles of hidden coal mining and meatpacking waste that had sedimented into the ravine a century earlier and continued to leach heavy metals (Stewart, Jungkind and Losey 2020; Stewart 2022). As this research uncovered and mapped sedimented waste, it also revealed the historical connection between ongoing pollution and local histories of coal mining and meatpacking. And while these sedimented histories were local, their histories were entangled with the much broader projects of settler colonialism and industrial capitalism in Western Canada. The same industrial logic that disposed the waste into the ravine for a decade was implicated in the colonial appropriation of the ravine from the Papaschase Cree, the uneven exposure of impoverished farmers during the Great Depression, and the contemporary exposure of homeless populations. The persistence of century-old waste and its effects resonated far beyond the contemporary middle-class concerns that had first brought it to my attention. Instead of limiting the ethico-political frame of this research simply to the community I started with, these concerns opened the entangled histories of unevenly distributed harms, exploitation, and colonial appropriation. My research showed how mapping these pollutants in the present and building a politics to mitigate their harms first required understanding the broader histories that served as their conditions of possibility. This research revealed the myriad other communities across time and space whose lives were impacted by the changing environment of Mill Creek Ravine. In revealing these histories, the research not only facilitated a more robust understanding of the stakes of the persistent past but also revealed overlapping concerns across different communities both in the present and past. An archaeology of concern is a way that archaeological methods can be used to attend to environmental anxieties within a local community by historicizing unsettling environmental phenomena. By mapping environmental transformations within a broader historical context, archaeology can reveal how concerns articulate with other concerns and begin the process of linking coalitions of concerned communities across time and space.
title_zh: 有毒废物与忧虑的社区：构建一种关切的考古学
abstract_zh: 每年，人类引起的气候变化的破坏性影响愈发明显，而人类的社会经济实践也在造成更多的破坏。在面对这种环境转型时，考古学的作用是什么？作为一门专门研究不同时间尺度下人类与环境关系轮廓的学科，考古学对于将我们当前的危机置于长期背景中是不可或缺的。在这篇短文中，我想提出一个不同的论点。考古学的作用不仅仅是提供人类与环境相互作用的深层背景，而是作为一种研究当下人类沉积物隐藏历史的方法。除了揭示持久和潜在废物的历史轨迹外，这种方法将考古学视为一种协作实践，将日常社区关切与更广泛的社会逻辑联系起来，以建立更广泛的联盟。我们正生活在加布里埃尔·赫克特（2018）所说的“废物的巅峰”时代。像工业资本主义、帝国主义和定居者殖民主义这样的全球性项目在特定地点落地，为了自身目的重塑它们。随着这些项目改造地貌并留下堆积如山的腐烂废物，它们改变了环境以及依赖这些环境的社会自我再生产的方式。这些转变具有不同的影响和可读性（Murphy 2013）。某些生态系统面临更大风险，某些社区更容易受到这些转变的影响。某些人类活动的持久性是显而易见的灾难性。对一个依赖森林狩猎的社区来说，森林被砍伐的长期威胁是毋庸置疑的。但在大多数情况下，这些转变的影响是潜伏而缓慢的。重金属从尾矿（采矿作业留下的废料）中浸出进入饮用水。杀虫剂在食物链中生物累积。从这些全球项目中被忽视的一面辐射出来，这些转变的毒性影响往往是缓慢的、隐藏的且难以理解的（Nixon 2011）。这与考古学有什么关系？我们当代的危机是一个隐藏的过去及其回响效应的问题。考古学是对潜伏的人造物体、它们的历史及其持久影响的研究。将这场危机仅仅定位在生态和经济的唯物主义领域将是一个错误。以全球环境危机的名义，否定考古学为实现与地方社区更加协作所做的一切工作（Atalay 2006; McAnany and Rowe 2015）也将是一个错误。那正是乔·马斯科（2017）和桑迪·亨特（本论坛）所警告的那种对“危机”的反应性回应。与其说是单一的共同危机，不如说是无数的社区，其生存与当地环境纠缠在一起，正在应对不稳定的隐藏力量。这并不是否认存在组织这些力量的全球逻辑，但全球范围内发生的环境转型必须首先从生活其中的社区、这些转型从中产生的无数沉积历史，以及使这些转型有意义的各种情境化认识和不认识的形式来理解。知识和意义与地方交织在一起（Basso 1996; Casey 2013）。如果环境是社区记忆历史、组织现在和准备未来的组成部分，那么环境变化和潜在伤害就对社区再生产、导航和认识其世界的方式构成了存在性挑战。地方性的认识方式不仅仅是脆弱性的来源；它们也是社区理解和应对这些转型的核心能力。经过几代/几千年发展起来的地方性知识，是注意到定义人类引起的气候变化的往往是微妙转变的重要媒介。随着环境变化，食物和知识的场所被破坏，社区变得忧虑。通过忧虑，我指的是社区对变化环境中微妙现象的情感反应（Puig de la Bellacassa 2010; Latour 2008）。忧虑是不安的感觉，伴随着不稳定的河岸、光秃的森林以及社区赖以生存的驯鹿群中无法解释的健康问题而出现。忧虑比利益更不连贯，它们从中产生的现象是“麻烦而动荡的”，并且不容易以一种能清楚揭示伤害和利益的方式被解读（Puig de la Bellacassa 2010）。忧虑并不代表当地人拥有而科学家缺乏的纯粹而直接的知识形式。事实上，这些现象的模糊性和离奇性使它们容易受到不准确的解释甚至阴谋论的影响。同时，忧虑围绕着新兴现象发展，这些现象的影响是分散的，其历史是全球纠缠的。一个衰退的驯鹿群有能力在不同社区和认识方式（国家环保主义者和土著猎人）中动员忧虑，即使产生非常不同且具有非常不同利害关系的忧虑。玛丽亚·普伊赫·德拉贝拉卡萨（2010）认为，虽然利益通常是零和的，并导致冲突关系，但忧虑是更加开放的，并且更善于在不同群体之间表达关怀。一个社区的忧虑不仅在其内部循环，而且指向一个可能的未来，在这些未来中这些忧虑可以得到缓解，并指向一个可以合作缓解它的其他方的联盟。社区对变化环境的忧虑为考古学家提供了一个协作的开放空间，使他们能够以对社区有用但超越地方利益的方式动员他们的方法。面对社区忧虑，考古学既能翻译也能发掘。在某些情况下，考古研究可以使社区已经知道的东西变得可读，但以一种可以促使其他群体采取行动的方式（Liboiron 2021）。这最好地体现在艾玛·吉尔希尼（本论坛）与拉布拉多因纽特人的合作中。在这个案例中，因纽特人知道军事设施留下的持久废物正在将有害毒素浸入土壤并使人患病，但政府声称该地点已被修复。通过考古调查证明修复是谎言，艾玛的工作将因纽特社区的忧虑转化为政府可读的登记形式。在其他情况下，当地人对他们遇到的令人不安的环境现象的原因知之甚少。在这里，考古学家可以使用他们的历史重建方法，调查导致这些环境转变的人造残留物以及导致这些沉积残留物的历史原因。在我自己对埃德蒙顿米尔克里克峡谷公园的研究中，当地社区居民——主要是中产阶级社区的居民——开始担心一个深受喜爱的城市公园中溪流的水质。这些忧虑既来自于一个公民科学水质监测项目，该项目确定该小溪是阿尔伯塔省所有城市小溪中污染最严重的，也来自于当地人在小溪中遇到令人不安现象的非正式遭遇：泡沫状的水、变成粉红色的水草以及生病的宠物。虽然水质检测揭示了存在哪些污染物，我转而求助于考古学来揭示污染背后的历史。通过对米尔克里克峡谷进行考古调查和发掘，我发现了一个世纪前沉积在峡谷中并继续浸出重金属的隐藏煤矿和肉类加工废物堆（Stewart, Jungkind and Losey 2020; Stewart 2022）。这项研究在揭示和绘制沉积废物地图的同时，也揭示了持续污染与当地煤矿和肉类加工历史之间的历史联系。虽然这些沉积的历史是地方性的，但它们的历史与加拿大西部更广泛的定居者殖民主义和工业资本主义项目纠缠在一起。将废物倾倒进峡谷十年的同一工业逻辑，也涉及从帕帕塞克里族手中殖民侵占峡谷、大萧条期间贫困农民的不平等暴露以及当代无家可归人口的暴露。百年废物的持久性及其影响远远超出了最初引起我注意的当代中产阶级忧虑。这项研究将伦理政治框架局限于我开始的社区，而是打开了不平等的损害分配、剥削和殖民侵占的纠缠历史。我的研究显示，要在当下绘制这些污染物的图景并建立政治机制以减轻其危害，首先需要理解作为其可能性条件的更广泛历史。这项研究揭示了无数其他时空的社区，他们的生活受到米尔克里克峡谷环境变化的影响。通过揭示这些历史，这项研究不仅促进了对持久过去利害关系的更深入理解，也揭示了当下和过去不同社区之间重叠的忧虑。一种关切的考古学是考古方法用于关注地方社区内环境焦虑的一种方式，通过将令人不安的环境现象历史化。通过将环境转型置于更广泛的历史背景中绘制地图，考古学可以揭示忧虑如何与其他忧虑相互关联，并开始连接跨越时空的忧虑社区联盟。

title: Using multi-methods in archaeology: Circulatory infrastructure, cybernetics and 19th-century communication technologies in Australia
abstract: The Overland Telegraph system linked Australia to nascent global information and communication networks. Its arrival marked a key milestone in what we call Australia’s ‘telegraph time’—a fifty-year period from 1854–1904 when telegraphic systems were a significant driver of changes in economic, political and cultural activities. This British colonial infrastructure also marked the beginnings of the displacement of First Nations people along the route. In this paper, we explore how a multi-method and cybernetic, or complex systems, approach to the study of large-scale systems like telegraphy can make these histories and heritage more legible and meaningful today. We combine industrial, historical and indigenous archaeologies, systems engineering, cultural anthropology, photography, and critical theory to research the Overland Telegraph Line (OTL) and, in so doing, better reveal the socio-technical scale and impact of the OTL as a circulatory infrastructure. Our multi-disciplinary study of the ‘flows’ of the OTL—the material, the archival, the decommissioning, the repurposing, and the corridors of connection that remain—make visible its workings and highlight its enduring impacts. This multi-methods approach case study provides a model for archaeology generally, but especially the archaeology of linear features, such as pathways, journeyscapes, Songlines and linear infrastructure.
title_zh: 在考古学中使用多种方法：澳大利亚的循环基础设施、控制论与19世纪通信技术
abstract_zh: 陆上电报系统将澳大利亚与新兴的全球信息和通信网络连接起来。它的到来标志着我们称之为澳大利亚“电报时代”的一个关键里程碑——从1854年到1904年的五十年间，电报系统成为经济、政治和文化活动变革的重要驱动力。这一英国殖民基础设施也标志着沿线原住民流离失所的开始。在本文中，我们探讨了如何使用多方法及控制论（或复杂系统）的方法来研究像电报这样的大型系统，使这些历史和遗产在今天更具可读性和意义。我们结合了工业考古学、历史考古学和土著考古学、系统工程、文化人类学、摄影和批判理论来研究陆上电报线路（OTL），从而更好地揭示OTL作为循环基础设施的社会技术规模和影响。我们对OTL的“流动”——物质、档案、退役、重新利用以及仍然存在的连接走廊——的多学科研究，使其运作可见并突显其持久影响。这种多方法案例研究为一般考古学，尤其是线性特征（如小径、旅程景观、歌谣线和线性基础设施）的考古学提供了模型。

title: Waste Donations
abstract: In Istanbul, shopkeepers frequently dispose of their paper and plastic waste by giving it to select migrant waste pickers. This article examines these waste donations as a novel form of hospitable giving in Turkey, a country that has hosted millions of irregular migrants and asylum seekers since 2011. By analyzing the mutual obligations these donations create and the diverse ways that shopkeepers justify helping migrants, the article argues that waste donations occur primarily when they enable shopkeepers to reproduce their moral authority over migrant waste pickers. In doing so, it explores two related issues: the consequences of the state’s retreat from providing universal welfare opportunities to irregular migrants; and the embedding of migrant hospitality within service relations in a precarious urban economy. The article concludes by rethinking informal waste labor and host-guest dynamics through the lens of dependent relations. ÖZET İstanbul’daki esnaflar, kâğıt ve plastik atıkları sıklıkla kendi seçtikleri yabancı kâğıt toplayıcılarına vererek bertaraf etmektedirler. Bu makale, 2011’den beri milyonlarca düzensiz mülteci ve sığınmacıya ev sahipliği yapan Türkiye’de, bu tür atık bağışlarını misafirperverliğin yeni bir şekli olarak incelemektedir. Atık bağışlarının yol açtığı karşılıklı yükümlülükleri ve esnafın yabancılara yardım etmeyi meşrulaştırma yolları analiz edilerek, bu tür bağışların öncelikle esnafın yabancı atık toplayıcıları üzerinde ahlaki otoritesini sağlayabildiği durumlarda gerçekleştiği ileri sürülmektedir. Bu doğrultuda, iki bağlantılı konu incelenmektedir: devletin düzensiz göçmenlere evrensel sosyal koruma sağlamaktan çekilmesinin sonuçları; ve hiçbir güvencesi olmayan sokak ekonomisinde faaliyet gösteren atık toplayıcılarıyla esnaf arasındaki misafirperverliğe dayalı hizmet ilişkilerinin doğurduğu etkiler. Makale, enformel atık işçiliği ve ev sahibi–misafir dinamiklerini, bağımlılık ilişkileri merceğinden yeniden gözleyerek sonuçlanmaktadır.
title_zh: 废物捐赠
abstract_zh: 在伊斯坦布尔，店主经常将他们的纸和塑料废物送给选定的移民拾荒者。本文将这些废物捐赠视为土耳其自2011年以来接纳数百万非正规移民和寻求庇护者的一种新型好客捐赠。通过分析这些捐赠产生的相互义务以及店主证明帮助移民合理化的多种方式，文章认为废物捐赠主要发生在它们能使店主维持对移民拾荒者的道德权威时。在此过程中，文章探讨了两个相关问题：国家退出为非正规移民提供普遍福利机会的后果；以及在脆弱的城市经济中，移民好客如何嵌入服务关系。文章最后通过依赖关系的视角重新思考非正规废物劳动和主客动态。

title: Cannibalistic exchanges with mountain‐ancestors: Moral economies of gold mining in northern Peru

authors.name: Ana Mariella Bacigalupo
institutions: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

journal_name: Journal of Latin American and Caribbean Anthropology
abstract: Abstract Campesinos (peasants) and norteños (northerner entrepreneurs) in highland Huamachuco, la Libertad, northern Peru—reconcile their mining within Andean practices about the perceived sentience and agency of mountain‐ancestors ( apus ). They do so by engaging in two different types of apu cannibalism that are antithetical to each other. I analyze how the conflict between Andean campesino communities who practice small‐scale underground mining on the apu El Toro site, and, the Summa Gold open‐pit mining company (owned by former campesinos now norteño) also on apu El Toro, reshapes, on both sides, relationalities with mountain‐ancestors and capitalism. I explore miners’ practical moral economies with apus , the local government, and legal authorities to secure economic and political benefits as their worlds are transformed by capitalism. I also analyze how the power inequality between campesino and norteño miners shapes these exchanges, their ability to control the limits of extractivism, and the rhetoric around mining contamination.
title_zh: 与山祖的互食交换：秘鲁北部金矿开采的道德经济
abstract_zh: 摘要 秘鲁北部拉利伯塔德省瓦马丘科高地的农民和北方企业家——将他们的小规模采矿与安第斯山脉关于山祖（apus）被认为有感知和能动性的实践相调和。他们通过参与两种截然不同的山祖食人行为来实现这一点。我分析了在埃尔托罗山从事地下小规模采矿的安第斯农民社区与也在埃尔托罗山的苏马黄金露天采矿公司（由前农民转为北方企业家所有）之间的冲突如何重塑双方与山祖和资本主义的关系。我探讨了矿工与山祖、地方政府和法律当局之间的实用道德经济，以在其世界被资本主义转变时确保经济和政治利益。我还分析了农民和北方企业家矿工之间的权力不平等如何塑造这些交换、他们对控制采掘主义极限的能力以及关于采矿污染的言论。

title: Cult, cosmos, and craft at a Thai art academy
abstract: ‘Cult, cosmos, and craft at a Thai art academy’ is part of a collective experiment in digital composition published within this double special issue of TAJA. Our aim has been to ignite and enable novel forms of social analysis. We invited contributors to creatively rethink the form of the academic article with us and built a custom-designed website to host the results. All original research contributions in this collection are made up of two parts: a digital article and its author/s' exegetical commentary. They have been peer reviewed as a pair. (See our introduction, ‘Epistemic attunements: Experiments in intermedial anthropology’, for an extended discussion of the rationale behind this adventure in ‘off-grid’ scholarship and why the digital article on the Curatorium website is not available as a pdf.) Access the digital article here: https://curatorium.au/taja-journal/form-content/cult-cosmos-craft. Or by clicking the link in this note.1 Read the authors' commentary below. [To experience Curatorium as intended please ensure the following browsers are used: Chrome version 121.0.6167.139 or later OR Safari version 16.6.1 or later.] We should begin by saying what has led us to compose our multimedia web article on khrop khru (‘covered by the guru’), an annual rite in Thailand's craft and vocational academies. Kirin Narayan and Ken George have been pursuing an ethnographic and historical study of Vishwakarma worship in India and beyond since 2017 and teamed up that year with Anthony Lovenheim Irwin—a specialist on Theravada Buddhism and material culture—to lead research into Thailand, where the Hindu-Buddhist deity Vishwakarma is known as Phra Witsanukam. No matter where research has taken us, Vishwakarma is celebrated as the patron deity of artisans, technicians, architects, engineers, and others whose livelihood relies on tools, machines, and fabrication—like the graduates of Thailand's vocational academies. Beyond its obvious relevance to regional studies, the broader aim of our ethnographic and comparative work on Vishwakarma worship has been to recuperate the role of technē and material culture in lived religion and lived cosmology. Our multimedia article, ‘Cult, cosmos, and craft at a Thai art academy’, is in keeping with that aim. For the purposes of this special issue of TAJA on ‘Epistemic attunements’, we also have taken steps to align and shape the article's collaborative design process with the cosmo-technical dispositions of Phra Witsanukam's devotees. In contrast to more-than-human approaches in multispecies ethnography, environmental anthropology, sensory ethnography, and affect theory—where ‘attunement’ has gained such methodological and analytic traction—we attune to the numinous, the luminous, the machine, and the tool, and the way devotees dwell, and indeed, attune with them and with each other. For this reason, in this essay, we have been drawn especially to the haptic core of khrop khru, in which a master teacher and devotee of Phra Witsanukam uses their hands to cover and guide the working hand and tool of a student artisan in fashioning an object or image. That ritual gesture is an occasion in which the ‘covering’ presence of Phra Witsanukam is immanent in the substance, surface, design, and touch of crafted objects and craft activity. Here, the act of making an image or other objects visibly aligns the world and cosmos. Working in the extended world of Vishwakarma and his followers has shown us that one of the ways people attune to the divine is through acts of crafting, construction, and artmaking. Khrop khru ritual puts focus on hand-based fabrication in a variety of forms and gives rise to a socio- and cosmo-technological assemblage we call ‘khrop khru society’. Participation in khrop khru ritual, which serves as initiation into that society, attunes new students to the divine, their teachers, the tools of their respective trades, and to their fellow initiates—creating cosmo-social networks and presenting specific ways of learning and being in the world. The three of us (Irwin, George and Narayan) were inducted into khrop khru society in ceremonies held at Rajamangala University of Technology, Lanna (Techno Chiang Mai) in late July 2019. We do not say so in order to claim privileged understanding of or full absorption into a ‘native's point of view’, but rather, to wed and attune khrop khru's cosmo-technical assemblage with the digital platform affordances and design processes that have gone into this article. We hope we have grounded our understanding of khrop khru by cultivating a receptivity to the haptic core of the rite from the time of our fieldwork through the writing-and-design collaboration of our article. That said, our understanding of khrop khru hardly derives from our receptivity to that core alone; we are not attempting a physiognomic reading of core craft objects to reveal the rite's mysteries and reach (cf. Ginzburg 1989, 33–36). Rather, we have come to know the workings of khrop khru, and have cultivated our sensibilities to its textures, through conversations, interviews, photographs, and performances made in the company of Phra Witsanukam's Thai devotees. Our goal for our contribution to the ‘Epistemic attunements’ curation was to convey to the reader-viewer the haptic, social, and aesthetic aspects of khrop khru ritual by using the visuality and movement of the special issue's web-based, digital platform. We conceived of the digital elements of this article over a number of Zoom sessions with Jennifer Deger, Victoria Baskin Coffey, and Caleb Kingston—pondering how the relatively passive touch-based medium of the internet, with its scrolling and touchscreens, could be enlivened by replicating the touch-based transmission of craft knowledge, disposition, and lineage brought about in khrop khru ritual. We settled on using material remnants of khrop khru ritual from the Department of Thai Painting at Bangkok's Poh Chang Academy of the Arts as an animating visual guide that would enhance readers' journeys as their fingers scrolled through sections of our piece. In the annual khrop khru rituals held at Poh Chang, new Thai painting students take turns tracing with a pencil the facial outline of the god Phra Sayamphuwanat as their working hands are held by their teachers. These lines of pencil lead build up slowly over the course of the ritual, and result in scores of dark-silvery lines covering the image of the god's face. These lines simultaneously obscure and illuminate the image on the manuscript page, adding texture and shimmer when they catch the light. We found this image to be not only visually striking, but also a captivating material distillation of khrop khru society, and so wanted to replicate in the digital article the slow accretion of pencil lines that takes place throughout the ritual. Once we settled on a slow building-up of virtual pencil lines, we were faced with the problem of how to create this visually complex element. We asked the professors in the Thai Painting Department at Poh Chang for permission to use the face of Phra Sayamphuwanat as it was repeatedly retraced with lines of glistening pencil lead during khrop khru. They happily gave consent and sent along some images of Phra Sayamphuwanat from their ritual manuscripts to be sure we had high-quality files to work from. Ethnography usually flows from the field to the office. Fieldnotes, memories, photographs, and textual materials are collected onsite, and then collated, synthesised, and analysed at the scholar's desk or screen. Fittingly, for this project on the god of crafting, arts, and design, we brought the field into the printshop and photography studio, where we relied on the skills of specialised masters to bring shape to what we had conceived. Artist and designer Amelia Toelke cleaned up the image of Phra Sayamphuwanat from the ritual manuscript in Adobe Photoshop so that it could be transferred to a screen for printing. She then produced the screen and spent a day pulling large-format screenprints at the Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, New York. Anthony Lovenheim Irwin joined Toelke as a studio assistant in the printshop, where they made two different sets of prints—the first on off-white paper with dark grey ink, and another on black paper with yellow ink, attempting to mimic the look of different ritual manuscripts used in Poh Chang's khrop khru ritual. Irwin sent photos of the screenprints as they came off the press to the professors at Poh Chang over social media. With the prints now made, we had to replicate the pencil lines that would build up on the image, and to capture each layer digitally for the web. For this we worked with Heath Iverson, a photographer and filmmaker based at the Purpose Makerspace in Philmont, New York. Toelke, Iverson, and Irwin then spent a full day carefully tracing and retracing the faces of the Phra Sayamphuwanat prints in the order specified by the master teachers at Poh Chang: facial outline, eyes, nose, mouth and, finally, the unalom—the mark of perfect being—placed between and above the eyes and on the god's lingam-shaped crown. We used different pencil thicknesses on different prints, and photographed each tracing individually so that they could later be put together in an animation for the digital article. At this point the specific aesthetics for the digital visual element had not yet been decided upon, so four different tracing sets were created. At the end of the day, we had hundreds of photos and significantly cramped hands. Ultimately, after consulting with Coffey and Kingston about what would work best for the online platform, we settled on the image and pencil lines that most closely resembled the one used in the ritual—black paper with yellow ink, covered with 108 pencil tracings. The hundreds of images were then sent along to Coffey and Kingston, who have edited and stitched together the individual photos to create the animations that enliven our piece at each new section. Through our collective back-and-forth, we started calling the different sections of the piece ‘layers’ in recognition of how the article builds upon itself, just as the repeated tracings of pencil lead on the face of the god amass into a lustrous image of a divine being. Our multimedia article begins with an audio-recording of a Thai classical music ensemble (piphat) playing a ritual invocation to the Buddha and Phra Witsanukam. It is accompanied by printed text. A title page follows. The article then proceeds through ‘layers’ of description, interpretation, and analysis in replication of the layered ritualised tracings that adorn Phra Sayamphuwanat's visage during khrop khru ceremonies. The layers are as follows: Layer One – Surface Impressions Layer Two – Why Khrop Khru? Layer Three – Who is Phra Witsanukam? Layer Four – Khrop and Khru Layer Five – The 2019 Khrop Khru at Poh Chang Layer Six – Lineage and Cult Membership Layer Seven – Khrop Khru and the Sacralisation of Technicity Layer Eight – Khrop Khru, Cosmos, and Far-Futurity Layer Nine – Conclusion We hope these thematic or topical layers go far in capturing some of the rich textures of khrop khru ritual, and that the animation we have devised in collaboration with the Curatorium Editorial Collective hints at the way khrop khru society is itself a self-attuning assemblage of human, non-human, and divine beings. All translations from our Thai source materials and interviews are by Anthony Lovenheim Irwin. We gratefully acknowledge the support of the Australian Research Council for our ethnographic research in India and Thailand (Discovery Project Award DP170104212, K. Narayan and K. George, Co-Chief Investigators; A.L. Irwin, Research Partner for Thailand). Open access publishing has been facilitated by the Australian National University as part of the Wiley–Australian National University agreement via the Council of Australian University Librarians. Our warm thanks to Jennifer Deger, Victoria Baskin Coffey, Caleb Kingston, Sebastian J. Lowe, Lisa Stefanoff, and the Curatorium Editorial Collective for their invitation to take part in ‘Epistemic attunements’. Anthony Lovenheim Irwin wishes to acknowledge the Association for Asian Studies Pipeline Fellowship Program, which supported him while drafting this article. We would like to thank Irving Chan Johnson for his support and crucial contacts at Poh Chang. In Bangkok we would like to thank Achan Pramot Buntem, Achan Wichai Rakchat, Achan Chatchai Siripant, and all of the other professors at Poh Chang's Faculty of Thai Painting; Achan Chirapat Prapanvidya; Mr Prasoet Saeueng; Mr Sathit Kumar Pawa; Mrs. Nion Chanthakawanich; and Achan Prakirati Satasut. We gratefully acknowledge, too, the Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, New York, where the image was screenprinted, and Purpose Cooperative in Philmont, New York, where the visuals were photographed. Lastly, we thank Deborah Wong and two anonymous reviewers selected by TAJA for their exceedingly helpful comments and corrections to our manuscript. title_zh: 泰国一所艺术学院的崇拜、宇宙与工艺
abstract_zh: 《泰国一所艺术学院的崇拜、宇宙与工艺》是TAJA双特刊中一个集体数字写作实验的一部分。我们的目的是激发并实现新形式的社会分析。我们邀请贡献者与我们一同创造性地重新思考学术文章的形式，并建立了一个定制设计的网站来承载成果。本合集的所有原创研究贡献由两部分组成：一篇数字文章及其作者的释经评论。它们作为一对接受了同行评审。（关于这次“离网”学术冒险背后的理由，以及为什么Curatorium网站上的数字文章不提供PDF格式，请参见我们的引言《认知调谐：中介人类学实验》。）在此访问数字文章：https://curatorium.au/taja-journal/form-content/cult-cosmos-craft，或点击本注中的链接。1 阅读下面的作者评论。[体验Curatorium的预期效果请确保使用以下浏览器：Chrome版本121.0.6167.139或更高，或Safari版本16.6.1或更高。]我们首先需要说明是什么促使我们撰写关于khrop khru（“被古鲁覆盖”）的多媒体网络文章，这是泰国工艺和职业学院一年一度的仪式。Kirin Narayan和Ken George自2017年以来一直在对印度及其他地区的维什瓦卡玛崇拜进行民族志和历史研究，并于当年与Anthony Lovenheim Irwin（一位南传佛教和物质文化专家）合作，将研究扩展到泰国，在那里印度教-佛教神祇维什瓦卡玛被称为帕拉维萨努卡姆。无论研究将我们带到何处，维什瓦卡玛都被尊崇为工匠、技师、建筑师、工程师以及那些依靠工具、机器和制造为生的人——如泰国职业学院的毕业生——的守护神。除了对区域研究的明显意义外，我们对维什瓦卡玛崇拜的民族志和比较工作的更广泛目的是恢复技术在活态宗教和活态宇宙论中的作用。我们的多媒体文章《崇拜、宇宙与工艺》与此目的相一致。为了本期TAJA特刊《认知调谐》，我们还采取措施将文章的合作设计过程与帕拉维萨努卡姆信徒的宇宙技术倾向对齐并塑造。与多物种民族志、环境人类学、感官民族志和情感理论中的“多物”方法（其中“调谐”获得了方法论和分析上的关注）不同，我们调谐于神圣、明亮、机器和工具，以及信徒们栖居并实际上与它们及彼此调谐的方式。出于这个原因，在本文中，我们特别被khrop khru的触觉核心所吸引，其中一位大师教师和帕拉维萨努卡姆的信徒用手覆盖并引导学生工匠的工作手和工具，以塑造一个物体或图像。那个仪式姿态是一个场合，其中帕拉维萨努卡姆的“覆盖”存在内在于被造物体和工艺活动的物质、表面、设计和触感中。在这里，制作图像或其他物体的行为明显地使世界和宇宙对齐。在维什瓦卡玛及其追随者的扩展世界中工作向我们表明，人们调谐于神性的一种方式是通过制造、建造和艺术创作的行为。Khrop khru仪式将注意力集中在各种形式的手工制造上，并产生了一个我们称之为“khrop khru社会”的社会和宇宙技术集合体。参与khrop khru仪式，作为进入该社会的入门，使新学生调谐于神性、他们的老师、他们各自行业的工具以及他们的同修——创造宇宙社会网络并呈现特定的学习方式和存在于世界的方式。我们三人（Irwin、George和Narayan）于2019年7月下旬在兰纳皇家理工大学（Techno Chiang Mai）举行的仪式中被引入khrop khru社会。我们这么说并不是为了声称对“本地人的观点”有特权理解或完全吸收，而是为了将khrop khru的宇宙技术集合体与进入本文的数字平台可供性和设计过程结合并调谐。我们希望我们通过培养对仪式触觉核心的接受性——从实地工作到文章写作与设计合作——来奠定我们对khrop khru的理解。尽管如此，我们对khrop khru的理解并非仅仅来自我们对那个核心的接受性；我们并非试图对核心工艺物品进行相面术解读以揭示仪式的奥秘和范围。相反，我们通过与帕拉维萨努卡姆在泰国的信徒的对话、访谈、照片和表演来了解khrop khru的运作，并培养对其质地的敏感度。我们对本期《认知调谐》策展的贡献目标是利用特刊网络数字平台的视觉性和运动性，向读者-观看者传达khrop khru仪式的触觉、社会和审美方面。我们与Jennifer Deger、Victoria Baskin Coffey和Caleb Kingston通过多次Zoom会议构思了本文的数字元素，思考如何通过复制khrop khru仪式中工艺知识、性情和传承的触觉传递，来活跃互联网这一相对被动的触觉媒介（滚屏和触摸屏）。我们决定使用曼谷Poh Chang艺术学院泰国绘画系的khrop khru仪式物质残留物作为动画视觉指南，以增强读者手指滚动浏览文章各部分时的旅程。在Poh Chang每年举行的khrop khru仪式中，新的泰国绘画学生轮流用铅笔描摹神祇Phra Sayamphuwanat的脸部轮廓，而他们的手被老师握住。铅笔的线条在仪式过程中慢慢堆积，结果形成数十条深银色线条覆盖神祇脸部的图像。这些线条同时模糊和照亮手稿页上的图像，在光线照射时增添质感和闪光。我们发现这个图像不仅视觉上震撼，而且是khrop khru社会的一个迷人物质浓缩，因此希望在数字文章中复制仪式中铅笔线条的缓慢积累。一旦我们决定缓慢积累虚拟铅笔线条，我们面临着如何创建这个视觉复杂元素的问题。我们请求Poh Chang泰国绘画系的教授允许使用Phra Sayamphuwanat的脸部，因为它在khrop khru中被反复用闪闪发光的铅笔线条描摹。他们欣然同意，并寄来了一些他们仪式手稿中的Phra Sayamphuwanat图像，以确保我们有高质量的文件。民族志通常从田野流向办公室。田野笔记、记忆、照片和文本材料在现场收集，然后在学者的办公桌或屏幕前整理、综合和分析。对于这个关于工艺、艺术和设计之神的项目，恰当地，我们将田野带入了印刷店和摄影工作室，依靠专业大师的技能来塑造我们所构思的东西。艺术家兼设计师Amelia Toelke在Adobe Photoshop中清除了仪式手稿中的Phra Sayamphuwanat图像，以便将其转移到屏幕上进行印刷。然后她制作了丝网，并花了一天时间在纽约州Rosendale的女性工作室工作室进行大幅丝网印刷。Anthony Lovenheim Irwin作为工作室助手加入Toelke，在印刷店制作了两组不同的印刷品——第一组在米白色纸上用深灰色墨水，另一组在黑色纸上用黄色墨水，试图模仿Poh Chang的khrop khru仪式中使用的不同仪式手稿的外观。Irwin将印刷品从印刷机出来的照片通过社交媒体发送给Poh Chang的教授。现在印刷品已制作完成，我们必须复制会在图像上积累的铅笔线条，并为网络捕获每一层数字图像。为此，我们与纽约州Philmont的Purpose Makerspace的摄影师和电影制作人Heath Iverson合作。Toelke、Iverson和Irwin然后花了一整天按照Poh Chang大师教师指定的顺序仔细描摹和再描摹Phra Sayamphuwanat印刷品的脸部：脸部轮廓、眼睛、鼻子、嘴巴，最后是unalom——完美存在的标记——放置在眼睛之间和之上以及神祇的灵伽形王冠上。我们在不同的印刷品上使用了不同的铅笔厚度，并单独拍摄了每个描摹，以便稍后可以将它们组合成数字文章的动画。此时数字视觉元素的具体美学尚未确定，因此创建了四组不同的描摹。一天结束时，我们有数百张照片和明显抽筋的手。最终，在与Coffey和Kingston咨询了在线平台上最适合的内容后，我们决定使用最接近仪式中使用的图像和铅笔线条——黑色纸上的黄色墨水，覆盖了108次铅笔描摹。然后，数百张图像被发送给Coffey和Kingston，他们编辑并拼接了各个照片，创建了在每个新部分使我们的文章活跃的动画。通过我们的集体反复交流，我们开始称文章的不同部分为“层”，以承认文章如何自我构建，就像铅笔线条在神祇脸上的重复描摹累积成神圣存在的光彩图像一样。我们的多媒体文章以一段泰国古典音乐合奏（piphat）演奏的仪式祈请的音频录音开始，祈请佛陀和帕拉维萨努卡姆。伴随打印文本。随后是标题页。文章然后通过描述、解释和分析的“层”进行，复制了在khrop khru仪式中装饰Phra Sayamphuwanat面容的层叠仪式化描摹。这些层如下：第一层——表面印象；第二层——为什么khrop khru？；第三层——帕拉维萨努卡姆是谁？；第四层——Khrop和Khru；第五层——2019年Poh Chang的khrop khru；第六层——谱系与教团成员；第七层——Khrop khru与技术性的神圣化；第八层——Khrop khru、宇宙与远未来；第九层——结论。我们希望这些主题或专题的层能很好地捕捉khrop khru仪式丰富质地的一些方面，并且我们与Curatorium编辑集体合作设计的动画能暗示khrop khru社会本身是如何成为一个由人类、非人类和神圣存在组成的自调谐集合体。所有来自泰文资料和访谈的翻译均由Anthony Lovenheim Irwin完成。开放获取出版由澳大利亚国立大学促进，作为Wiley—澳大利亚国立大学协议通过澳大利亚大学图书馆员委员会的一部分。我们衷心感谢澳大利亚研究委员会对我们印度和泰国民族志研究的支持（发现项目奖DP170104212，K. Narayan和K. George共同首席研究员；A.L. Irwin为泰国研究合作伙伴）。开放获取出版由澳大利亚国立大学作为Wiley—澳大利亚国立大学协议通过澳大利亚大学图书馆员委员会的一部分促成。我们衷心感谢Jennifer Deger、Victoria Baskin Coffey、Caleb Kingston、Sebastian J. Lowe、Lisa Stefanoff和Curatorium编辑集体邀请我们参与《认知调谐》。Anthony Lovenheim Irwin感谢亚洲研究协会管道奖学金计划，该计划在撰写本文时支持了他。我们要感谢Irving Chan Johnson在Poh Chang的支持和关键联系人。在曼谷，我们要感谢Achan Pramot Buntem、Achan Wichai Rakchat、Achan Chatchai Siripant以及Poh Chang泰国绘画学院的所有其他教授；Achan Chirapat Prapanvidya；Prasoet Saeueng先生；Sathit Kumar Pawa先生；Nion Chanthakawanich夫人；以及Achan Prakirati Satasut。在清迈，我们衷心感谢Achan Natachak Na Chiang Mai和Achan Phonsin Ratanachudet。在清莱，我们要感谢清莱技术学院的所有教授，以及Ravi和Uma Upra夫妇。在纽约，我们衷心感谢Amelia Toelke和Heath Iverson帮助为本项目制作Phra Sayamphuwanat的视觉材料。我们也感谢纽约州Rosendale的女性工作室工作室，那里进行了丝网印刷，以及纽约州Philmont的Purpose Cooperative，那里拍摄了视觉材料。最后，我们感谢Deborah Wong和TAJA选定的两位匿名审稿人，他们对我们的手稿提供了极为有益的意见和修正。支持本研究结果的数据可根据合理要求从通讯作者处获得。

title: Dangerous winds: Criminal threats and the indigenized security of wind power in Colombia
journal_name: Journal of Latin American and Caribbean Anthropology
abstract: Abstract Global energy companies have regularly depended on state and private security for sustaining their operations, often with deadly consequences for union leaders, environmental defenders, and local communities. This article examines how these security arrangements are mutating amid the rapid expansion of renewable energy in Latin America. It uncovers how wind energy companies in Colombia rely on Indigenous knowledge, social networks, and legal norms to safeguard themselves in La Guajira, a border region reputed by outsiders as haunted by criminality and (il)legal practices. Through long‐term ethnographic research of corporate spaces, I argue that Wayúu lifeways are mobilized by green energy capital to craft a hybrid security apparatus that, though failure‐prone, is crucial for Colombia's low‐carbon future. This case reveals how corporate and Indigenous configurations of protection and risk prevention work in tandem across sites that are being demarcated for the energy transition and climate change mitigation in Latin America.
title_zh: 危险的风：哥伦比亚风电的刑事威胁与本土化安全
abstract_zh: 摘要 全球能源公司通常依赖国家和私人安保来维持其运营，这常常对工会领袖、环保活动家和当地社区造成致命后果。本文考察了在拉丁美洲可再生能源快速扩张的背景下，这些安保安排如何发生变异。它揭示了哥伦比亚的风能公司如何依靠土著知识、社会网络和法律规范在拉瓜希拉省进行自我保护，该边境地区被外界认为充满犯罪和非法活动。通过对企业空间的长期民族志研究，我认为威乌人的生活方式被绿色能源资本动员起来，构建了一种混合安保机制，尽管容易失败，但对哥伦比亚的低碳未来至关重要。这一案例揭示了企业和本土的保护与风险预防配置如何在拉丁美洲能源转型和气候变化缓解的划定区域协同运作。

title: Despotism on the shop floor: Foreign company labour governance in Ethiopia's industrial park
abstract: In recent years, Ethiopia has become a prime destination for labour‐intensive, export‐oriented manufacturing industries by virtue of its favourable investment climate and cheap labour. This article examines the labour governance and disciplinary strategies of foreign companies in Ethiopia's industrial park, focusing on the Blue Apparel Company (BAC) in the Bole Lemi Industrial Park, Addis Ababa. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork conducted from August 2021 to August 2022, the study reveals how relaxed labour regulations and the absence of trade unions enable foreign firms to enforce strict, profit‐driven governance. The analysis highlights despotic management practices, hierarchical power dynamics and their impact on local workers. The findings shed light on the intricacies of labour control in globalized production regimes and highlight the challenges workers encounter in emerging economies.
title_zh: 车间内的专制：埃塞俄比亚工业园中外资公司的劳工治理
abstract_zh: 近年来，埃塞俄比亚凭借其有利的投资环境和廉价劳动力，已成为劳动密集型和出口导向型制造业的主要目的地。本文考察了埃塞俄比亚工业园中外资公司的劳工治理和纪律策略，重点关注亚的斯亚贝巴博莱莱米工业园的Blue Apparel Company（BAC）。基于2021年8月至2022年8月进行的民族志田野调查，研究揭示了宽松的劳工法规和工会的缺失如何使外国公司得以实施严格的、利润驱动的治理。分析强调了专制管理实践、等级权力动态及其对当地工人的影响。研究结果揭示了全球化生产体制中劳工控制的复杂性，并突出了新兴经济体工人面临的挑战。

title: Energopolitics of Transition: The Political Ecology of Anticipation in the Portuguese Lithium Rush
abstract: ABSTRACT: This article examines the current mining revival in Europe, focusing on the dispute over lithium mining projects in Portugal. Lithium's growing role in energy storage explains its global speculative boom and its popularity in the socio-technological imaginary of the energy transition. In Portugal, lithium mining applications have skyrocketed in the last decade following the European call for the internal supply of critical raw materials. In 2018, the Portuguese government launched the National Lithium Strategy to assess potential resources and the feasibility of industrial development projects. The lithium rush has quickly become a controversial topic in national debates on energy transition and sustainable development. Community participation has also become an issue, as a highly centralized decisionmaking process has turned a politically sensitive issue into a technocratic matter, triggering opposition from local communities who remain aware of the socio-environmental legacy of past mining booms and busts. The analysis focuses on a specific case in 2019, when the lithium rush came to public attention, to unpack the politics of time underlying the mining revival and opposition to it in the context of the energy transition. The latter is examined as a field of negotiation, friction, and conflict through which the different temporalities of the European periphery are articulated. Highlighting the relevance of internal and external unequal relations for understanding the conflict over lithium, the article argues that while the case of Portugal exemplifies lithium onshoring in the Global North, it also shows that the making of internal resource frontiers for the energy transition builds on—and reinforces—historical dynamics of dispossession and peripheralization; and that such stratification of unequal relations finds temporal refraction in the ways socio-ecological futures are anticipated and imagined in the dispute over the energy transition.
title_zh: 转型的能源政治：葡萄牙锂矿热潮中的预期政治生态学
abstract_zh: 摘要：本文考察了当前欧洲的采矿复兴，重点关注葡萄牙锂矿项目的争议。锂在能源储存中日益增长的作用解释了其在全球的投机热潮及其在能源转型的社会技术想象中受欢迎的原因。在葡萄牙，过去十年里，随着欧盟对关键原材料内部供应的呼吁，锂矿申请数量激增。2018年，葡萄牙政府启动了国家锂战略，以评估潜在资源和工业发展项目的可行性。锂矿热潮迅速成为国家关于能源转型和可持续发展的辩论中一个有争议的话题。社区参与也成为一个问题，因为高度集中的决策过程将政治敏感问题变成了技术官僚事务，引发了当地社区的反对，他们仍然记得过去采矿繁荣和萧条的社会环境遗留问题。分析聚焦于2019年锂矿热潮引起公众关注的一个具体案例，以揭示能源转型背景下采矿复兴及其反对背后的时间政治。后者被视为一个谈判、摩擦和冲突的领域，通过它，欧洲外围的不同时间性得以表达。文章强调了内外不平等关系对于理解锂矿冲突的相关性，认为虽然葡萄牙案例代表了全球北方的锂矿本土化，但也表明，为能源转型创建内部资源前沿建立在——并强化了——历史上的剥夺和边缘化动态；这种不平等的分层在关于能源转型的争议中，通过社会生态未来的预期和想象方式找到了时间折射。
