And from the view of Malagasy port authorities, the container ships full of supplies became an increasingly lucrative source of income from duties. Not simply a follow the money or follow the suture narrative, Halvorson's book inquires into the motivations and testimonies of Minnesotan and Malagasy participants in this transnational humanitarian trade, situating them in personal relationships and broader systems of biomedical capitalism. In this latter sense, Halvorson offers an unusually cogent definition of neoliberalism (instead of letting the word roam over the ethnography as a foggy specter, as is often the case). Gesturing to Loïc Wacquant, she writes: "neoliberalism is not characterized by the total evisceration of the state but the reconstitution of it through a variety of market reforms that support the interest of a political elite" (30). In this case, the elites include doctors, church workers, and NGO volunteers both in Minnesota and Madagascar. But it is clear from her conversations with people in both countries that to be designated "elite" from this theoretical vantage point did not exempt any one from worrying about money, jobs, health, or faith. The book is structured by six chapters that traverse Minnesota and Madagascar. The first chapter reflects on how Minnesota Lutherans remember and forget—or sometimes rebuke—their history of medical missions in Madagascar. Distinguishing between a previous model of colonial missionary imposition and a contemporary model of accompaniment and partnership, the Minnesotans, in Halvorson's view, "create a split between the (less moral) early colonial past and the (more moral) humanitarian present" (52). The second chapter details the establishment and workings of two US NGOs focused on providing medical supplies to Madagascar, and argues that these groups are shaped by a "biospiritual imaginary" that brings together conservative and liberal Lutherans in Minnesota. The third chapter hones in on the people and infrastructures that enable the movement of medical discards, through a lens of "economies of blessings and sins" that label some supplies as junk and other supplies as useful, and even redemptive. In the next chapter, focused on questions and concepts of value, Halvorson shows how the US and Malagasy medical and Christian organizations generate different kinds of value through this exchange and its attending relationships. For example, by casting off [End Page 1626] their discards, US hospitals seek a redemption at...
title_zh: 改宗之地：从马达加斯加到明尼苏达的医疗援助与全球基督教的转变
abstract_zh: 评论：《改宗之地：从马达加斯加到明尼苏达的医疗援助与全球基督教的转变》，作者布里特·哈尔沃森。帕梅拉·E·克拉森。布里特·哈尔沃森，《改宗之地：从马达加斯加到明尼苏达的医疗援助与全球基督教的转变》。芝加哥：芝加哥大学出版社，2018年。288页。《改宗之地》讲述了传教士回国后，在放弃殖民假设但不愿放弃赋予其职业意义和精神预兆的故事或关系的情况下，医疗传教活动的后续故事。该书聚焦于明尼苏达州的一个路德宗非政府组织，该组织将美国多余的医疗用品运往马达加斯加的一个姐妹组织，追踪医疗废弃物——如缝合线和血检指刺——如何通过集装箱船或民族志学者的行李箱从美国医院运往马达加斯加诊所。作为20世纪60年代后主流新教徒从公开的殖民传教工作转向的一部分，美国路德宗传教士减少了明尼苏达与马达加斯加之间的旅行，将传教重新 envision 为“伙伴关系”或“陪伴”而非改宗。多余的医疗用品取代了人员，成为马达加斯加基督徒与其明尼苏达伙伴之间的慈善纽带。通过追踪从明尼苏达志愿者仓库到马达加斯加目的地的医疗废弃物，作者布里特·哈尔沃森表明这些医疗援助形式的意义在多重意义上都是“工具性的”。对于明尼苏达路德宗信徒来说，捐赠是上帝之爱以及他们陪伴马达加斯加基督徒承诺的有形标志。同样但不同地，对于马达加斯加基督徒（包括医生）来说，医疗用品最有价值的不是其治疗用途，而是它们承诺的外国联系和未来的社会资本。从美国医疗组织的角度来看，从美国医院储藏室转移到马达加斯加诊所的废弃物代表着税收减免。而从马达加斯加港务局的角度来看，装满物资的集装箱船成为关税收入日益丰厚的来源。哈尔沃森的书不仅仅是“跟着钱走”或“跟着缝线走”的叙述，而是探究了明尼苏达和马达加斯加参与者在这场跨国人道主义贸易中的动机和证词，将其置于个人关系和更广泛的生物医学资本主义体系中。就后者而言，哈尔沃森提供了一个异常清晰的新自由主义定义（而不是任由这个词像模糊的幽灵一样笼罩民族志）。她引用Loïc Wacquant写道：“新自由主义的特征不是国家的彻底瓦解，而是通过支持政治精英利益的各种市场改革对其进行重建”（30）。在这种情况下，精英包括明尼苏达和马达加斯加的医生、教会工作人员和非政府组织志愿者。但从她与两国人民的对话中可以清楚地看到，从这一理论角度被指定为“精英”并不能使任何人免于担心金钱、工作、健康或信仰。本书由六章组成，跨越明尼苏达和马达加斯加。第一章反思明尼苏达路德宗信徒如何记住、忘记或有时指责他们在马达加斯加的医疗传教历史。哈尔沃森认为，通过区分过去的殖民传教强制模式和当代的陪伴与伙伴关系模式，明尼苏达人“在（道德较差的）早期殖民过去与（更道德的）人道主义现在之间制造了分裂”（52）。第二章详述了两个专注于向马达加斯加提供医疗用品的美国非政府组织的建立和运作，并认为这些组织受到“生物精神想象”的塑造，该想象将明尼苏达的保守派和自由派路德宗信徒聚集在一起。第三章通过“祝福与罪孽的经济”视角，聚焦于使医疗废弃物流动的人员和基础设施，该视角将一些物资标记为垃圾，其他则标记为有用甚至救赎之物。在下一章中，聚焦于价值和概念问题，哈尔沃森展示了美国和马达加斯加的医疗和基督教组织如何通过这种交换及其伴随的关系产生不同类型的价值。例如，通过丢弃废弃物，美国医院寻求一种救赎……

title: Do algorithms have a right to the city? Waze and algorithmic spatiality
abstract: This article introduces the notion of algorithmic spatiality as a way to capture the unique spatial knowledge created by digital mobile media, and the way that this knowledge acts upon space, and is perceived by other actors involved in the production of space. Focusing on the navigation giant Waze, it asks how this new spatial actor legitimates the knowledge it creates about space and the effects incurred by this knowledge. In theoretical terms, it asks how Waze asserts its ‘right to the city’ through a discourse of a superior knowledge of space. These questions are discussed in light of a case study of the clash between Waze and local residents over the application’s common practice of diverting large volumes of traffic through side-roads, located in quiet neighbourhoods and villages in Israel. Over a period of two years, these clashes – by legal, political, and discursive means – reached public discussions in news outlets and social media, and these form the corpus of the research. The article shows how along long-established forms of knowledge which underlie different actors’ right to the city – experts’ knowledge, democratic knowledge, market knowledge, and local knowledge – emerges a new kind of knowledge, backed by big-data and algorithms and managed by a quasi-monopolistic platform, which claims a legitimate right to the production of space. Traditionally a right upheld by underprivileged groups and individuals, the right to the city is currently upheld by a socio-technical assemblage.
title_zh: 算法有城市权吗？Waze与算法空间性
abstract_zh: 本文引入了算法空间性的概念，以捕捉数字移动媒体创造的独特空间知识，以及这些知识作用于空间的方式，并被其他参与空间生产的行动者所感知。以导航巨头Waze为焦点，探讨这一新的空间行动者如何使其创造的关于空间的知识以及这些知识所产生的影响合法化。在理论层面，探讨Waze如何通过声称拥有优越的空间知识来主张其‘城市权’。这些问题通过Waze与当地居民之间关于该应用程序将大量交通引导至以色列安静社区和村庄小路的常见做法的冲突案例研究进行讨论。在两年多的时间里，这些冲突——通过法律、政治和话语手段——在新闻媒体和社交媒体上引发了公开讨论，这些构成了研究语料。文章展示了在长期存在的、构成不同行动者城市权的知识形式——专家知识、民主知识、市场知识和地方知识——之外，一种由大数据和算法支持、由准垄断平台管理的新型知识出现，并声称对空间生产拥有合法权利。城市权传统上由弱势群体和个人持有，现在则由一个社会技术集合体持有。

title: Lab hands and knowing toxic substances in Uganda
abstract: How does one know a toxic substance? Perhaps paradoxically, through contact with it, as I show ethnographically from a molecular biology laboratory in Uganda, a site where people routinely handle a range of chemicals, including potentially hazardous toxicants. I analyse an everyday situation in which researchers worked with ethidium bromide, a substance regularly used to stain DNA bands in gels at this Ugandan lab but also in many comparable labs elsewhere. Ethidium bromide is one of the most fear‐inspiring chemicals at this lab; it is considered a potent mutagen and thus counts as highly carcinogenic. While the lab has clear safety procedures concerning how to handle this substance correctly, these are often not implemented in a hard‐to‐control lab setting marked by both material deprivation and a steady flow of unremunerated volunteers who seek to gain practical experience. I show how experienced Ugandan scientists have learned to mitigate their own risk of exposure to ethidium bromide by developing choreographed routines that prevent them from inadvertently touching it. I examine this as a way of ‘handling’ a dangerous substance, developing and habituating skilled movements of hands and bodies that then are passed on to other researchers. It is not an abstract knowledge of a substance's chemical properties that counts here; instead, knowing a toxic substance implies practical routines of handling.
title_zh: 乌干达实验室中的手与有毒物质认知
abstract_zh: 人们如何认知有毒物质？或许矛盾的是，通过与其接触，正如我在乌干达的一个分子生物学实验室的民族志研究中所展示的，那里的人们日常处理一系列化学品，包括潜在的危险有毒物质。我分析了一个日常情境，其中研究人员使用溴化乙锭，这是一种在乌干达实验室以及许多其他类似实验室中常规用于凝胶中DNA条带染色的物质。在该实验室，溴化乙锭是最令人恐惧的化学品之一；它被认为是一种强效诱变剂，因此被视为高致癌物。尽管实验室有关于如何正确处理这种物质的明确安全程序，但在一个以物质匮乏和源源不断的无偿志愿者（寻求实践经验）为特征的难以控制的实验室环境中，这些程序往往无法实施。我展示了有经验的乌干达科学家如何通过发展出一套编排好的常规动作来学会减轻自身接触溴化乙锭的风险，这些动作可以防止他们意外触碰到它。我将其视为一种“处理”危险物质的方式，发展和习惯化熟练的手和身体动作，然后这些动作会传递给其他研究人员。这里重要的不是对物质化学性质的抽象知识；相反，认知有毒物质意味着实际的处理常规。

title: Living with toxic development: Shipbreaking in the industrializing zone of Sitakunda, Bangladesh
abstract: Based on ethnographic fieldwork among local communities and shipbreaking workers, this essay focuses on the lived experiences of toxicity in the rapidly industrializing zone of Sitakunda, Bangladesh. Shipbreaking is receiving attention as a zone of toxic exposure. There is pressure for increased regulation and protection for workers. In contrast, other forms of pollution in the industrial zone of Sitakunda, such as water, air and noise pollution, are neglected or ignored. Worries about pollution and health highlight the unevenness of promises of development to come, also expressed by marginalized fishing communities structurally excluded from industrialization. My interlocutors describe unnayan (economic development) as bishakto (poisonous, toxic). I conceptualize this as ‘toxic development’ to draw attention to how ‘ordinary people’ (migrant workers, fishing and agricultural communities, shipbreaking workers and manual labourers) without capital, land or social networks of influence endure poisonous industrial activities that both create livelihoods and destroy them.
title_zh: 与有毒发展共存：孟加拉国Sitakunda工业化区的拆船业
abstract_zh: 基于在当地社区和拆船工人中的民族志田野调查，本文重点关注孟加拉国快速工业化区Sitakunda中关于毒性的生活经验。拆船业作为有毒暴露区域受到关注，要求加强监管和保护工人的压力不断增加。相比之下，Sitakunda工业区其他形式的污染，如水、空气和噪音污染，则被忽视或忽略。对污染和健康的担忧凸显了发展承诺的不均衡性，也体现在被排斥在工业化之外的边缘化渔业社区中。我的访谈对象将unnayan（经济发展）描述为bishakto（有毒的）。我将此概念化为“有毒发展”，以引起人们对没有资本、土地或社会网络影响的“普通人”（移民工人、渔业和农业社区、拆船工人和体力劳动者）如何忍受既创造生计又摧毁生计的有毒工业活动的关注。

title: Non-/Human Infrastructures and Digital Gifts: The Cables, Waves and Brokers of Solomon Islands Internet
abstract: This article demonstrates how nonhuman and human infrastructural assemblages, and the brokers that operate as assemblers within them, give rise to localised Internets. With an ethnographic emphasis on the digital transformations of Solomon Islands, we examine agentive brokerage practices surrounding digital multimedia files, downloaded off the global Internet and circulated offline as gifts via MicroSDs. We show how digital brokers use their comparatively unique manoeuvrability within digital infrastructural assemblages. They extend the Internet to offline rural environments, while following and strengthening local systems of moral economic social reproduction. Recognising the interconnectedness of human and nonhuman actors, these brokers are also dependent on the broader infrastructural assemblages in which they operate, especially the cables and waves that initially allow digital bits to travel to Solomon Islands. Localised Internets such as Solomon Islands are, thus, continuously in flux, being perpetually reassembled by the agentive practices of their constituent parts.
title_zh: 非/人类基础设施与数字礼物：所罗门群岛互联网的电缆、电波和中间人
abstract_zh: 本文展示了非人类和人类基础设施组合，以及在其中充当组装者的中间人如何产生本地化的互联网。通过对所罗门群岛数字转型的民族志强调，我们考察了围绕数字多媒体文件的代理性中间人实践，这些文件从全球互联网下载并通过MicroSD作为礼物离线传播。我们展示了数字中间人如何利用他们在数字基础设施组合中相对独特的可操控性。他们将互联网扩展到离线的农村环境，同时遵循并加强当地道德经济的社会再生产的系统。认识到人类和非人类行动者的相互关联性，这些中间人也依赖于他们所处的更广泛的基础设施组合，尤其是最初允许数字比特传输到所罗门群岛的电缆和电波。因此，诸如所罗门群岛这样的本地化互联网不断处于变化之中，由其组成部分的代理性实践持续重新组装而成。

title: Organic taste and labour on Indian tea plantations*
abstract: Goût biologique et labour dans les plantations de thé indiennes Cet article adopte une perspective multi‐espèces sur le goût pour explorer comment l’agriculture biologique affecte à la fois les relations non humaines et le travail humain dans les plantations de thé indiennes. Les planteurs de thé biologique utilisent le goût pour évaluer les conditions du sol et les changements climatiques et pour appliquer des pratiques biologiques en conséquence. L’article soutient que, d’une part, les planteurs cultivent stratégiquement des formes de collaboration entre les théiers, les champignons, les vaches et les micro‐organismes du sol pour améliorer le goût des cultures en monoculture. D’autre part, puisque ces formes de collaboration requièrent et reproduisent le travail précaire des travailleurs et des superviseurs du thé, leur résistance aux pratiques biologiques affecte également les goûts. Le terroir du thé biologique se caractérise à la fois par l’unité des espèces dans les monocultures et par les inégalités du travail dans les plantations.
title_zh: 印度茶园中的有机口味与劳动
abstract_zh: 本文采用多物种视角探讨口味，研究有机农业如何影响印度茶园中的非人类关系和人类劳动。有机茶农利用口味评估土壤条件和气候变化，并据此应用有机实践。文章认为，一方面，茶农策略性地培育茶树、真菌、奶牛和土壤微生物之间的合作形式，以改善单一种植作物的口味。另一方面，由于这些合作形式需要并再生产了茶工和监工的 precarious 劳动，他们对有机实践的抵制也影响了口味。有机茶的 terroir 特征既包括单一种植中的物种统一性，也包括种植园中的劳动不平等。

title: Permeable persons and plastic packaging in India: from biomoral substance exchange to chemotoxic transmission
journal_name: JOURNAL OF THE ROYAL ANTHROPOLOGICAL INSTITUTE
abstract: Abstract In contemporary India, it has become commonplace to hear middle‐class people speak of ‘chemicals’ in the environment, in food, and in everyday commodities. Anxieties revolve around the bodily absorption of these ‘chemicals’, and plastic packaging has come under particular scrutiny as a source of such leached substances. Although anthropological studies have highlighted South Asian conceptions of the person as permeable and affected, through the exchange of biomoral substances, by transactions with the environment, humans, and nonhumans, the concern about ‘chemicals’ references a different type of transfer: that of chemotoxic transmission. Such concern foregrounds new anxieties about the permeable body in the contaminated, ecologically damaged world of late modernity. The case of plastic packaging is illustrative of the differences between frameworks of biomoral substance exchange and chemotoxic transmission. In illuminating those differences, this article focuses on public concerns regarding the bodily absorption of ‘chemicals’, why these concerns are compelling as a political ecological critique of capitalist extraction, and the insights they can offer to anthropological research on the permeable body.
title_zh: 印度的可渗透身体和塑料包装：从生物道德物质交换到化学毒性传播
abstract_zh: 在当代印度，中产阶级人士常谈论环境、食品和日常商品中的“化学物质”。这些焦虑围绕身体对这些“化学物质”的吸收，而塑料包装作为此类浸出物质的来源受到特别关注。尽管人类学研究强调了南亚将人视为可渗透的、并通过与环境和人类及非人类的生物道德物质交换而受影响的概念，但对“化学物质”的担忧指的是另一种类型的转移：化学毒性传播。这种担忧突出了在晚期现代性受污染、生态破坏的世界中可渗透身体的新焦虑。塑料包装的案例说明了生物道德物质交换与化学毒性传播框架之间的差异。通过阐明这些差异，本文聚焦公众对身体吸收“化学物质”的担忧，为何这些担忧作为对资本主义开采的政治生态批判具有说服力，以及它们能为关于可渗透身体的人类学研究提供的见解。

title: Scattered Things: Virtue Ethics and Objectness in Indigenous Amazonia
abstract: This article seeks to extend the enduring focus on the body and bodily substance in Amazonia, which have historically eclipsed other forms of relatedness and ethical practices. Among the Venezuelan Sanema, morality is enacted predominantly through manufactured items rather than solely corporeal expressions of relatedness. While artefacts of all forms are receiving increased recognition in the region, they are often explored within a non-dualist frame that foregrounds inalienability, ownership and subjectification. Yet, the Sanema ethnography reveals that dissolving dualisms in this way suppresses the existence of important categories such as objects. Focusing on how ethical practices are enacted through partible beads and diesel-powered generators, this paper reveals how alienable goods among the Sanema are valued precisely for their ‘objectness’ rather than their personified qualities.
title_zh: 散落之物：土著亚马孙的德性伦理与物性
abstract_zh: 本文旨在扩展亚马孙地区长期以来对身体及身体物质的关注，这种关注在历史上遮蔽了其他形式的关联性和伦理实践。在委内瑞拉萨内马人中，道德主要通过制造品来体现，而不仅仅是身体上的关联表达。虽然各种形式的物品在该地区日益受到重视，但通常是在一种非二元论框架下探讨，强调不可让渡性、所有权和主体化。然而，萨内马人的民族志揭示，以这种方式消解二元论压制了诸如物体等重要范畴的存在。通过聚焦于可分割的珠子与柴油发电机如何体现伦理实践，本文揭示了萨内马人中的可让渡物品正是因其“物性”而非人格化特征而受到珍视。

title: The Feel of 13,000 Containers: How Pilots Learn to Navigate Changing Logistical Environments
abstract: This article analyses how the 2016 expansion of the Panama Canal changed the work of the pilots responsible for navigating massive ships through the chokepoint. For pilots, the expansion meant learning to maneuver Neo-Panamax vessels that dwarfed anything in their experience. The pilot training associated with the expansion reveals a paradox at the heart of a shipping industry that pursues efficiencies through economies of scale and automation. In the confined waters where maritime routes converge, increased ship size and traffic may render a pilot’s embodied capacity to ‘feel’ how ships handle in particular environments more – not less – important. Combining analysis of historical shipping transitions, interviews, and observations at a 1:25 scale physical model training facility where pilots maneuver miniature megaships through a miniature canal, I argue that the Panama Canal Authority's institutional recognition of the importance of ‘feel’ in contemporary interoceanic transit indexes the emergence of a logistical environment that elevates the status of some forms of embodied knowledge, even as it diminishes others.
title_zh: 感受13,000个集装箱：引航员如何学会应对变化的物流环境
abstract_zh: 本文分析了2016年巴拿马运河扩建如何改变了负责引导巨型船舶通过该咽喉要道的引航员的工作。对引航员而言，扩建意味着学习操纵远超其经验的新巴拿马型船只。与扩建相关的引航员培训揭示了航运业通过规模经济和自动化追求效率的核心悖论。在海上航线交汇的狭窄水域，船舶尺寸增大和交通量增加可能使引航员‘感受’船舶在特定环境中操控方式的具身能力变得更加重要——而非相反。结合对历史航运转型的分析、访谈以及在1:25比例物理模型训练设施（引航员在此操纵微型超级油轮通过微型运河）中的观察，我认为巴拿马运河管理局对‘感觉’在当代跨洋运输中重要性的制度性认可，标志着一种物流环境的出现，它提升了某些具身知识的地位，同时削弱了其他形式的具身知识。

title: The Stuff of Contention and Care: Affective Materiality and Everyday Learning in Bristol, UK
abstract: Abstract Drawing on fieldwork in Bristol, UK, the article resituates the increasingly popular policy framing of a “learning city” within recent anthropological debates on urban political materiality. Using research findings from fieldwork conducted in sites of informal and non‐formal learning on the margins of a UNESCO Learning City, we argue for an ethnography that is attentive to the ways in which learning manifests itself in everyday life. Through three field sites—a community space, a bicycle workshop, and a contested heritage campaign—we demonstrate the significance of material culture, controversy, and care as constitutive of learning processes within urban life. Through these examples, we aim to reframe questions on the complexity of learning at a city scale as part of affect‐driven knowledge and the material, embodied transmission of skill and everyday practice. By tracing how learning plays out in everyday life, we can begin to interrogate what happens beyond the neoliberal forms of educational governance, and the extent to which the everyday practices challenge or reinforce top‐down formulations as well as potentially transforming forms of knowledge production.
title_zh: 争议与关怀之物：英国布里斯托尔的情感物质性与日常学习
abstract_zh: 摘要 基于在英国布里斯托尔的田野调查，本文将近来越来越流行的“学习型城市”政策框架重新置于近期关于城市政治物质性的人类学辩论中。利用在联合国教科文组织学习型城市边缘的非正规和非正式学习场所进行的田野调查结果，我们主张一种关注学习在日常生活中表现方式的民族志。通过三个田野点——一个社区空间、一个自行车工坊和一个有争议的遗产运动——我们展示了物质文化、争议和关怀作为城市生活中学习过程构成要素的重要性。通过这些例子，我们旨在将城市尺度上学习复杂性的问题重新框定为情感驱动知识以及技能和日常实践的物质性、具身传递的一部分。通过追踪学习在日常生活如何展开，我们可以开始审视超越新自由主义形式的教育治理之外发生了什么，以及日常实践在多大程度上挑战或强化了自上而下的构想，并可能改变知识生产的形式。

title: The Unfinished Lampposts: The (anti‐) Politics of the Amsterdam Smart Lighting Project
abstract: Abstract Smart city projects across the world are invested with the ideal that smart technological innovation smoothly negotiates the objectives, interests, and moral orientations of many different stakeholders. This article explores the politics of this ideal of “smart seamlessness” by taking a close look at the unfolding of the Amsterdam Smart Lighting project undertaken by a consortium of civic, academic, and corporate partners at a square in Amsterdam Southeast. This project envisioned the “smartening up” of lampposts on the square by making them real‐time adaptive to local conditions. As these plans were only partially realized due to a multitude of institutional, cultural, and material frictions, the materiality of the perpetually “unfinished smart lampposts” was subject to a constant interplay of shifting understandings regarding their social, political, and technological significance. Whereas the formal narrative of the project suggests this process of meaning‐making to be fully inclusive, producing “learnings” for all participants, the article contrasts this strategic and explicit inclusivity with the implicit “action orientation” (Haughton et al. 2013) of the project. While the Smart Lighting project’s narrative explicitly gestures toward open and inclusive innovation, it produced more implicit and subtle markers of exclusion that alienated those participants unfamiliar with the jargon, style, and pace of market‐oriented forms of spatial development.
title_zh: 未完成的路灯：阿姆斯特丹智能照明项目的（反）政治
abstract_zh: 世界各地的智慧城市项目都怀有一个理想，即智能技术创新能够顺利协调众多不同利益相关者的目标、利益和道德取向。本文通过仔细审视阿姆斯特丹东南部一个广场上由公民、学术和企业合作伙伴组成的联合体开展的“阿姆斯特丹智能照明”项目的展开过程，探讨了这种“智能无缝”理想的政治。该项目设想通过使广场上的路灯实时适应当地条件来“智能化”它们。由于制度、文化和物质摩擦的多重原因，这些计划仅部分实现，因此永远“未完成的智能路灯”的物质性经历了对其社会、政治和技术意义的不断变化的理解的持续相互作用。尽管项目的正式叙事表明这一意义建构过程是完全包容的，为所有参与者创造了“学习”，但文章将这种战略性和明确的包容性与项目隐含的“行动导向”（Haughton等人2013）进行了对比。虽然智能照明项目的叙事明确指向开放和包容的创新，但它产生了更微妙和隐含的排斥标记，使那些不熟悉以市场为导向的空间发展形式的行话、风格和节奏的参与者感到疏离。

title: Transformation and the Satisfaction of Work
abstract: This article suggests a new conceptual framework for understanding why some types of work are experienced in more satisfying ways than others. The analysis is based on research in an Indian scrap metal yard, where work entails disassembling things that other people no longer want. In spite of the demanding conditions of the labor and the social stigma attached to it, employees express satisfaction with the work process. This observation raises questions about theories of labor, which see satisfaction as arising from work that is creative, skilled, and task-based. The article argues that transformation is a social process that should be used as the primary analytic for explaining work satisfaction. Theories of creativity, skill, and task are secondary analytics that describe subsets of transformative action.
title_zh: 转型与工作满意度
abstract_zh: 本文提出了一个新的概念框架，用于理解为什么某些类型的工作比其他工作更能令人满意。该分析基于对印度一个废金属场的研究，那里的工作涉及拆卸他人不再需要的东西。尽管劳动条件苛刻且带有社会污名，员工仍对工作过程表示满意。这一观察结果引发了对劳动理论的疑问，这些理论认为满意度源于创造性、技能性和任务性的工作。文章认为，转型是一种社会过程，应作为解释工作满意度的主要分析工具。创造力、技能和任务理论是描述转型行动子集的次要分析工具。

title: Under Construction: Technologies of Development in Ethiopia by Daniel Mains
abstract: Reviewed by: Under Construction: Technologies of Development in Ethiopia by Daniel Mains Jon Abbink Daniel Mains, Under Construction: Technologies of Development in Ethiopia. Durham: Duke University Press, 2019. 240 pp. The basic argument of this finely crafted ethnographic study is that "construction" in a developing country—in this case Ethiopia—is a multidimensional phenomenon of both a material and symbolic nature, and fraught with both progress or infrastructural improvements as well as disruption and destruction. Daniel Mains has highlighted these two poles in their interactive entanglements in the daily lives of ordinary Ethiopians in urban settings. He specifically approaches construction as a "site for exploring everyday encounters between citizens, the state, and infrastructural technologies" (2). Under Construction is based on in-depth fieldwork in Ethiopia, a self-designated "developmental" state and a country going through a major phase of political, economic, and social reconstruction, not to say upheaval. Indeed, the country's government over the past two decades has been obsessed with development in a quantitative sense: more roads, more power lines, more buildings, more concrete as prime measurement of progress (with one Minister some time ago boasting about the "developmental achievement" of a record m3 of concrete poured out during the preceding budget year). Mains's work has a relevant but light theoretical touch, inspired by neo-Marxism and postmodern political studies of governance, and connects to a recent but rapidly growing scholarly tradition of infrastructural studies: of technologies, roads, monumental buildings/projects, or transport systems. Much attention is (rightly) paid to "productive inequalities" (the dynamics of which are best described in the chapter on the Bajaj, the motorcycle taxi, see below), and to the interaction of people, labor, state officers, and the material elements of change—the stones, asphalt, [End Page 529] concrete, dust, machines, water in stagnant or flowing form, fuel, and mud. Throughout the book, the analysis of "temporalities" is key, referring to the rhythms, expectations, and practices of change, produced by the interaction of state construction activities with people's engagements and responses to them in their own lives. Mains convincingly demonstrates that focusing on "construction" provides an ideal framework to understand such temporal changes. One of the strengths of this book is indeed the fine-grained exploration of how such infrastructural works, planned and executed (though not always completed) by a dirigiste (ambitious) state are interpreted and responded to by citizens—i.e. how they "navigate" the challenges and disruptive effects in their quotidian routines and their livelihood strategies. "Construction" often comes as part of a wider—political—package that attempts to build or reconstruct "legitimacy" for the state, as Mains demonstrates most clearly in his first chapter on the building of the mammoth Blue Nile hydro-electricity dam in Ethiopia (the "Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam," or GERD), started under the autocratic first prime minister of federal Ethiopia, Meles Zenawi (in power in 1991–2012). In his analysis, Mains connects to some core themes, often made in the literature, on state legitimacy building, problematic planning in the face of strategies of subversion and "adaptation," and people's covert resistance, but his case material is good and original and analyzed in a perceptive and phenomenological style. He illustrates his account with a number of sometimes pretty dismal photographs of blocked, torn-up roads and mud pools, and of propagandistic state posters of grand projects, but also of nice finished traffic lanes, and of people working on the cobblestone roads. Unfortunately, the chapter on the Bajaj has no pictures. The book has five core chapters—which were also published earlier as journal articles, but are well-connected—that share a focus on innovative, indeed transformative, developmental technologies: the large GERD hydro-electric dam (still under construction); urban asphalt road building and its impact on individual lives and communities; the "affective" dimensions of urban development, in that the state evokes attachment or rejection of citizens; the three-wheel motorcycle taxis (the Bajaj) and their attempted "governance" by city authorities in Hawassa; and the massive cobblestone road building enterprise. The arena of all five cases is urban (the cities of Jimma and Hawassa); the methods and the reporting are qualitative. [End Page 530] The main interpretive argument...
title_zh: 施工中：埃塞俄比亚的发展技术
abstract_zh: 书评：丹尼尔·梅因斯的《施工中：埃塞俄比亚的发展技术》。乔恩·阿宾克评述。达勒姆：杜克大学出版社，2019年。240页。这部精心创作的民族志研究的基本论点是，发展中国家的“建设”是一个涉及物质和象征双重维度的多维现象，既伴随着进步或基础设施改善，也伴随着破坏和毁灭。丹尼尔·梅因斯在城市环境中普通埃塞俄比亚人的日常生活中突出了这两个极端及其相互纠缠。他特别将建设视为“探索公民、国家与基础设施技术之间日常遭遇的场所”（2）。《施工中》基于在埃塞俄比亚的深入田野调查，该国是一个自称为“发展型”的国家，正处于政治、经济和社会重建（甚至可以说是动荡）的重要阶段。事实上，过去二十年该国政府痴迷于数量意义上的发展：更多道路、更多电线、更多建筑、更多混凝土，作为进步的主要衡量标准（不久前一位部长曾吹嘘上一个预算年度浇筑了创纪录的立方米混凝土这一“发展成就”）。梅因斯的作品具有相关但轻松的理论触角，受新马克思主义和后现代政治治理研究的启发，并与近期迅速增长的基础设施研究学术传统相联系：涉及技术、道路、纪念性建筑/项目或交通系统。书中相当大篇幅（正确地）关注“生产性不平等”（其动态在关于Bajaj（摩托车出租车）的章节中有最佳描述，见下文），以及人、劳动、国家官员与变化的物质要素——石头、沥青、混凝土、灰尘、机器、静止或流动的水、燃料和泥浆——之间的互动。整本书中，对“时间性”的分析是关键，指的是变化的节奏、期望和实践，这些由国家建设活动与人们在自身生活中对它们的参与和回应之间的互动产生。梅因斯令人信服地证明，聚焦于“建设”为理解这种时间性变化提供了理想框架。本书的优势之一正是细致入微地探索了由干预主义（雄心勃勃的）国家规划和执行（尽管并非总能完成）的基础设施工程如何被公民解读和回应——即他们如何在日常惯例和生计策略中“应对”挑战和破坏性影响。“建设”往往作为更广泛的政治一揽子计划的一部分出现，该计划试图建立或重建国家的“合法性”，正如梅因斯在关于埃塞俄比亚蓝尼罗河巨型水电站大坝（“埃塞俄比亚复兴大坝”或GERD）建设的第一章中最清晰展示的那样，该大坝在联邦埃塞俄比亚的第一位独裁总理梅莱斯·泽纳维（1991-2012年在位）领导下启动。在分析中，梅因斯联系到文献中经常出现的一些核心主题：国家合法性建设、面对颠覆和“适应”策略的问题规划，以及人们的隐性抵抗。但他的案例材料出色且原创，并以敏锐的现象学风格进行分析。他用一些有时相当阴郁的照片来阐述他的叙述：被堵塞、撕裂的道路和泥潭，以及宣传国家宏大项目的海报，但也有漂亮的完工车道，以及人们在鹅卵石路上工作的场景。遗憾的是，关于Bajaj的章节没有图片。本书有五章核心内容——这些章节也曾作为期刊文章发表，但彼此联系紧密——都聚焦于创新甚至变革性的发展技术：大型GERD水电站大坝（仍在建设中）；城市沥青道路建设及其对个人生活和社区的影响；城市发展的“情感”维度（即国家唤起公民的依恋或排斥）；三轮摩托车出租车（Bajaj）及其由哈瓦萨市当局试图进行的“治理”；以及大规模的鹅卵石道路建设企业。五个案例的舞台都是城市（吉马和哈瓦萨市）；方法和报告都是定性的。主要解释性论证……

title: Waiting for accelerations. Speculating on guar seeds in the Indian desert
abstract: This article unfolds how an extreme acceleration in the price of a seed in 2012 changed farming in a rural area of India by reorienting the imagined sources of wealth in farming. The seed in question is guar which have been grown for centuries for cow fodder, but which is also used in fracking, and because of a growing international demand combined with a limited supply and wild speculation, the prices in 2012 grew exponentially with 1500% in a period of 3 months, after which it crashed at a similar rate. The article argues that this acceleration of prices caused an escalation that changed the perspective of change for farmers. it shifted the main focus from farming as a repetitive event tied to the seasonal weather changes, to one of future potentiality tied to sudden market movements. This shift in the scale of measuring change in farming moved farmers from producing seeds to also speculating in seeds, through methods of trading and stocking. The guar price acceleration opened up to imaginaries of new avenues of future income from farming that was not flowing in with the rain, but with the market.
title_zh: 等待加速：印度沙漠中的瓜尔豆种子投机
abstract_zh: 本文阐述了2012年一种种子价格的极端加速如何通过重新定位农业财富的想象来源，改变了印度农村地区的农业。这种种子是瓜尔豆，几个世纪以来一直用作牛饲料，但也用于水力压裂。由于国际需求增长、供应有限以及疯狂投机，2012年价格在3个月内呈指数级增长1500%，之后又以类似速度暴跌。文章认为，这种价格加速引发了升级，改变了农民对变化的看法。它将主要焦点从作为与季节性天气变化相关的重复事件的农业，转向了与市场突变相关的未来潜力。这种衡量农业变化的尺度的转变，使农民从生产种子转向通过交易和储存来投机种子。瓜尔豆价格加速开启了对农业未来收入新途径的想象，这些收入不再随雨水而来，而是随市场而来。

title: Beyond factory safety: labor unions, militant protest, and the accelerated ambitions of Bangladesh’s export garment industry
abstract: This article explores the relationship between labor unions and labor precarity in Bangladesh’s garment industry. After a string of high-profile factory disasters—including the 2013 collapse of the Rana Plaza garment factory building—Bangladeshi labor unions have played a central role in new global initiatives to improve factory safety. These initiatives have provided an opportunity for unions to influence the governance of labor standards in a context of low levels of factory unionization. We argue that such global initiatives have deepened an existing divide between the conciliatory stance of mainstream, politically connected Bangladeshi unions and workers’ more radical responses to precarity. Militant protests have advanced workers’ interests historically, but are increasingly delegitimized and subject to violent crackdowns. This article contributes to our understanding of the fraught relationship between precarious workers and traditional labor unions by showing that when unions devote themselves to the technocratic improvement of labor standards without confronting the structural conditions of precarity itself, workers can be made more vulnerable—a situation that becomes heightened in a context of fast industrial expansion.
title_zh: 超越工厂安全：孟加拉国出口服装业的工会、激进抗议与加速的野心
keywords_zh: 工厂（面向对象程序设计）
abstract_zh: 本文探讨了孟加拉国服装业中工会与劳工不稳定性之间的关系。在发生一系列引人注目的工厂灾难（包括2013年拉纳广场服装厂大楼倒塌）之后，孟加拉国工会已在改善工厂安全的新的全球倡议中发挥核心作用。这些倡议为工会提供了在工厂工会化水平低下的背景下影响劳工标准治理的机会。我们认为，此类全球倡议加深了主流、有政治联系的孟加拉国工会的调和立场与工人对不稳定性更激进的回应之间已有的鸿沟。历史上，激进抗议曾促进工人利益，但如今越来越被非法化并遭受暴力镇压。本文通过展示当工会致力于技术官僚式的劳工标准改进而不直面不稳定性本身的结构性条件时，工人可能变得更加脆弱——这种情况在工业快速扩张的背景下变得更加严重，从而有助于我们理解不稳定工人与传统工会之间充满困扰的关系。

title: Bottleneck: Moving, Building, and Belonging in an African City by Caroline Melly
abstract: Reviewed by: Bottleneck: Moving, Building, and Belonging in an African City by Caroline Melly Michael Degani Caroline Melly, Bottleneck: Moving, Building, and Belonging in an African City. Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 2017. 224 pp. In this lucid and well-written ethnography, Caroline Melly asks us to consider the problems of mobility that arise in mid-2000s Dakar and in African urban life more broadly. This is an extended post-structural adjustment period in which high levels of GDP growth, splashy foreign investment, and massive state-sponsored construction projects offset the ordinary and long-running malaise of urban life for the majority poor. Bottleneck thus contributes to a rich literature on Africa "afterwards"—after the Cold War (Piot 2010) and after development (Ferguson 2006)—where socioeconomic inequality and its spatial logic of borders and enclaves sort out the winners and losers, and render passage between the two ever more fraught and miraculous. Melly deftly evokes this pressurized suspension through the concept of embouteillage, or bottleneck, which is at once a writerly metaphor and a "scholarly device" (128). In this sense it is very much what Dominic Boyer and Cymene Howe (2015) call a "portable analytic," a concept that can capture certain experiences and (somewhat ironically, in this case) move easily across different ethnographic domains. Yet the term, Melly suggests, is no mere contrivance, but is rooted in the ethnographic realities of endless traffic jams (Chapter 2); half-finished, remittance-financed, "inside-out houses" (Chapter 3); and clandestine migration to Europe (Chapter 5). She encountered these issues during her time as an intern at the downtown offices of APIX, Senegal's national investment promotion agency, quixotically tasked with courting the largely mythical figure of the entrepreneurial "migrant investor" (Chapter 4). Thinking about these various sites as bottlenecked gets at the sense that there are imaginable futures to aspire to, but getting to them is constricted and unpredictable. [End Page 259] For Dakarois, positioned at a longstanding "cosmopolitan crossroads" of global flow, mobility is as elusive as it is crucial (4). Given its concern with mobility and circulation, infrastructure is an important leitmotif of the book. The 2000s were indeed in many respects the infrastructure decade, with massive new investments soaking up foreign capital and contributing to the hype around "Africa Rising." But the often-spectacular poetics and promises of these mega-projects belie the cruddiness of aging public provisioning systems that were laid down during the post-independence era of the "salary man" (32). Hence, referencing the work of Julie Chu (2014), Melly demonstrates what it means to "[think] infrastructurally" (11)—to attend to the daily logistics that give Dakar its particular and often frustrating sense of collective experience. "Et les embouteillage?" (And how are the bottlenecks?). This question, Melly reports, was folded into the texture of daily life, a pleasantry with which to greet friends and fellow urbanites (6). In a certain sense, to "think infrastructurally" is to try and see what is in front of our eyes—the often taken-for-granted activities of "moving, building, and belonging" in an African city. On this count, Chapter 2 features a wonderful discussion of the cab driver, or "taksimann," as the workhorse of bottlenecked urban mobility in Dakar, a figure that one development worker smugly dismissed as a means to researching urban migration, but not an end—not a source of knowledge about migration itself. To the contrary, taxi drivers, who often rent vehicles owned by more successful migrants, both endure the narrow side of the bottleneck and make the best of it, boning up on English and French while stuck in traffic, and diversifying their services to include tours and other sorts of errands. This chapter also speaks to Melly's refreshing directness as an ethnographer. It is surely an open secret that taxi drivers, with their Muchona the Hornetesque liminality, have long been charismatic and irresistible interlocutors for anthropologists (Turner 1967). Melly thus shows the benefits of taking them seriously in a world of congested cities. It is in these descriptions of the creative arrangements that happen at the bottleneck, rather than of the bottleneck itself, that the book is perhaps strongest, bridging the seemingly divergent trajectories of rich...
title_zh: 瓶颈：在非洲城市的迁移、建造与归属
abstract_zh: 这本清晰且文笔优美的民族志由卡罗琳·梅利撰写，要求我们思考21世纪初达喀尔以及更广泛的非洲城市生活中出现的流动性问题。这是一个结构调整后的延长时期，高GDP增长、炫目的外国投资和大型国家资助的建设项目抵消了大多数穷人在城市生活中的日常和长期不满。《瓶颈》因此为关于“之后”的非洲——冷战后（Piot 2010）和发展后（Ferguson 2006）——的丰富文献做出了贡献，其中社会经济不平等及其空间逻辑（边界和飞地）区分了赢家和输家，并使两者之间的通道更加艰难和不可思议。梅利通过“embouteillage”（瓶颈）的概念巧妙地唤起了这种受压的悬置状态，这既是一种写作者隐喻，也是一种“学术工具”（128）。在这个意义上，它非常符合多米尼克·博耶和赛敏·豪（2015）所称的“便携分析”，一个能够捕捉某些体验并且（有些讽刺的是，在这种情况下）能轻松跨越不同民族志领域的概念。然而，梅利认为，这个词并非单纯的虚构，而是植根于无尽的交通堵塞（第二章）、半成品且由汇款资助的“里外颠倒的房子”（第三章）以及秘密移民到欧洲（第五章）的民族志现实。她在塞内加尔国家投资促进机构APIX市中心的办公室实习期间遇到了这些问题，该机构不切实际地负责吸引几乎神话般的“移民投资者”企业家（第四章）。将这些不同的场所视为瓶颈，有助于理解存在着可以憧憬的未来，但到达这些未来的道路狭窄且不可预测。[第259页] 对于达喀尔人来说，他们处于全球流动的长期“世界主义十字路口”，流动性既难以捉摸又至关重要（4）。鉴于其对流动性和循环的关注，基础设施是本书的一个重要主题。21世纪初在某种意义上确实是基础设施的十年，大规模的新投资吸收了外国资本，并助长了“非洲崛起”的炒作。但这些大型项目通常壮观的诗意和承诺掩盖了后独立时代“工薪族”（32）时期建立的老化公共供应系统的破旧。因此，引用朱莉·朱（2014）的研究，梅利展示了“从基础设施角度思考”（11）意味着什么——关注那些使达喀尔具有独特且常常令人沮丧的集体体验感的日常物流。“Et les embouteillage？”（瓶颈怎么样了？）梅利报告说，这个问题融入了日常生活的纹理，成为一种问候朋友和城市居民的客套话（6）。从某种意义上说，“从基础设施角度思考”就是试图看清我们眼前的东西——非洲城市中那些常常被视为理所当然的“迁移、建造和归属”活动。在这方面，第二章精彩地讨论了出租车司机（或“taksimann”）作为达喀尔瓶颈城市交通的主力，一个被某发展工作者蔑视为研究城市迁移的手段而非目的——不是关于迁移本身的知识来源——的人物。相反，出租车司机通常租用更成功的移民拥有的车辆，他们既要忍受瓶颈的狭窄一面，又要充分利用它，在堵车时学习英语和法语，并使其服务多样化，包括旅游和其他差事。这一章也体现了梅利作为民族志学者的直接性。出租车司机以其类似于穆乔纳·霍内特的阈限性，长期以来一直是人类学家眼中具有魅力且不可抗拒的对话者，这无疑是一个公开的秘密（Turner 1967）。因此，梅利展示了在一个拥堵城市的世界里重视他们的好处。正是在这些对发生在瓶颈处的创造性安排（而非瓶颈本身）的描述中，这本书或许最为出色，它连接了看似不同的轨迹……

title: Cameras at Work: Dusty Lenses and Processed Videos in the Quarries of Hyderabad
abstract: Ethnographic filmmakers have always looked for new ways to record lives. Drawing from Gilbert Simondon’s ideas on technology, this article explores the technical conditions of filmmaking through the materiality of environments, digital and optical devices, recording formats, and human actions. It considers the work of cameras as participants in the stone quarries of Hyderabad (Telangana, India), and discusses how infrastructures of digital videos are hacked and acted upon. This article suggests that to contribute to theories in visual anthropology, and understand practices of ethnographic filmmaking, we need to reveal how cameras work with filmmakers, but also through them.
title_zh: 工作中的相机：海得拉巴采石场中的布满灰尘的镜头与处理过的视频
abstract_zh: 民族志电影制作人一直在寻找记录生活的新方法。借鉴吉尔伯特·西蒙东关于技术的观点，本文通过环境、数字和光学设备、录制格式以及人类行为的物质性来探讨电影制作的技术条件。文章将相机视为印度特伦甘纳邦海得拉巴石矿的参与者，并讨论了数字视频基础设施如何被破解和操纵。本文认为，为了对视觉人类学理论做出贡献，并理解民族志电影制作的实践，我们需要揭示相机如何与电影制作人合作，同时也通过他们来运作。

title: CARAVANS OF THE NORTH: A COMPARISON OF 20 th C CARAVANS IN NORTHERN CANADA AND NORTHERN CHILE
abstract: An examination of the historic caravans of northern Canada in the 20 th c reveals compelling historical, technological, economic, social, political, and kinship comparisons to the developments of caravans in northern Chile in the 20 th c. In Canada, the transport of goods across the northern reaches of the prairie provinces was spurred by mining and logging interests, and began with horses and donkeys, subsequently shifting to gasoline engine power when they became available, via "cat (caterpillar tractor) freight sleighs". In northern Chile, camelid caravans had been replaced in many instances by horse and donkey caravans to haul the goods required for mining copper and nitrate. As vehicles became available, the horse and donkey caravans were replaced at the same time that roads were built, often along the same trails that had been used by animal caravans for hundreds and thousands of years. While rapid and convenient vehicle transport is widely available in both Canada and Chile, transport that is dependent upon and limited by specific environmental parameters has not been universally replaced, and continues to fill important social, economic, political, and behavioural roles that can be considered in reviewing and reconstructing ancient caravan lifeways.
title_zh: 北方的商队：加拿大北部与智利北部20世纪商队比较
abstract_zh: 对20世纪加拿大北部历史商队的考察揭示了与20世纪智利北部商队发展在历史、技术、经济、社会、政治和亲属关系方面的引人注目的比较。在加拿大，横跨草原省份北部地区的货物运输由采矿和伐木利益驱动，最初使用马和驴，随后在可获取时转向汽油发动机动力，通过“猫（履带式拖拉机）货运雪橇”进行。在智利北部，骆驼科动物商队在多种情况下已被马和驴商队取代，以运输铜和硝酸盐开采所需的货物。随着车辆的出现，马和驴商队在修建道路的同时被取代，这些道路通常沿着动物商队已经使用了成百上千年的同一路线。尽管在加拿大和智利，快速便捷的车辆运输已广泛可用，但依赖于特定环境参数并受其限制的运输并未被普遍取代，并且继续在考虑和重建古代商队生活方式中可以发挥重要的社会、经济、政治和行为角色。

title: Data centers as infrastructural in‐betweens:
abstract: ABSTRACT On Iceland's Reykjanes peninsula, a new industry is taking root in the ruins of a US military base: digital data storage. The new data centers, where transnational corporations pay to store terabytes of information, have been lauded as transformative for the region. But as they engage the military base's physical infrastructures, spatial orders, and affective resonances, they reprise and cement Reykjanes's former role as an infrastructural in‐between : a node in others’ networks, both built in and left out. Thus, while digital networks are often imagined as overcoming marginality through the “death of distance” or “compression of space‐time,” their layering amid imperial legacies means that on Reykjanes they perpetuate marginality. These conditions illustrate the unevenly emplaced impacts of cloud computing and unsettle the techno‐utopian ideal of connectivity. [ infrastructure, information technology, data centers, militarism, intermediarity, marginality, Iceland ]
title_zh: 作为基础设施中间节点的数据中心
abstract_zh: 摘要：在冰岛雷克雅内斯半岛，一个新兴行业正在美国军事基地的废墟中扎根：数字数据存储。跨国公司付费存储海量信息的新数据中心被誉为该地区的变革力量。然而，当它们利用军事基地的物理基础设施、空间秩序和情感共鸣时，它们重演并固化了雷克雅内斯作为基础设施中间节点的旧角色——既是他人网络中的一个节点，又既被建设又被排斥。因此，尽管数字网络常被想象为通过“距离的消失”或“时空压缩”克服边缘性，但它们与帝国遗产的交织意味着在雷克雅内斯，它们反而延续了边缘性。这些条件揭示了云计算的不均衡嵌入影响，并动摇了技术乌托邦式的连接理想。[基础设施、信息技术、数据中心、军事主义、中间性、边缘性、冰岛]

title: Frame, Game, and Circuit: Truth and the Human in Japanese Human-machine Interface Research
abstract: This essay tracks the ‘human’ emergent in human-centred technologies (HCTs) in Japan. A primary aim of HCTs is to extract the true intention of the user and actualise it as machine action. Beyond this, HCT researchers maintained that creating such technologies would give them access to the truth of the human itself. In this essay, I examine the games of truth played in HCT, in which teachers exercise authority over students by defining their true intentions for them, and students learned what they needed to become good researchers. I then show how through analogical relations, human subjects with esteemed qualities became what HCTs must be, and HCTs a means for imagining what human beings truly are. What emerged were truths that transcended human and machine: all are systems of information and, in the end, the right machine can approach humanity enough to fulfil even the most human of responsibilities.
title_zh: 框架、游戏与电路：日本人机界面研究中的真理与人类
abstract_zh: 本文追踪了日本以人为中心的技术（HCT）中涌现的“人类”。HCT的一个主要目标是提取用户的真实意图并将其实现为机器行动。除此之外，HCT研究者坚持认为，创造这样的技术将使他们能够触及人类本身的真相。在本文中，我考察了HCT中进行的真理游戏，其中教师通过为学生定义其真实意图来行使权威，而学生则学习成为优秀研究者所需的技能。然后，我展示了通过类比关系，具有受尊敬品质的人类主体变成了HCT必须成为的样子，而HCT则成为想象人类真正面目的手段。涌现出的真理超越了人类和机器：一切都是信息系统，最终，正确的机器可以足够接近人性，以履行甚至最人性化的责任。

title: Kenya and China's labour relations: infrastructural development for whom, by whom?
abstract: Abstract The Kenyan government's long-term development strategy, Vision 2030, has emphasized infrastructural investments, which it believes will lead to sustained economic growth. The government has appealed to China to fund large-scale projects in the transport sector, and as a consequence of this, construction firms from China have emerged as significant employers in the country. While the Kenyan government contends with the ongoing burden of youth unemployment, it must also reconcile the ambiguities of China's role in Africa and its implications for the labour market. This article examines two Chinese-built infrastructure projects in Kenya and their intersection with several issues involving migrant labour and local rumours of Chinese prisoners, as well as the state's vision for industrialization and youth employment. Kenyans utilize both online and interpersonal channels of discourse to critique present-day employment practices in the transport sector, and it is argued that these counter-channels of discourse represent a particular articulation of knowledge used by Kenyans to construct meaning and interpret ambiguous situations. Through a theoretical analysis of rumour, this article illustrates how ordinary Kenyans are pooling their intellectual resources to understand Sino-Kenyan labour relations in the absence of transparency and participatory government processes in the infrastructure sector.
title_zh: 肯尼亚与中国的劳动关系：为谁、由谁进行的基础设施建设？
abstract_zh: 摘要 肯尼亚政府的长期发展战略《愿景2030》强调基础设施投资，认为这将带来持续的经济增长。政府已向中国寻求资金用于交通领域的大型项目，因此中国建筑公司成为该国的重要雇主。在肯尼亚政府应对青年失业问题的同时，也必须调和中国在非洲角色的模糊性及其对劳动力市场的影响。本文考察了肯尼亚两个由中国建造的基础设施项目，以及它们与涉及移民劳工和当地关于中国囚犯的谣言等多个问题的交集，同时涉及国家对工业化和青年就业的愿景。肯尼亚人利用线上和线下的对话渠道来批评当前交通部门的就业实践，本文认为这些反向的对话渠道代表了肯尼亚人用来构建意义和解释模糊情境的一种特殊知识表达。通过谣言的理论分析，本文展示了普通肯尼亚人如何在基础设施部门缺乏透明度和参与性政府过程的情况下，汇集他们的知识资源来理解中肯劳动关系。

title: Managing Dirt: Disciplines of Cleanliness and Contamination at a Kentucky Auto Parts Factory
abstract: A legacy of coal mining and manufacturing work in Appalachia has linked regional working-class identity and perceptions of the region to shared experiences of dangerous and stigmatised dirty work. At the same time, manufacturing work here increasingly relies on computerised machinery, systematised practices of cleanliness, and ties to global corporations. This paper, based on 18 months of ethnographic field research explores practices of cleanliness and contamination at a multinational auto parts manufacturing plant in Appalachian Kentucky – a region whose labour history is closely intertwined with ideologies of dirt, class, and moral reform. Findings show that workers negotiate belonging and class identity through strategies of embracing or avoiding dirt and performing practices and personas of cleanliness at work. I argue that lean manufacturing ideals of cleanliness, and their negotiation, intersect with larger discourses of dirty work in Appalachia and the US South to reproduce local ideologies and symbolic categories of class difference.
title_zh: 管理污垢：肯塔基州一家汽车零部件工厂的清洁与污染规范
abstract_zh: 阿巴拉契亚地区煤矿开采和制造业工作的历史遗产，将地区工人阶级身份和对该地区的认知与危险且被污名化的肮脏工作的共同经历联系起来。同时，这里的制造业工作越来越依赖计算机化机械、系统化的清洁实践以及与全球公司的联系。本文基于18个月的民族志田野研究，探讨了肯塔基州阿巴拉契亚地区一家跨国汽车零部件制造厂的清洁与污染实践——该地区的劳动历史与污垢、阶级和道德改革的意识形态紧密交织。研究结果表明，工人通过接受或回避污垢的策略以及在工作中表现清洁实践和角色来协商归属感和阶级身份。我认为，精益制造所倡导的清洁理想及其协商，与阿巴拉契亚和美国南部更广泛的肮脏工作话语相互交织，从而再生产了地方意识形态和阶级差异的象征性范畴。

title: Oligopolistic suppliers, symbiotic value chains and workers' bargaining power: labour contestation in South China at an ascendant global footwear firm
journal_name: GLOBAL NETWORKS-A JOURNAL OF TRANSNATIONAL AFFAIRS
abstract: Abstract In this article, I analyse changes in the power relationship between lead firms, manufacturers and workers by examining a strike that took place in South China in 2014 among workers at the Taiwanese footwear giant, Yue Yuen. In the process, I demonstrate that there is a link between increased labour costs, capital consolidation and greater value capture at the bottom of the global supply chain. I argue that footwear value chains are seeing a falling level of monopsony power and the emergence of enormous oligopolistic suppliers, which are transforming the power imbalances of global supply chains towards a more mutually dependent ‘buyer–producer symbiosis’. The Yue Yuen strike shows a maturing industrial working class, facing pressures on social reproduction in China, adapting its bargaining strategies vis‐à‐vis the developmental state. Influxes of profit raise the ceiling for what can be demanded of employers, stimulating those same employers to pursue more aggressive means of holding onto their profits. The example of the Yue Yuen strike is an indicator of what are fundamental changes in the production process, dynamics within the value chain, and power and agency of workers in labour‐intensive production. The strike demonstrates that consolidation is playing a decisive role in shaping the power relationship between domestic manufacturers and transnational brands, which, in turn, is directly affecting the bargaining power of workers.
title_zh: 寡头供应商、共生价值链与工人议价能力：华南一家崛起的全球鞋业公司的劳工抗争
abstract_zh: 在本文中，我通过分析2014年华南地区台资制鞋巨头裕元（Yue Yuen）工人发生的罢工，探讨了主导企业、制造商与工人之间权力关系的变化。在此过程中，我论证了劳动力成本上升、资本整合与全球供应链底层价值捕获增加之间的联系。我认为，制鞋价值链正在经历买方垄断力量的下降以及巨大的寡头供应商的出现，这正在将全球供应链的权力失衡转变为更加相互依赖的'买方-生产者共生关系'。裕元罢工显示出一个成熟的产业工人阶级，面临中国社会再生产的压力，正在调整其针对发展型国家的议价策略。利润的涌入提高了对雇主提出要求的空间，同时也刺激这些雇主采取更激进的手段来保住利润。裕元罢工的例子表明了劳动密集型生产中生产过程、价值链动态以及工人权力和能动性发生的根本性变化。该罢工表明，整合在塑造国内制造商与跨国品牌之间的权力关系方面发挥着决定性作用，而这又直接影响工人的议价能力。

title: Panlongcheng, Zhengzhou and the Movement of Metal in Early Bronze Age China
abstract: Abstract The role of Panlongcheng—a walled settlement on the Yangtze River with obvious links to the Erligang capital at Zhengzhou, ~ 500 km to the north—in early Bronze Age China has been the subject of much debate. Panlongcheng is a typical Erligang site (~ 1500–1300 BC), with evidence for people of elite status, unlike any other site apart from Zhengzhou itself. The tombs and bronzes at Panlongcheng, as well as other materials, closely resemble those at Zhengzhou. Why was Panlongcheng established along the Yangtze River, and what were the Erligang elites doing there? Considering the rich copper deposits in this area, it is widely assumed that the major function of Panlongcheng was to ship metal to Zhengzhou, and in return to receive bronze vessels from Zhengzhou. The purpose of this paper is to revisit this discussion through a re-evaluation of the scientific data on the bronzes from each site. A series of differences and similarities in the chemical and isotopic compositions of the metal objects at Panlongcheng and Zhengzhou are identified, suggesting that the relationship was more complex than was previously thought. In this light, despite a close social and presumably political affiliation with Zhengzhou, Panlongcheng appears likely to have had its own metal-casting capability, rather than having to rely completely on finished objects imported from Zhengzhou. This discovery encourages scholars to re-consider the metal supply network and the underlying political landscape in early dynastic China, shifting from a linear model to a complex but probably more realistic one.
title_zh: 盘龙城、郑州与早期中国青铜时代的金属流动
abstract_zh: 摘要 盘龙城——长江流域一个与郑州二里岗都城（相距约500公里）有明显联系的城墙聚落——在早期中国青铜时代中的作用一直是许多争论的主题。盘龙城是典型的二里岗遗址（约公元前1500-1300年），有精英地位人群的证据，这一点除郑州外其他遗址均不具备。盘龙城的墓葬、青铜器以及其他材料与郑州的非常相似。为何盘龙城要建立在长江沿岸？二里岗精英在那里做什么？考虑到该地区丰富的铜矿资源，普遍认为盘龙城的主要功能是将金属运往郑州，并作为交换接收来自郑州的青铜容器。本文旨在通过重新评估两地青铜器的科学数据来重新审视这一讨论。盘龙城和郑州金属物体的化学和同位素组成存在一系列差异和相似之处，表明这种关系比先前认为的更为复杂。由此看来，尽管盘龙城与郑州有密切的社会和政治联系，但似乎拥有自己的金属铸造能力，而非完全依赖从郑州输入的成品。这一发现鼓励学者重新考虑早期王朝中国的金属供应网络及其背后的政治格局，从线性模型转向复杂但可能更现实的模型。

title: Photographies in Africa in the digital age
abstract: In recent years, all kinds of African photographies, both on the continent and in the diaspora, have undergone a digital ‘revolution’ (Ekine and Manji 2012). Without doubt, the key driver of this trend has been the rapid, and massive, influx to practically all African countries of ever more affordable third generation/advanced mobile phone handsets, or smartphones. Even compared with earlier technological revolutions on the continent, both the speed and the scale of this spread have been simply breathtaking. For example, the establishment of transistor radio sets – the process through which personal radios became ubiquitous across Africa – occurred over the period of at least a decade and a half (between roughly the late 1950s and the early 1970s). Similarly, the original mobile phone revolution – i.e. the process through which early generation/low functionality mobile phones went from being a source of novelty, to a domain for experimentation, to technologies that were routinized in everyday life, throughout the continent – took more than a decade to unfold (the crucial years being those between roughly 1999 and 2010) (Vokes 2018b). Against both of those earlier processes, the emergence of smartphones occurred over a much shorter timeframe. Between 2011 and mid-2015 alone, the number of smartphones being imported into Africa – the majority of them sub-US$100 Android-based systems – jumped from around 10 million units per annum to almost 100 million (Tshabalala 2015), as a result of which these devices became quickly established as a common feature of everyday life. Today, more than one-third of all mobile phones in Africa are smartphones, and this percentage is set to rise to two-thirds by 2020 (GSMA Intelligence 2017).
title_zh: 数字时代的非洲摄影
abstract_zh: 近年来，在非洲大陆和散居世界各地的各类非洲摄影都经历了一场数字‘革命’（Ekine and Manji 2012）。毫无疑问，这一趋势的关键驱动力是快速且大规模涌入几乎每一个非洲国家的越来越便宜的第三代/高级移动电话手机——即智能手机。即使与早期非洲的技术革命相比，这一传播的速度和规模也令人惊叹。例如，晶体管收音机的普及（个人收音机在非洲普及的过程）至少跨越了十五年（大致在20世纪50年代末到70年代初）。同样，最初的手机革命——即早期低功能手机从新奇事物到实验领域再到日常生活中的常规技术的过程——也用了十多年才展开（关键年份大致在1999年至2010年间）。与这两次早期过程相比，智能手机的出现时间要短得多。仅2011年至2015年年中，非洲进口的智能手机（其中大多数是售价低于100美元的安卓系统手机）数量就从每年约1000万部跃升至近1亿部，这些设备迅速成为日常生活中的常见特征。如今，非洲超过三分之一的手机是智能手机，预计到2020年这一比例将升至三分之二（GSMA Intelligence 2017）。

title: Projects of devotion: energy exploration and moral ambition in the cosmoeconomy of oil and gas in the Western United States
journal_name: JOURNAL OF THE ROYAL ANTHROPOLOGICAL INSTITUTE
abstract: Abstract This essay considers how people working in the oil and gas industry in Colorado perceive their involvement in energy exploration in relation to broader practices of devotion, compassion, and outreach. I argue that although their energy projects may appear to merely echo companies’ formal promotional pitches, the oilfield and corporate actors’ own moral ambitions reveal more‐than‐human cosmoeconomic visions of oil's potentiality. This essay thus demonstrates how multiple and diverging ethical registers intersect and inform the valuation of oil.
title_zh: 虔诚的项目：美国西部油气能源勘探的道德抱负与宇宙经济学
abstract_zh: 本文探讨了科罗拉多州石油和天然气行业的工作人员如何将其参与能源勘探与更广泛的虔诚、同情和外展实践联系起来。我认为，尽管他们的能源项目可能看似只是对公司正式宣传的简单重复，但油田和企业行动者自身的道德抱负揭示了石油潜能的超越人类宇宙经济愿景。因此，本文展示了多种且相互分歧的道德规范如何交汇并影响石油的估值。

title: Racial hair: the persistence and resistance of a category
journal_name: JOURNAL OF THE ROYAL ANTHROPOLOGICAL INSTITUTE
abstract: Abstract This article analyses how hair and race are entangled both within anthropology and in the commercial world of the billion‐dollar global market for human hair. Focusing in particular on detached hair, it explores the recurring dynamic through which hair is racialized, on the one hand, and resists racialization, on the other. This process is traced in three interrelated contexts, the roots of which are embedded in historical conditions of domination and oppression. The first is that of nineteenth‐ and early twentieth‐century physical anthropology, when hair was thought to provide a key to racial distinctions. The second refers to contemporary black hair cultures in which hair is racialized both in the marketplace, where it is advertised through ethnic signifiers, and in the natural hair movement, which relies on ideas of authenticity based on biological differences. The third context is that of factories in China, where items such as ‘Brazilian’ hair extensions and ‘Afro’ wigs are physically manufactured through combinations of hair and labour that confound ethnic, racial, and national boundaries. By shifting attention to the materiality of hair, the article highlights the enduring materiality of race, exposing its shape‐shifting qualities and persistent ideologies and providing a unique angle onto the dynamics of nature‐culture articulations.
title_zh: 种族化的头发：一个类别的持久性与抵抗性
abstract_zh: 摘要 本文分析了头发和种族如何在人类学以及全球数十亿美元的人发商业市场中相互纠缠。特别关注分离的头发，探讨了头发一方面被种族化、另一方面抵抗种族化的反复动态。这一过程在三个相互关联的语境中被追溯，其根源根植于历史上的统治和压迫条件。第一个语境是19世纪和20世纪初的体质人类学，当时头发被认为是种族区别的关键。第二个语境涉及当代黑人头发文化，其中头发在市场中被种族化（通过种族标志进行广告宣传），以及在自然头发运动中，该运动依赖于基于生物差异的真实性观念。第三个语境是中国工厂，在那里，诸如“巴西”发束和“非洲”假发等物品通过头发和劳动的组合被物理制造，这些组合混淆了民族、种族和国家的界限。通过将注意力转向头发的物质性，本文突显了种族的持久物质性，揭示了其变形特质和持久的意识形态，并为自然-文化衔接的动态提供了独特视角。

title: Royal Roads and Entangled Webs: Mining Metals and Making Value in El Cubo, Guanajuato, Mexico
abstract: In this article I study recent struggles in the gold mining town of El Cubo, Guanajuato, Mexico, over what should happen to mining profits. Rather than framing these primarily or only in terms of a chain from production to consumption and periphery to metropole, I explore them as points of intersection, divergent paths, or entangled webs. This knottier perspective, allied to a more expansive theorization of value-making as “the politics of making meaningful difference and making differences meaningful” (as I said in 2013), allows us to see these contests in a new light, as attempts to revalue places close to the mines and people with long-standing connections to those places. By doing this we can recognize the capacities of miners and others in mining communities to create and contest value in the intersections of entangled webs, rather than seeing them only as those left behind in the transfer of value along a commodity chain.
title_zh: 皇家道路与纠缠之网：墨西哥瓜纳华托州埃尔库博的金属开采与价值创造
abstract_zh: 在本文中，我研究了墨西哥瓜纳华托州埃尔库博金矿小镇近期关于采矿利润应如何处理而发生的斗争。我没有将这些斗争主要或仅仅从生产到消费、从边缘到中心链条的角度进行框架化，而是将其探索为交汇点、分叉路径或纠缠之网。这种更纠结的视角，结合对价值创造更扩展的理论化为“制造有意义差异和使差异有意义之政治”（如我在2013年所言），使我们能够以新的视角看待这些抗争，将其视为重新评价靠近矿场的地方以及长期与这些地方有联系的人们所作的努力。通过这样做，我们可以认识到矿工和采矿社区中其他人在纠缠之网的交汇处创造和争夺价值的能力，而不是仅仅将他们视为商品链价值转移中的被遗弃者。

title: Spaceship in the Desert: Energy, Climate Change, and Urban Design in Abu Dhabi by Gökçe Günel
abstract: Reviewed by: Spaceship in the Desert: Energy, Climate Change, and Urban Design in Abu Dhabi by Gökçe Günel Idalina Baptista Gökçe Günel, Spaceship in the Desert: Energy, Climate Change, and Urban Design in Abu Dhabi. Durham: Duke University Press, 2019. 272 pp. Spaceship in the Desert is a timely contribution to a growing field of anthropological scholarship on energy. Günel engages Abu Dhabi’s Masdar City as a site for exploring intersecting concerns over climate change, technology, knowledge production, and uncanny moral paths pursued in the name of sustainable futures. It is full of ethnographic detail based on the author’s time spent in Masdar, as well as attendance at conferences, events, and other insightful conversations related to the experiment. The book seems to integrate expanded versions of a number of previously published articles in its core five chapters, which are brought together by an Introduction and an Epilogue with further reflections on Masdar City’s experiment as a whole. The Introduction familiarizes readers with Masdar City, expands on the book’s key contributions and methodological approach, and provides an outline of the book. It opens with ethnographic vignettes that capture the market-oriented approach that prevailed throughout the (then short) life of this experiment. This much is encapsulated in the chapter’s subtitle— “The Soul of Carbon Dioxide”—a reference to an informant’s attempts at making visible the “soul” of CO2 through monetary terms. Furthermore, the chapter outlines one of its key analytical foci and contribution of the book: what the author calls “technical adjustments.” These consist of experimental tweaks to the energy status quo that foreground technological fixes over a moral and ethical consideration of a future without oil and pervasive consumption. Each subsequent chapter focuses on a different “technical adjustment,” although the narrative does not always return to this broad idea or its theorization. Instead, each one engages with key [End Page 1309] thinking relevant to historicize the “technical adjustment” under analysis. This is quite useful as it contextualizes Masdar’s experiments and their path-dependencies, showing how these are shaped over time by flows of ideas and policies through various networks. Ultimately, Günel seems less concerned with adjudicating on the successes or failures of each “technical adjustment” than she is in exploring the productive tensions found in their potential for invoking an oil-less future. Chapter 1 explores the language of choice to describe Masdar in the years that followed the project’s launch in 2006. It draws on futuristic imagery from science fiction and space utopia/dystopia, as well as the idea of the frontier, all tempered with allusions to the vernacular Arab city. Here, we learn of the origins of the book’s title, Spaceship in the Desert, used less as metaphor than as metonym, neatly depicting Masdar as a bounded, self-sufficient, high-tech, futuristic experiment in the Emirate’s desert. The notion of experiment comes through strongly in this chapter, although it is also present throughout the book. The chapter (and the book as a whole) may have benefitted from engaging with literature on energy experiments being developed in other social sciences (namely in geography—work by Harriet Bulkeley and Vanesa Castán Broto come to mind). Instead, Günel shows how the experiment presents itself as a frontier for performing novel livelihoods that could be adopted elsewhere. In the eyes of its promoters, Masdar’s relevance—as prototype, potential, and promise—stands not on how it actually works, but on the bodily performance of what Masdar may become by those who live in it or visit it. The author argues that it is through the performance of a hi-tech prototype that the success of Masdar is anticipated, although not without being confronted with the everyday idiosyncrasies of its experimental technology. In the end, the futuristic language and imagery used for Masdar is largely an asocial and apolitical stance on sustainability, seldom acknowledging looming concerns over social justice. Chapter 2 delves into the politics of how Masdar, as an energy experiment, is made appealing through beautiful buildings and research contracts. It focuses on the role played by the establishment of Masdar...
title_zh: 沙漠中的飞船：阿布扎比的能源、气候变化与城市设计
abstract_zh: 书评：Gökçe Günel著《沙漠中的飞船：阿布扎比的能源、气候变化与城市设计》Idalina Baptista Gökçe Günel，《沙漠中的飞船：阿布扎比的能源、气候变化与城市设计》。达勒姆：杜克大学出版社，2019年。272页。《沙漠中的飞船》是对日益增长的能源人类学学术领域的及时贡献。Günel将阿布扎比的马斯达尔城作为探索气候变化、技术、知识生产以及以可持续未来为名所追求的超凡道德路径等诸多交叉问题的场所。书中充满了基于作者在马斯达尔度过的时光以及参加相关会议、活动和其他富有洞察力的对话的民族志细节。该书似乎在核心五章中整合了先前发表的多篇文章的扩展版本，这些章节由引言和结语串联，后者进一步反思了马斯达尔城的整体实验。引言让读者熟悉马斯达尔城，阐述了该书的主要贡献和方法论路径，并提供了全书的大纲。开篇的民族志片段捕捉了在该实验（当时短暂的）生命周期中盛行的市场导向方法。这在本章的副标题——“二氧化碳的灵魂”——中得到了概括，该副标题引用了一位信息提供者试图通过货币术语使二氧化碳的“灵魂”可见的努力。此外，本章概述了该书的一个关键分析焦点和贡献：作者所谓的“技术调整”。这些调整包括对能源现状的实验性微调，这些调整优先考虑技术修复，而非对没有石油和普遍消费的未来的道德伦理考量。随后的每一章都聚焦于一个不同的“技术调整”，尽管叙述并不总是回到这个宽泛的概念或其理论化。相反，每一章都涉及与历史化所分析之“技术调整”相关的关键思考。这非常有用，因为它将马斯达尔的实验及其路径依赖性置于背景中，展示了这些实验如何随着时间的推移通过思想与政策的网络流动而塑造。最终，Günel似乎更关注于探索每个“技术调整”在唤起无油未来方面的潜力中所产生的生产性张力，而非评判其成功或失败。第一章探讨了2006年项目启动后几年中描述马斯达尔的语言选择。它借鉴了科幻小说和太空乌托邦/反乌托邦的未来主义意象，以及边疆的概念，并兼顾了对阿拉伯本土城市的暗示。在这里，我们了解到书名的由来——《沙漠中的飞船》——与其说是隐喻，不如说是转喻，恰当地将马斯达尔描绘成酋长国沙漠中一个边界分明、自给自足、高科技、未来主义的实验。实验的概念在这一章中强烈呈现，尽管它也贯穿全书。本章（以及整本书）若能借鉴其他社会科学（特别是地理学——Harriet Bulkeley和Vanesa Castán Broto的工作浮现在脑海中）正在发展的能源实验文献，可能会受益。相反，Günel展示了该实验如何表现为一个可为其他地方采纳的新型生活方式的边疆。在其推动者眼中，马斯达尔的相关性——作为原型、潜力和承诺——并不取决于它实际如何运作，而是取决于那些生活或访问其中的人对马斯达尔可能成为之物的身体表演。作者认为，正是通过高科技原型的表演，马斯达尔的成功被预期，尽管并非没有遇到其实验性技术的日常特质。最终，用于马斯达尔的未来主义语言和意象在很大程度上是一种非社会、非政治的可持续性立场，很少承认对社会正义的迫在眉睫的担忧。第二章深入探讨了马斯达尔作为能源实验如何通过美丽的建筑和研究合同变得吸引人的政治。它集中于建立马斯达尔所扮演的角色……

title: The solar good: energy ethics in poor markets
journal_name: JOURNAL OF THE ROYAL ANTHROPOLOGICAL INSTITUTE
abstract: Abstract What are the ethical commitments of people who design, build, and sell solar photovoltaic technologies to those living in energy poverty across sub‐Saharan Africa and South Asia? Over the past decade, dramatic falls in the cost of solar photovoltaics have seen our increased capacity to convert sunlight into electricity married to projects of governance, social or moral reform, and expressions of care for distant others. Tracing these projects across the floor of an international trade fair in Dubai and a social enterprise in India, this essay shows that the pursuit of the solar good hinges on the knowable ground that is capitalism today.
title_zh: 太阳能善行：贫困市场中的能源伦理
abstract_zh: 摘要 那些为撒哈拉以南非洲和南亚的能源贫困人口设计、建造和销售太阳能光伏技术的人，他们的伦理承诺是什么？过去十年中，太阳能光伏成本的急剧下降使我们将阳光转化为电力的能力增强，并与治理、社会或道德改革项目以及对远方他人的关怀表达相结合。通过追踪这些项目在迪拜的一个国际贸易展览会和印度的一家社会企业中的表现，本文表明，追求太阳能善行取决于当今资本主义的可认识基础。

title: Transpacific precarities: responding to Souvankham Thammavongsa’sFoundand Rita Wong’sforagein East Asia
abstract: This essay investigates the stakes involved in responding to transpacific texts in East Asia, specifically in universities in Macau and Taiwan. It focuses on responses to two texts that represent in distinct ways precariatized lives in a transpacific frame: Souvankham Thammavongsa’s Found, a text that uncovers a path from Laos to a refugee camp in Thailand to Canada, a path made legible through a scrapbook kept by Thammavongsa’s father; and Rita Wong’s forage, a text that cuts across and between South China and North America to track the movements of peoples and goods and waste, including the movement of electronic waste (or “e-waste”). By discussing selected responses to these texts, this essay investigates how such responses can be considered as part of a long-term pedagogical process of cultivating imaginations and striving to develop forms of responsibility to what this essay calls transpacific precarities. It suggests that carefully attending to such responses, always partial and in progress, can help us to better understand Asian American studies in East Asia as it continues to evolve through acts of teaching and learning in different sites.
title_zh: 跨太平洋的不稳定性：回应Souvankham Thammavongsa的《发现》和Rita Wong的《搜寻》在东亚
abstract_zh: 本文探讨了在东亚（具体是澳门和台湾的大学）回应跨太平洋文本所涉及的利害关系。重点分析了对两部文本的反应，这些文本以不同方式展现了跨太平洋框架下的不稳定生活：Souvankham Thammavongsa的《发现》，该文本揭示了一条从老挝到泰国难民营再到加拿大的路径，这条路径通过Thammavongsa父亲保存的剪贴簿得以呈现；以及Rita Wong的《搜寻》，该文本跨越华南和北美，追踪人员、商品和废物的流动，包括电子废物（或“电子垃圾”）的流动。通过讨论对这些文本的选择性回应，本文探讨了这些回应如何被视为长期教学过程中的一部分，以培养想象力并努力发展对本文所称的跨太平洋不稳定性的责任形式。文章认为，仔细关注这些始终不完整且在进行中的回应，有助于我们更好地理解在东亚的亚裔美国人研究，因为它通过在不同地点的教学和学习行为继续演变。

title: United Nigerian Textiles Limited and Chinese–Nigerian textile-manufacturing collaboration in Kaduna
abstract: Abstract In 1964, the newly established Hong Kong-based Cha Group partnered with the Northern Nigerian Regional Development Corporation to open the United Nigerian Textiles Limited (UNTL) mill in Kaduna – the largest textile mill in Northern Nigeria. The Cha Group later expanded, building textile mills in other parts of the country. Both Chinese and Nigerian managers and workers were involved in UNTL mills, which by 1980 provided printed cotton textiles for the Nigerian market and for other markets in West Africa. Yet this Chinese–Nigeria collaboration could not overcome factors external to the textile-manufacturing industry. Declining infrastructure, erratic electricity, frequent changes in political leadership at the federal level, and the smuggling of less-costly imported textiles (often from China) undermined local textile manufacturing, while inflationary pressures associated with the national oil industry undermined agricultural production, exacerbating the difficulties of obtaining raw Nigerian cotton. In 2007, the UNTL mill in Kaduna closed, although it resumed production in December 2010, assisted by the 100 billion naira Cotton, Textile and Garment Development Fund. Cha Group officials also used their knowledge of the Nigerian textile market as the basis for the marketing of branded, high-quality manufactured textiles, known as Da Viva ® , at company-franchised shops in major Nigerian cities. The Cha Group took advantage of digital innovation, both in the printing of these popular textiles and also by advertising them on an attractive website. This article considers the ways in which the United Nigerian Textiles Plc company has maintained production of grey cloth and printed textiles at its mills in Kaduna and Ikorodu-Lagos, along with the marketing of Da Viva ® cotton prints, which suggests the continuing, if contradictory, possibilities for this Nigerian–Chinese textile-manufacturing collaboration.
title_zh: 尼日利亚联合纺织有限公司与中尼在卡杜纳的纺织制造合作
abstract_zh: 1964年，新成立的香港查氏集团与北尼日利亚地区发展公司合作，在卡杜纳开设了尼日利亚联合纺织有限公司（UNTL）——北尼日利亚最大的纺织厂。查氏集团后来扩大规模，在该国其他地区建立了纺织厂。UNTL工厂涉及中国和尼日利亚的管理人员和工人，到1980年，它为尼日利亚市场以及西非其他市场提供印花棉纺织品。然而，这种中尼合作无法克服纺织制造业外部的因素。基础设施退化、电力不稳定、联邦层面政治领导层的频繁更迭，以及廉价进口纺织品（通常来自中国）的走私，削弱了本地纺织制造业，而与国家石油工业相关的通胀压力破坏了农业生产，加剧了获取尼日利亚原棉的困难。2007年，卡杜纳的UNTL工厂关闭，但在2010年12月，借助1000亿奈拉的棉花、纺织品和服装发展基金，它恢复了生产。查氏集团官员还利用他们对尼日利亚纺织品市场的了解，在尼日利亚主要城市的公司特许商店销售名为Da Viva®的品牌高质量制造纺织品。查氏集团利用数字创新，不仅在这些流行纺织品的印花上，还通过一个吸引人的网站进行广告。本文探讨了尼日利亚联合纺织有限公司如何在其卡杜纳和伊科罗杜-拉各斯的工厂保持坯布和印花纺织品的生产，以及Da Viva®棉印花的营销，这表明这种中尼纺织制造合作持续但矛盾的可能性。

title: Vertical farming: tin mining and agro-mineros in Bolivia
abstract: Throughout Bolivia, collectives of small-scale miners known as ‘mining cooperatives’ have developed a reputation for cutthroat extractive practices that were shaped by neoliberal restructuring starting in the 1980s. Charting a history that starts at the turn of the twentieth century, this paper argues that cooperative mining in the tin belt of Northern Potosí has emerged as a vertical instantiation of small-holder farming practices that migrated, along with miners themselves, from surrounding indigenous ayllus. In the subterranean, however, these practices interacted with the legacies of tin mining, which was characterized by labor hierarchies that corresponded with vertical variation in ore quality. New social striations crystallized as small-holder farming customs settled into the subterranean structure, creating sharp social differentiation across these subsoil ‘family farms.’ The class composition of mining cooperatives at the national level has been shaped by these entangled underground histories, with implications for the country’s economic and environmental futures.
title_zh: 垂直农业：玻利维亚的锡矿开采与农业矿工
abstract_zh: 在整个玻利维亚，被称为“矿业合作社”的小规模矿工集体以冷酷无情的开采实践而闻名，这些实践是由1980年代开始的新自由主义重组塑造的。本文追溯了从二十世纪初开始的历史，认为北波托西锡矿带的合作采矿是小型农户实践（这些实践随矿工本身从周围的土著艾柳迁移而来）的垂直体现。然而，在地下，这些实践与锡矿开采的遗产相互作用，锡矿开采的特点是与矿石质量的垂直变化相对应的劳动等级制度。随着小农耕作习俗沉淀到地下结构中，新的社会分层结晶出来，在这些地下“家庭农场”中形成了尖锐的社会分化。国家层面矿业合作社的阶级构成受到这些纠缠不清的地下历史的影响，对该国的经济和环境未来具有影响。

title: Yellow Woman: Suspicion and Cooperation on Liberia's Gold Mines
abstract: ABSTRACT Yellow Woman is a multimodal ethnographic research project combining text and film to explore the dynamics of cooperation and suspicion on a Liberian gold mine. The sixteen‐minute single‐take video places the viewer in a uniquely “filmic” position; in other words, it allows the viewer to experience the end of a gold mining operation as only a camera can render it. But it is a point of view that simultaneously captures the tensions and surveillance practices of mine bosses and the laborers themselves. These men, despite the collective nature of their work and their long associations with one another, nevertheless remain constantly vigilant against the possibilities of deception and theft. The text that accompanies the film provides the ethnographic context that the film itself cannot and explores the aesthetic and stylistic choices through which the film communicates. [ ethnographic film, mining, Liberia ]
title_zh: 黄女人：利比里亚金矿上的猜疑与合作
abstract_zh: 摘要《黄女人》是一个多模态民族志研究项目，结合文本和电影，探索利比里亚金矿上合作与猜疑的动态。这部16分钟的单镜头视频将观众置于一种独特的“电影”位置；换句话说，它让观众只能以摄像机所能呈现的方式体验金矿开采作业的终结。但这一视角同时捕捉了矿主和工人自身的紧张关系与监视实践。这些工人尽管工作具有集体性质且彼此长期合作，却始终对欺骗和盗窃的可能性保持警惕。伴随电影的文字提供了电影本身无法提供的民族志背景，并探讨了电影借以传达信息的美学与风格选择。[民族志电影，采矿，利比里亚]

title: A world of cheapness: Affordability, shoddiness, and second‐best options in Guinea and China
abstract: For people who trade and consume low‐priced, low‐quality goods, cheapness shapes their experiences of the world. In Guinea, West Africa, affordable Chinese‐manufactured goods expand the limits of people's everyday lives, while Guinean traders seek their fortunes by traveling to China to buy cheap merchandise. However, shoddy products that break easily often disappoint consumers, and traders find their journeys to China risky and difficult; many of them would migrate elsewhere if they could. Exploring the parallels between traders' and consumers' perspectives, this article considers how cheapness and second‐best options allow people to participate in a globalized economy of manufactured goods, thereby improving their quality of life in ways that work sometimes, but not as well as they would like.
title_zh: 廉价的世界：几内亚和中国的 affordability、shoddiness 和次优选择
abstract_zh: 对于交易和消费低价、低质量商品的人来说，廉价塑造了他们对世界的体验。在西非的几内亚，价格实惠的中国制造商品拓宽了人们日常生活的界限，而几内亚商人通过前往中国购买廉价商品来寻求财富。然而，容易损坏的劣质产品常常令消费者失望，商人也发现他们的中国之行充满风险且困难重重；许多人如果可以的话会选择移居别处。本文通过探讨商人和消费者视角的相似之处，考虑廉价和次优选择如何使人们参与全球化的制成品经济，从而以有时有效但不如意的方式改善他们的生活质量。

title: Analyzing the Evolution of a Digital Technology Intervention: One Laptop Per Child in a Remote Papua New Guinea Community
abstract: Abstract This article offers an ethnographic account of the evolution of a One Laptop per Child intervention program in Oksapmin communities (Papua New Guinea). The analysis examines the intervention’s evolution as historically contingent, revealing how interdependent actions of multiple stakeholders create and partially resolve perceived threats to the program’s continuation under changing circumstances. The approach contrasts with those that explain the success or failure of interventions based upon “fit” to cultural context.
title_zh: 分析数字技术干预的演变：巴布亚新几内亚偏远社区的一孩一笔记本项目
abstract_zh: 摘要 本文提供了巴布亚新几内亚奥克斯普明社区“一孩一笔记本”干预项目演变的民族志记录。分析将干预的演变视为历史偶然，揭示了多个利益相关者的相互依存的行动如何在变化的环境中创造并部分解决对项目持续性的感知威胁。这种方法与那些基于“适应”文化背景来解释干预成功或失败的方法形成对比。

title: Cyborg Preparedness: Incorporating Knowing and Caring Bodies into Emergency Infrastructures
abstract: Biopreparedness exercises are commonly depicted as indispensable means to enable people to respond to outbreaks of highly pathogenic infectious diseases. In this article, based on a 4-year multisited ethnography conducted in Frankfurt and London, we argue that exercises mobilize past and present events in a continuous rehearsal for the implementation and stabilization of emergency infrastructures. While relying on the embodied knowledge and the body techniques of its participants, these infrastructures necessitate continuous attention, investment, and training. Through these techniques, preventive assemblages create what we term "cyborg preparedness," whereby human bodies, clinical architectures, and technical artifacts are subject to emerging forms of urban governance.
title_zh: 赛博格准备：将认知和关怀的身体纳入应急基础设施
abstract_zh: 生物准备演习通常被描述为使人们能够应对高致病性传染病暴发的不可或缺的手段。本文基于在法兰克福和伦敦进行的为期四年的多点民族志研究，认为演习动员了过去和现在的事件，以持续预演应急基础设施的实施和稳定。这些基础设施依赖参与者的具身知识和身体技术，同时也需要持续的关注、投资和培训。通过这些技术，预防性集合体创造了我们称之为“赛博格准备”的状态，其中人类身体、临床建筑和技术制品都受到新兴城市治理形式的影响。

title: Enclosing the Gold-Mining Commons of Mongolia: The Vanishing Ninja and the Development Project as Resource

authors.name: Gantulga Munkherdene
institutions: Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology

abstract: Since its emergence in the mid-1990s, unauthorized small-scale gold mining—widely known as “ninja mining”—has grown to become a central element of Mongolia’s informal economy, engaging tens of thousands of people in seasonal, unregulated, and occasionally dangerous labor. In this paper we set out to show that the story of ninja mining is illustrative of the wider transformation of political economy that Mongolia has experienced, in which a de facto public resource was created in the wake of the collapsed state socialist economy, only to be progressively privatized and enclosed by increasingly powerful mining company interests. We examine the implementation of a development project aimed at providing sustainable livelihoods for those engaged in unauthorized mining. Drawing upon anthropological critiques of development, we explore the ways in which the project, while arguably succeeding in its own terms, failed to meet the expectations of the miners involved. Committed as it was to working within the new private property regime for land introduced by “neoliberal” reforms, the project constructed the ninja “problem” in terms of a lack of formalization and training. It was ultimately unable to address the fundamental issues of property relations and access to resources that lie at the heart of the ninja phenomenon.
title_zh: 包围蒙古的金矿公地：消失的忍者与发展项目作为资源
abstract_zh: 自上世纪90年代中期出现以来，未经授权的小规模金矿开采——广泛被称为“忍者采矿”——已发展成为蒙古非正规经济的核心组成部分，吸引了数万人从事季节性、无监管且有时危险的劳动。在本文中，我们旨在表明，忍者采矿的故事说明了蒙古所经历的政治经济更广泛的转型，在这一转型中，随着国家社会主义经济体崩溃，事实上的公共资源被创造出来，却逐渐被日益强大的矿业公司利益私有化和圈占。我们考察了一个旨在为从事未经授权采矿的人提供可持续生计的发展项目的实施。借鉴人类学对发展的批判，我们探讨了该项目尽管可以说在其自身层面上取得了成功，却未能满足所涉及矿工期望的方式。该项目致力于在“新自由主义”改革引入的新的土地私有产权制度内运作，将忍者“问题”构建为缺乏正规化和培训。它最终无法解决位于忍者现象核心的财产关系和资源获取的根本问题。

title: Fantaw, Setargew Kenaw: Technology-Culture Dialogue. Cultural and Sociotechnical Appropriation of Mobile Phones in Ethiopia

title: Front and Back Covers, Volume 34, Number 3. June 2018
abstract: Cover caption, volume 34 issue 3 Front Cover: UNDERAGE LABOUR IN LEBANON The Lebanese scrap metal industry — one of the country's largest exports — relies heavily on marginalized young boys displaced from their homes in Syria. In their article in this issue, Elizabeth Saleh and Adrien Zakar focus on Harun, a 14‐year‐old waste picker promoted by his community from novice to scrapyard master (muallim). They follow him as he discreetly rummages in the rubbish of Beirut pushing a cart made from recovered plastic baskets and bins. Underage waste pickers are not supposed to be working and yet this is the only legitimate reason for their presence in Lebanon. During their tours across Beirut these underage waste pickers collect iron, copper and fizzy drink cans. They navigate the city concealing play under the guise of work. Through these salvaging games they foster a community of complicity among themselves that functions according to age hierarchies and involves rites of passage and codes of conduct. Although only just a child, Harun is mastering muallim — literally ‘the one who knows’ — learning the art of informal trade while confronting his social exclusion by mastering subterfuge and irony. Back Cover: IS DOWSING ‘UNSCIENTIFIC’? In this issue, Jonathan Woolley draws attention to a contemporary controversy in the media surrounding the reported use of dowsing by UK water companies. He delves into the background of this practice. Dowsing is a customary method for finding hidden water, objects or mineral deposits, practised in many European or European settler societies. While scientists and sceptics maintain that it is totally ineffective, dowsing is trusted by many practitioners even today, to divine accurate information about the world around them. Although frequently characterized as ‘pseudoscience’ by its critics, the practice of dowsing actually predates the scientific revolution by centuries. Therefore, to describe it as a form of ‘pseudoscience’ is inaccurate, as dowsing is based on embodied ways of knowing, quite distinct from the scientific method. Pseudoscientific theories of dowsing's efficacy — such as attributing the movement of rods to geomagnetic forces — are a late 19th‐century commentary on the practice that many dowsers today reject. In his 16th‐century treatment of mining and the smelting of ore, Agricola's De re metallica includes a detailed description of dowsing for metal ore. Image source: Agricola's De re metallica , Book 7, 1556.
title_zh: 第34卷第3期封面与封底，2018年6月
